comments.text: SunnyMoose 2026-04-17: Fresh-eyes audit — minor hardening observation on fcp-oauth/src/error.rs. OAuthError::StateMismatch (error.rs:16) Display format is 'OAuth state mismatch: expected {expected}, got {actual}' and echoes both full state values into the error string. State values are 32-byte base64url CSRF tokens (~43 chars, generated via OsRng). While the state is single-use and is 'dead' after a mismatch (no further use in the flow), including it verbatim in Display/to_string output means the expected value will appear in any log line, bug-report tracebacks, or CI captures that stringify the error. Low severity: this only matters if (a) logs are accessible to an attacker AND (b) the attacker can race the legitimate user's in-flight callback. Realistic attack surface is narrow. Hardening recommendation: redact or hash-prefix the state in Display (e.g. 'expected {expected_prefix}...' showing only the first 8 chars) while keeping the full values in the structured Debug output. The actual value disclosure is slightly more acceptable since it's attacker-supplied data, but the expected value is secret-until-callback. Debug auto-derive already exposes both; if a caller Debug-dumps, they're responsible for the redaction choice. For the default Display path used in logs, tightening would be prudent. Not patching — touches public Display output of a named error variant, so downstream string-matching tests may break. Flagged for future hardening decision. This was the last concrete pass I had on fcp-oauth source files (token.rs, oauth2.rs, pkce.rs, oauth1.rs, provider.rs, error.rs all reviewed).

comments.text: SunnyMoose 2026-04-17: PATCHED — fcp-mesh coordinator panic on adversarial u64::MAX fencing token from expired lease. Finding: earlier defensive patch (commit 1233c361) addressed rebase_next_seq with saturating_add, but coordinator.rs:534 next_fencing_token retained checked_add(1).expect('fencing token space exhausted'). An adversarial peer reporting ObservedLeaseAuthority with expires_at in the past AND fencing_token = u64::MAX causes: (1) rebase_next_seq saturates next_seq to u64::MAX, (2) active-filter drops the expired poisoned lease, (3) acquire takes the grant branch since active.is_empty(), (4) next_fencing_token computes token=u64::MAX and then checked_add(1)=None → **PANIC**. The existing regression test (coordinator.rs:1013) only covers the ACTIVE poisoned lease case, where acquire short-circuits to Denied without reaching next_fencing_token. Fix landed (commit 1de6f11e): next_fencing_token now returns Option<u64>, refusing to hand out a token when next_seq reaches u64::MAX. acquire() maps None to AcquireOutcome::Conflict { holders:[], fencing_tokens:[], reason:'fencing token space exhausted' } with a timeline event recording the refusal. Added regression test acquire_does_not_panic_on_u64_max_fencing_token_with_expired_lease covering the exact attack vector. Change is mechanical + backward-compatible on AcquireOutcome (no new enum variant). Verification: local cargo check blocked by pre-existing asupersync upstream compile errors (71 errors — same blocker documented for all my patches this session); mechanical change, minimal risk. Running totals: 7 concrete fix patches now in fcp-oauth (2) + fcp-mesh (5) + plumbing/style patches, + logged architectural gaps and validation-gap findings.

comments.text: SunnyMoose 2026-04-17: Architectural observation on fcp-mesh gossip inbound dispatch — MeshGossip::handle_summary (gossip.rs:1257) has ZERO production call sites. Only test callers in gossip.rs itself and crates/fcp-conformance/src/harness.rs:820 reach this entry point. node.rs has no handle_gossip / dispatch_gossip / receive_gossip / GossipSummary pattern match — no incoming wire message route to this handler. Same class of 'scaffolded but not dispatched' gap as the QuarantineStore I logged earlier this session. Implication: my previously-flagged architectural gaps about handle_summary not verifying summary.signature (and similarly handle_symbol_ack / handle_decode_status) are DORMANT, not live exploits — because the dispatcher that would route untrusted wire traffic into these handlers doesn't exist in production yet. The gossip OUTGOING side is wired (announce_object/announce_symbol from MeshNode flow through gossip, prune_stale_peers from my 76c6f805 patch gates the peer_states map), but INCOMING (handle_summary/handle_request) is not. Net-assessment of the cumulative 'architectural signature-verification gaps' logged earlier: they become live on the day the gossip dispatch is wired into the inbound transport path — at that point the signature-verification gate must be added BEFORE the handle_ entrypoints. Until then, these are design-debt markers, not vulnerabilities. Still worth recording; the gap list is now part of the coordination bead.

comments.text: SunnyMoose 2026-04-17: Fresh-eyes audit — gossip.rs IBLT decode safety + RevocationPushMessage structure. IbltPlaceholder::decode_with_limits (gossip.rs:327) correctly orders defenses: (1) length check vs max_bytes BEFORE serde_json::from_slice at line 332 (prevents oversize allocation during deserialization), (2) empty-bytes short-circuit at line 339, (3) serde_json deserialization with caller-supplied max_bytes already validated above, (4) post-decode length check vs max_changes at line 345. Clean. RevocationPushMessage (gossip.rs:852) carries revoked_ids: Vec<ObjectId> with NO explicit per-message size cap; revocation-push-specific bounds would come from transport-layer max-message-bytes (same defense-in-depth observation as handle_summary iblt bytes). Since no production dispatcher currently routes RevocationPushMessage into a handler (consistent with the handle_summary dispatch-gap I just logged), this remains design-debt rather than a live vulnerability. Once dispatch is wired, the handler MUST: (a) verify signature (currently Optional per message schema), (b) enforce max-revoked_ids-per-push cap on the inbound side. Current observed state: all revocation-push infrastructure is present at the data-model level (RevocationPushMessage, RevocationPushPolicy, GossipConfig.max_revocation_push_peers), the OUTGOING sender side exists in gossip.rs, and the receiver side is not yet wired. Flagged to be batched with the dispatch-wiring work when that happens. Nothing more to add without overlapping previously-recorded findings.

## fcp-crypto fresh-eyes audit (SunnyMoose, 2026-04-18)

13/13 source files audited. ALL CLEAN PASSES. No bugs or defensive gaps found.

### Files reviewed:
1. ed25519.rs (936 lines) — Ed25519 sign/verify, domain separation via BLAKE3 context, RFC 8032 vectors
2. aead.rs (993 lines) — ChaCha20/XChaCha20-Poly1305, deprecated random 96-bit nonces, RFC 8439 vector
3. mac.rs (599 lines) — BLAKE3 keyed MAC, constant-time verify via subtle, incremental MAC
4. cose.rs (1448 lines) — COSE_Sign1/CWT, verify-before-trust, BTreeMap deterministic CBOR, timing validation
5. hkdf.rs (602 lines) — HKDF-SHA256, domain-separated FCP2 derivation, RFC 5869 vectors
6. hpke_seal.rs (749 lines) — HPKE sealed boxes, AAD context binding, deterministic CBOR AAD
7. shamir.rs (1487 lines) — GF(2^8) Shamir SSS, constant-time field ops (Russian peasant), Fermat inverse
8. x25519.rs (685 lines) — X25519 ECDH, all-zero shared secret rejection (low-order point defense), RFC 7748 vector
9. frost.rs (1694 lines) — FROST threshold DKG+signing, nonce consumed by move, comprehensive validation
10. canonicalize.rs (668 lines) — RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, domain separation, duplicate key detection
11. kid.rs (441 lines) — KID derivation (BLAKE3 truncated), constant-time equality
12. error.rs (480 lines) — thiserror error types, no sensitive data leakage
13. lib.rs (124 lines) — Crate root, forbid(unsafe_code), warn(missing_docs)

### Key security properties verified:
- forbid(unsafe_code) at crate root
- Constant-time ops throughout (subtle crate for MAC verify, KID equality, Shamir GF(2^8))
- ZeroizeOnDrop on ALL secret types (signing keys, AEAD keys, HKDF derived keys, FROST signing shares/nonces, shared secrets)
- Debug redaction on all secret types
- Domain separation in every primitive (ed25519 context, HKDF info, HPKE info, KID prefix, canonical signing domain)
- FROST nonce consumed by move (prevents reuse — the #1 FROST security property)
- X25519 rejects all-zero shared secrets (low-order point defense)
- COSE verify-before-trust discipline
- RFC test vectors: Ed25519 (8032), AEAD (8439), HKDF (5869), X25519 (7748)
- Deterministic CBOR per RFC 8949 with duplicate key detection
- Comprehensive FROST input validation at every boundary

### Architectural notes:
- No gaps needing patches (unlike fcp-mesh/fcp-oauth which had 7 concrete fixes)
- The crypto crate is well-hardened — clean constant-time discipline, proper zeroization, and thorough test coverage
- This is the most security-critical crate and it passes with flying colors

SunnyMoose fresh-eyes audit: fcp-bootstrap (11 files, 14472 lines) — CLEAN PASS

## Files Audited

1. recovery_phrase.rs (700 lines) — BIP39 24-word, 256-bit entropy via rand::thread_rng().fill_bytes. ZeroizeOnDrop + constant-time equality via subtle. HKDF domain-separated derivation (salt=FCP2-OWNER-KEY-V1, info=owner-signing-key). Seed zeroized after key creation. Debug shows only word_count:24.

2. cold_recovery.rs (785 lines) — from_phrase with optional fingerprint verification. Uses create_deterministic (epoch timestamp). Standard recovery warnings (NoAuditHistory, RevocationStateUnknown, SingleNodeStart, DataLoss).

3. ceremony.rs (2300 lines) — ThresholdCeremony state machine: Gathering→Round1→Round2→Complete. Rogue-key mitigation: empty proof-of-knowledge rejection (line 555). Empty share/ciphertext rejection. can_resume_after_abort only allows Gathering/Round1 (NOT Round2 — shares may be exposed). Double verification: FROST verifying key + Ed25519 owner key after aggregation.

4. genesis.rs (1277 lines) — 5 required zones (z:owner, z:private, z:work, z:community, z:public). create_deterministic sets timestamp to epoch for reproducible fingerprints. Fingerprint: BLAKE3(owner_public_key || schema_version)[0..12] base64. Validation: schema version, owner key validity, future timestamp (5min tolerance), required zones, zone ID format. OwnerKeypair with ZeroizeOnDrop.

5. time_validation.rs (781 lines) — NTP drift detection: Valid (<30s), DriftWarning (30s-5min), DriftError (>5min). Tries pool.ntp.org, time.google.com, time.cloudflare.com. CannotValidate allows bootstrap to proceed (offline-friendly).

6. hardware_token.rs (3072 lines) — PKCS#11 integration via cryptoki. HardwareTokenPin: ZeroizeOnDrop, constant-time equality, debug redaction. AuthenticatedTokenSession: timeout/expiry, close-on-drop with exactly-once semantics (close_action taken by Option::take prevents double-close). Provider probe mutex for thread safety. Initialization idempotency (CryptokiAlreadyInitialized OK). Session cleanup on login failure. Certificate selection: deterministic ranking (Ed25519 > X25519 > ECDSA-P256 > ECDSA-P384; RSA/Other refused). Token identity matching with unknown wildcard. map_pkcs11_error maps all CK error codes to typed variants.

7. error.rs (822 lines) — Comprehensive BootstrapError enum with typed hardware-token refusal variants. No sensitive data leakage.

8. lib.rs (119 lines) — forbid(unsafe_code), warn(missing_docs).

9. workflow.rs (1873 lines) — Atomic genesis write: write-to-temp → fsync → rename → sync_directory. Phase lock cleanup ONLY after genesis is durable. Temp file cleaned up on failure. Partial state detection for crash recovery (lock file > genesis.partial > keys.partial priority). Force overwrite protection. Hardware token PIN required before any PKCS#11 work. Typed error mapping for all TokenError variants via map_hardware_token_error. summarize_detection_issues caps at 3 issues with total count.

10. phase.rs (1075 lines) — BootstrapPhase state machine with serde roundtrip. Lock file takes priority over partial markers. CeremonyRound2 is NOT resumable (shares may be exposed — consistent with ceremony.rs). Corrupt lock → fallback to TimeValidation. remove_phase_lock idempotent.

11. soft_token.rs (1669 lines, cfg(test)) — Deterministic soft-token harness. HKDF from fixed master seed + index for per-identity key derivation. CKA_ID from BLAKE3(public_key)[0..20]. Full pipeline verification pack: 11 scenarios covering success, wrong PIN, missing PIN, missing slot, incompatible key, CA-only, empty token, cleanup determinism, workflow integration, multi-key preference, deterministic rerun.

## Security Properties Confirmed
- All secret types: ZeroizeOnDrop + Debug redaction
- Constant-time operations throughout (PIN, keys) via subtle crate
- Atomic genesis persistence (write→fsync→rename→dirsync)
- Phase lock preserved on failure for crash recovery
- Hardware token sessions: close-on-drop with exactly-once semantics
- forbid(unsafe_code) at crate root
- Ed25519 mechanism required for bootstrap selection
- FROST ceremony non-resumable after Round2
- Deterministic certificate selection with stable sort tiebreak

## Verdict: CLEAN PASS — no bugs or defensive gaps found

title: TEST: Crypto Primitives Unit Tests (Ed25519, X25519, HPKE, AEAD, COSE)
description:
# TEST: Crypto Primitives Unit Tests


## Goal
Prove crypto primitives and encodings are correct via golden vectors + negative tests (Ed25519/X25519/HPKE/AEAD/COSE) without panics or side-channels in logs.

## Scope
Comprehensive unit tests for all cryptographic primitives used in FCP2.

## Test Categories

### Ed25519 Signatures
- [ ] Sign/verify roundtrip
- [ ] Verify with wrong key fails
- [ ] Verify with tampered message fails
- [ ] Signature malleability checks
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 8032

### X25519 Key Exchange
- [ ] ECDH produces same shared secret both ways
- [ ] Reject low-order points
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 7748

### HPKE Sealing (RFC 9180)
- [ ] Seal/unseal roundtrip
- [ ] Unseal with wrong key fails
- [ ] AAD binding is enforced
- [ ] Multiple recipients (sealed to multiple keys)
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 9180

### HKDF-SHA256
- [ ] Extract/expand produces correct output
- [ ] Context/info binding changes output
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 5869

### ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD
- [ ] Encrypt/decrypt roundtrip
- [ ] Tampered ciphertext fails authentication
- [ ] Tampered AAD fails authentication
- [ ] Nonce reuse detection (if stateful)
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 8439

### XChaCha20-Poly1305 (if used)
- [ ] Extended nonce handling
- [ ] Same test matrix as ChaCha20-Poly1305

### BLAKE3 Hashing
- [ ] Hash produces expected output
- [ ] Keyed MAC mode
- [ ] Incremental hashing
- [ ] Test vectors from BLAKE3 spec

### COSE_Sign1 Helpers
- [ ] Create/verify COSE_Sign1 structure
- [ ] Protected headers in AAD
- [ ] KID extraction
- [ ] Invalid COSE structures rejected
- [ ] Test vectors from RFC 9052

### KID (Key ID) Generation
- [ ] KID format is stable
- [ ] Same key produces same KID
- [ ] Different keys produce different KIDs
- [ ] KID truncation is correct (8 bytes)

## Golden Vectors
Each category MUST have golden vectors:
- Input bytes (hex)
- Expected output bytes (hex)
- Source reference (RFC, test suite, etc.)

## Fuzz Targets
- COSE structure parsing
- HPKE unsealing (malformed inputs)
- Signature verification (malformed signatures)

## Logging Requirements
All tests emit structured JSON logs with:
- `test_name`
- `primitive` (ed25519, x25519, etc.)
- `operation` (sign, verify, seal, etc.)
- `result` (pass/fail)
- `vector_source` (RFC reference or "generated")

## Acceptance Criteria
- All crypto operations have test coverage
- Golden vectors exist and match
- Fuzz targets run without panics
- No secret material in test logs

title: [FCP3] Mesh first refoundation from host first truthful surface to a V3 native platform
description:
Background: the current repository is truthful but host first in day to day operation. The practical control path runs through crates/fwc/src/main.rs, crates/fwc/src/catalog.rs, crates/fwc/src/readiness.rs, and crates/fcp-host/src/bin/fcp-host.rs, while crates/fcp-core/src/lib.rs still behaves like an overly broad semantic bucket and crates/fcp-protocol/src/lib.rs does not yet own the full FCPC and FCPS story.

Goal: make the platform genuinely mesh first in the sense intended by the V3 architecture, not merely more mesh flavored in naming or CLI copy. That means moving execution semantics, policy, evidence, durable truth, placement, leases, and failover into first class owners so that fcp-host becomes a node local root app over mesh native substrate layers and fwc can stay truthful while projecting mesh backed reality.

This initiative is the canonical migration graph. Success means: each major semantic noun has exactly one owner; FCPC is the normative live control and evidence plane; FCPS is the normative durable object plane; host local process state stops being the only source of truth for receipts, checkpoints, leases, and readiness; fwc consumes stable contracts instead of semantic buckets; and the cutover ends with deletion of transition scaffolding rather than permanent compatibility debt.

comments.author: CobaltHarbor
comments.text:
This initiative exists to prevent a common failure mode: making the CLI or docs sound more mesh native before the runtime, durability, evidence, and placement layers actually are. If a future implementer has to choose between appearing more mesh first and staying strictly truthful about what the platform can prove, truthful provenance wins.

Use this graph as the self contained replacement for the spec derived migration narrative. The intended order is: freeze semantics, carve real owners, realign durable and wire truth, converge host and SDK, prove mesh placement and failover on a narrow pilot, move operator surfaces onto those contracts, then delete the transition scaffolding. No compatibility shims, no permanent host local truth islands, and no fake mesh claims.

title: [FCP2] InvokeRequest/InvokeResponse: Schema Validation, Holder Proof, Binding Rules
description:
# [FCP2] InvokeRequest/InvokeResponse: Schema Validation, Holder Proof, Binding Rules

## Goal
Implement the canonical InvokeRequest and InvokeResponse structures that are the primary interface for connector invocation.

## Why This Deserves Its Own Bead
The spec defines detailed requirements for InvokeRequest/InvokeResponse that span multiple concerns:
- capability token embedding and holder_proof generation
- idempotency_key handling
- lease binding (when required)
- evidence attachment rules
- response envelope structure

This complexity warrants focused implementation and testing.

## InvokeRequest (NORMATIVE)
Fields:
- `request_id` (UUID)
- `connector_id` (ConnectorId)
- `operation_id` (SchemaId)
- `zone_id` (ZoneId)
- `token` (CapabilityToken - COSE_Sign1 bytes)
- `holder_proof` (Ed25519 signature; REQUIRED when token.holder_node present)
- `idempotency_key` (Option<String>) - REQUIRED for Risky/Dangerous ops
- `inputs` (CBOR map - schema-validated)
- `context` (InvokeContext - trace_id, request_tags, etc.)
- `lease_seq` (Option<u64>) - REQUIRED for singleton_writer connectors

### holder_proof Binding (NORMATIVE)
When token has `holder_node` set:
- signable bytes MUST bind: `request_id || operation_id || token.jti`
- signature by holder node signing key
- prevents replay by non-holder nodes

### Idempotency Rules
- For `IdempotencyPolicy::Strict` or Risky/Dangerous: idempotency_key MUST be set
- Key format: opaque string, max 128 bytes

## InvokeResponse (NORMATIVE)
Fields:
- `request_id` (matches request)
- `status` (Ok | Error)
- `outputs` (Option<CBOR map> - schema-validated)
- `error` (Option<FcpError>)
- `receipt_id` (Option<ObjectId> - OperationReceipt)
- `audit_event_id` (Option<ObjectId>)
- `decision_receipt_id` (Option<ObjectId> - for denials)
- `response_metadata` (timing, cache hints, etc.)

## Subtasks
- Define InvokeRequest and InvokeResponse canonical schemas
- Implement holder_proof generation and verification
- Implement idempotency_key validation
- Implement lease_seq binding checks
- Define InvokeContext propagation rules

## Acceptance Criteria
- Golden vectors for InvokeRequest canonical encoding
- Adversarial tests: missing holder_proof rejected, invalid idempotency_key rejected
- Property tests: holder_proof binding covers all required fields

title: [FCP2] Type Naming Standardization: SafetyTier vs RiskTier, Health Types
description:
# [FCP2] Type Naming Standardization: SafetyTier vs RiskTier, Health Types

## Goal
Establish clear, consistent naming conventions for key types across all FCP2 beads and implementation.

## Problem
The codebase has two similar-sounding but conceptually distinct types:
- `SafetyTier` - tool/operation safety classification
- `RiskTier` - quorum/consensus requirements

Some beads incorrectly use `RiskTier` when referring to tool safety levels, creating confusion.

## Canonical Type Naming

### SafetyTier (Tool/Operation Safety)

**Definition:** Classifies the safety level of a tool or operation for agent decision-making.

**Location:** `crates/fcp-core/src/capability.rs`

**Values:**
```rust
pub enum SafetyTier {
    Safe,       // No approval needed, read-only or benign
    Risky,      // Requires policy check, may have side effects
    Dangerous,  // Requires interactive approval
    Critical,   // Requires quorum/elevation
    Forbidden,  // Never allowed
}
```

**Use in:**
- Tool descriptors (`ToolDescriptor.safety_tier`)
- Operation metadata (`OperationMeta.safety_tier`)
- Provenance validation (`can_drive_operation(tier)`)
- CLI filtering (`--max-risk safe`)
- Agent decision logic

**NOT called:** `RiskTier`, `ToolRisk`, `OperationRisk`

### RiskTier (Quorum/Consensus)

**Definition:** Classifies the quorum requirements for distributed consensus operations.

**Location:** `crates/fcp-core/src/quorum.rs`

**Values:**
```rust
pub enum RiskTier {
    Safe,           // Single signature sufficient
    Risky,          // f+1 signatures required
    Dangerous,      // n-f signatures required
    CriticalWrite,  // Full quorum required
}
```

**Use in:**
- Quorum policy evaluation (`required_quorum(n, f, risk_tier)`)
- Signature set validation (`satisfies_quorum(policy, risk_tier)`)
- Lease operations (`LeaseType.default_risk_tier()`)

**NOT called:** `SafetyTier`, `QuorumTier`, `ConsensusLevel`

### ConnectorHealth (Connector Status)

**Definition:** Health status of a connector process.

title: [IDEA-01] SDK Connector Runtime Kit (Supervised Streaming/Polling)
description:
# SDK Connector Runtime Kit (Supervised Streaming/Polling)

## Goal
Provide a reusable, SDK-level runtime kit for connector authors that encapsulates the reliability patterns from the Discord/Telegram studies: supervised loops, backoff, resume, heartbeat/zombie detection, deterministic shutdown, and structured health transitions.

## Background / Why
Discord (streaming WebSocket) and Telegram (polling) independently implement the same reliability machinery. Without a shared SDK surface we get duplicated bugs, inconsistent health semantics, and regressions across connectors. A runtime kit makes these patterns mechanical and accelerates new connector development.

## Scope
- SDK module(s) used by connector implementations without host changes.
- No changes to external APIs; this is internal SDK ergonomics and correctness.
- Includes testing utilities and reference examples.

## Deliverables
- `fcp_sdk::runtime::{StreamingSupervisor, PollingSupervisor, SupervisorConfig}` with:
  - exponential backoff + jitter
  - retry budgets + cooldowns
  - shutdown signals
  - session resume hooks
  - deterministic health transitions (Healthy/Degraded/Unhealthy)
- Connector-facing trait adapters for platform-specific state (session IDs, cursor offsets).
- Structured logging fields (`connector_id`, `zone_id`, `operation_id`, `stream_key`, `sequence`).

## Tests
- Unit tests for backoff, retry budgets, and shutdown transitions.
- Integration tests with a fake stream/poll source (no external calls).
- Deterministic logging snapshots (JSONL schema once flywheel_connectors-11g2 lands).

## Acceptance Criteria
- At least one streaming connector can replace its custom loop with the SDK supervisor.
- At least one polling connector can replace its custom loop with the SDK supervisor.
- Health transitions are deterministic and observable via logs.

title: [FCP2] Offline Capability: Availability Tracking, OfflineAccess Metrics, Predictive Pre-staging
description:
# [FCP2] Offline Capability Tracking

## Goal
Implement the offline capability tracking from V2 spec section 21, enabling:
- Real-time availability tracking per object
- OfflineCapability/OfflineAccess metrics
- Predictive pre-staging based on user patterns
- Quantifiable offline resilience (SLO-ready)

## Normative Requirements (from FCP Specification V2 section 21)
- Nodes MUST track local symbol availability per object
- Nodes SHOULD support predictive pre-staging based on access patterns
- Offline resilience MUST be quantifiable (can_access, coverage ratio)

## Implementation Details

### OfflineCapability Schema
- accessible: HashMap<ObjectId, OfflineAccess>

### OfflineAccess Schema
- object_id: ObjectId
- local_symbols: usize (symbols held locally)
- k: usize (symbols needed for reconstruction)
- can_access(): bool (local_symbols >= k)
- coverage(): f64 (local_symbols / k)

### Predictive Pre-staging
- Track object access patterns per zone
- Pre-stage symbols for frequently accessed objects before needed
- Respect device storage constraints (DeviceProfile)
- Priority queue based on access frequency and recency

## Dependencies
- Requires Stores (1n78.15) for symbol tracking
- Requires DeviceProfile (wwq8) for storage constraints
- Integrates with Background Repair for coverage management

## Tests
- Unit tests: can_access(), coverage() calculations
- Integration tests: pre-staging triggers on access patterns
- E2E tests: offline read with reduced connectivity

## Acceptance Criteria
- Offline capability is queryable per object (can_access, coverage)
- Pre-staging improves offline availability for frequently accessed objects
- CLI reports offline readiness via fcp doctor --zone

- Canary rollout can be configured per connector.
- Automatic rollback triggers on health thresholds and is auditable.

title: Supply Chain Verification: Attestation + SBOM Gate
description:
# Supply Chain Verification: Attestation + SBOM Gate

## Goal
Block untrusted connector installs/updates by verifying signed supply-chain attestations and SBOMs before activation, with deterministic evidence bundles for audit and offline installs.

## Why (User Impact)
- Operators get cryptographic assurance that the binary matches audited provenance.
- Prevents downgrade/typosquat or mixed-identity artifacts from entering the mesh.
- Makes offline installs safer via cached, signed evidence.

## Scope
- Attestation + SBOM object schemas and signature verification.
- Host-side verification pipeline and policy gate during install/upgrade.
- CLI verify/report flows and machine-readable evidence bundles.
- Deterministic, redactable logs and receipts suitable for audits.

## Non-goals
- Implementing a full vulnerability scanner (we ingest/report external results).
- Replacing the registry; this is a gate on install/upgrade only.

## Deliverables
- Canonical schemas for SupplyChainAttestation and SBOM objects.
- Host verification pipeline (signature, provenance binding, policy checks).
- Evidence bundle object with stable hashes and redacted fields.
- CLI commands for verify/report/install gating.
- Unit/integration tests + E2E scripts with structured JSON logs.

## Security/Policy Notes
- Fail closed by default (missing/invalid attestation or SBOM blocks install).
- Support policy knobs: require_attestation, min_slsa_level, trusted_builders, allow_unsigned (dev-only).
- Verification must be deterministic (same inputs -> same evidence bundle hash).
- Never log secrets or raw tokens; redact sensitive fields in logs/evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Valid attestation+SBOM installs; invalid/unsigned is rejected unless explicit policy allows.
- Evidence bundle includes all verification steps, hashes, trust roots, and timestamps.
- Errors are actionable, deterministic, and redact secrets.
- Unit/integration tests cover positive/negative paths; E2E script passes in CI.

- Batch symbol requests and use Bytes for zero-copy in hot paths.

description:
# CLI: `fcp connector` (list/info/introspect) - Agent-Visible Discovery

## Goal
Implement connector discovery commands that agents (and operators) use to find and understand available connectors before invoking tools.

This fills the gap between Agent Integration (`1n78.30`) which defines the discovery API and the CLI which needs to expose it.

## Commands

### `fcp connector list`
List all registered connectors with summary info.

```bash
# Human output
fcp connector list
# ID              NAME          VERSION   TOOLS   RISK    STATUS
# fcp.discord     Discord       1.2.0     12      Risky   ✓ Healthy
# fcp.github      GitHub        2.0.1     24      Risky   ⚠ Degraded (rate limited)
# fcp.slack       Slack         1.0.0     8       Risky   ✓ Healthy
# fcp.anthropic   Anthropic     1.0.0     3       Safe    ✓ Healthy

# Filter by category
fcp connector list --category messaging
fcp connector list --category llm

# Filter by max risk tier
fcp connector list --max-risk safe
fcp connector list --max-risk moderate

# Filter by health
fcp connector list --healthy
fcp connector list --degraded

# JSON output for agents
fcp connector list --json
```

### `fcp connector info <connector>`
Show detailed connector information including manifest metadata.

```bash
fcp connector info fcp.discord
# Connector: fcp.discord
# Name: Discord
# Version: 1.2.0
# Archetype: Bidirectional
# Home Zone: z:private
# 
# Capabilities Required:
#   - discord.messages.read (Safe)
#   - discord.messages.send (Risky)
#   - discord.webhooks.manage (Dangerous)
# 
# Network Constraints:
#   Allowed: discord.com:443, gateway.discord.gg:443
#   CIDR Deny: default (RFC1918 + localhost)
# 
# State Model: singleton_writer
# Event Topics: message.new, message.edited, member.joined
# 
# Health: Healthy
# Uptime: 3d 14h 22m
# Last Health Check: 2s ago

fcp connector info fcp.discord --json
```

### `fcp connector introspect <connector>`
Return MCP-compatible tool descriptors for a connector.

```bash
# Human-readable tool list
fcp connector introspect fcp.discord
# Tools (12):
#   send_message      Send a message to a channel           Risky
#   send_dm           Send a direct message                 Risky  
#   list_channels     List channels in a guild              Safe
#   get_message       Get a specific message                Safe
#   ...

# Full MCP tool descriptors (JSON)
fcp connector introspect fcp.discord --json

# Single tool
fcp connector introspect fcp.discord --tool send_message --json
```

## Output Contracts

### ConnectorSummary (list)
```rust
pub struct ConnectorSummary {
    pub id: ConnectorId,
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub version: semver::Version,
    pub categories: Vec<String>,
    pub tool_count: u32,
    pub max_risk_tier: SafetyTier,
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub health: ConnectorHealth,
}
```

### ConnectorInfo (info)
```rust
pub struct ConnectorInfo {
    pub summary: ConnectorSummary,
    pub archetype: ConnectorArchetype,
    pub home_zone: ZoneId,
    pub capabilities: CapabilityDeclarations,
    pub network_constraints: NetworkConstraints,
    pub state_model: ConnectorStateModel,
    pub event_topics: Vec<EventTopic>,
    pub manifest_hash: ObjectId,
    pub installed_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

### ToolDescriptor (introspect) - SEP-1382 compliant
```rust
pub struct ToolDescriptor {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub input_schema: serde_json::Value,
    pub output_schema: serde_json::Value,
    pub risk_tier: SafetyTier,
    pub requires_confirmation: bool,
    pub idempotent: bool,
    pub supports_simulate: bool,
    pub latency_hint: LatencyHint,
    pub rate_limits: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub examples: Option<Vec<ToolExample>>,
    pub ai_hints: Option<String>,
}
```

## Tests

- test_connector_list_filters_by_risk
- test_connector_list_filters_by_health
- test_connector_info_includes_all_manifest_data

- connector_info_human.snap
- connector_info_json.snap
- connector_introspect_human.snap
- connector_introspect_json.snap

e2e/connector_discovery.sh with detailed logging

- [ ] `fcp connector list` returns all registered connectors
- [ ] Filtering by category, risk, and health works correctly
- [ ] `fcp connector info` returns full manifest-derived data
- [ ] `fcp connector introspect` returns MCP-compliant tool descriptors
- [ ] All commands support `--json` output

title: TEST: Revocation Unit/Adversarial Tests (Freshness, Chain Integrity, Scope Enforcement)
description:
# TEST: Revocation Unit/Adversarial Tests

## Goal
Prove that revocations are processed correctly and cannot be bypassed.

## Test Categories

### RevocationObject Parsing
- [ ] Valid revocation object parses
- [ ] Malformed CBOR rejected
- [ ] Missing required fields rejected
- [ ] Invalid scope rejected
- [ ] Owner signature verification succeeds/fails correctly

### Revocation Scopes
- [ ] Capability revocation: referenced capability becomes invalid
- [ ] IssuerKey revocation: tokens from that issuer become invalid
- [ ] NodeAttestation revocation: node operations become invalid
- [ ] ZoneKey revocation: triggers zone key rotation awareness
- [ ] ConnectorBinary revocation: connector cannot run

### RevocationEvent Chain
- [ ] Events hash-linked correctly (prev_hash binding)
- [ ] Monotonic seq enforced
- [ ] Duplicate seq rejected
- [ ] Gap in seq detected and flagged
- [ ] Out-of-order events handled correctly

### RevocationHead
- [ ] Quorum signatures required (n-f)
- [ ] Insufficient signatures rejected
- [ ] Signature from non-member rejected
- [ ] Signature set canonicalization (sorted by node_id)
- [ ] Multiple valid heads for same seq → fork detection

### Freshness Policy Enforcement
- [ ] Strict policy: stale revocation head → operation rejected
- [ ] Warn policy: stale head → operation allowed with degraded flag
- [ ] BestEffort policy: very stale head → operation allowed with audit
- [ ] max_age calculation correct
- [ ] Freshness check is O(1) (seq comparison, not chain traversal)

### RevocationRegistry
- [ ] Fast negative lookup (bloom filter or equivalent)
- [ ] False positives trigger full check
- [ ] True positive: revoked item correctly identified
- [ ] True negative: valid item passes quickly
- [ ] Registry update on new revocation event

### Attack Scenarios (Adversarial)
- [ ] Revocation withholding: node claims no revocations but others have them
- [ ] Revocation replay: old revocation re-submitted
- [ ] Revocation forgery: invalid owner signature rejected
- [ ] Stale frontier attack: verifier with very old revocation head
- [ ] Chain fork injection: two revocation heads for same seq detected

## Golden Vectors
- Valid revocation object bytes
- Valid revocation chain with multiple events
- RevocationHead with quorum signatures
- Bloom filter state after N revocations

## Fuzz Targets
- RevocationObject parsing
- RevocationEvent chain verification
- RevocationHead signature verification

## Logging Requirements
```json
{
  "test_name": "...",
  "revocation_scope": "Capability|IssuerKey|...",
  "target_id": "...",
  "chain_seq": 123,
  "result": "pass|fail",
  "reason_code": "...",
  "freshness_policy": "Strict|Warn|BestEffort"
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- All revocation scopes tested
- Chain integrity verified
- Attack scenarios blocked
- Freshness policies enforced correctly

Created comprehensive revocation_golden_vectors.rs with:
- Golden vectors for all 5 revocation scopes
- Chain integrity vectors (valid chain, gaps, duplicates, broken links)
- Freshness policy vectors for strict/warn/best_effort
- 7 adversarial attack tests (withholding, replay, stale frontier, fork injection, scope escalation, bloom bypass, flood)
- Chain integrity validation tests
- Quorum verification tests for RevocationHead

- **Operational**: Account linking, transaction sync, balance queries
- **Streaming**: Webhook events for transaction updates, errors

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Transaction sync cursors per Item
- State tracked: `{ item_cursors: HashMap<ItemId, SyncCursor> }`
- Lease required for writer fencing

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI MANDATORY**: Handles highly sensitive financial data
- Memory isolation for credentials
- Capability-gated hostcalls
- No raw credentials in connector memory

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // Plaid API endpoints (environment-specific)
    host_allow: vec\![
        "sandbox.plaid.com".into(),     // Sandbox
        "development.plaid.com".into(), // Development
        "production.plaid.com".into(),  // Production
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// Account data is highly sensitive but trusted from Plaid
account_data.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::NONE;

// Transaction descriptions may contain merchant names (external)
transaction.description.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT;

// User-provided institution selection
link_token_request.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `plaid.accounts.read` | Risky | Sensitive financial data |
| `plaid.transactions.read` | Risky | Sensitive financial data |
| `plaid.balances.read` | Risky | Sensitive financial data |
| `plaid.link.create` | Risky | Initiates account linking |
| `plaid.identity.read` | Dangerous | PII (name, address, SSN) |
| `plaid.auth.read` | Dangerous | Account/routing numbers |
| `plaid.item.remove` | Dangerous | Breaks integration |
| `plaid.assets.manage` | Dangerous | Credit report access |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Account Management
- Link bank accounts via Plaid Link
- List connected accounts
- Get account balances
- Manage Items (connections)

### Transaction Access
- Sync transactions (incremental)
- Categorize transactions
- Search transaction history
- Detect recurring transactions

### Financial Data
- Account/routing numbers (ACH)
- Identity verification
- Investment holdings
- Liability information

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Connect my bank account"
"Get my current balances"
"Show transactions from last month"
"Categorize my spending"
"Set up ACH transfer details"
"Verify my identity for compliance"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Stripe Integration
**Complete financial picture:**
- Plaid for bank data
- Stripe for payments
- Unified revenue + expense view

### HubSpot Integration
- Financial data for customer profiles
- Payment behavior analytics
- Revenue forecasting

### Airtable Integration
- Transaction export to tables
- Budget tracking dashboards
- Financial reporting

### Agent Mail Integration
- Balance alerts → agent threads
- Transaction anomaly notifications
- Financial status updates

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **Link API**: Account connection flow
- **Transactions API**: Transaction sync
- **Auth API**: Account/routing numbers
- **Identity API**: KYC verification

### Recommended Crates
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `serde_json` — JSON handling
- `chrono` — Date handling for transactions
- `secrecy` — Credential handling

### Environment Selection
| Environment | Use Case |
|-------------|----------|
| Sandbox | Testing with fake data |
| Development | Testing with real banks |
| Production | Live financial data |

### Rate Limits
```rust
RateLimits {
    requests_per_minute: 100,
    concurrent_requests: 10,
    // Per-endpoint limits vary
}
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:private:plaid:full` | Full access | All operations |
| `z:private:plaid:readonly` | Read-only | Balances, transactions |
| `z:private:plaid:link` | Link only | Account connection |

### Security Considerations
- Financial data is PII/NPI
- Audit all data access
- Never log account numbers
- Environment isolation critical

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — API operations
- `streaming` — Webhook event ingestion

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `{environment}.plaid.com:443`
- Environment selected at deployment

### Credential Injection
- client_id + secret via egress proxy
- access_token per Item via CredentialId
- Never persist raw credentials

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `plaid.accounts.read` — List accounts
- `plaid.balances.read` — Get balances
- `plaid.transactions.read` — Sync transactions
- `plaid.investments.read` — Holdings/securities

### Sensitive Read Operations
- `plaid.auth.read` — Account/routing numbers (Dangerous)
- `plaid.identity.read` — PII verification (Dangerous)

### Write Operations
- `plaid.link.create` — Create link token
- `plaid.link.exchange` — Exchange public token
- `plaid.item.remove` — Disconnect Item (Dangerous)

### Admin Operations
- `plaid.webhooks.manage` — Configure webhooks (Dangerous)
- `plaid.assets.manage` — Asset reports (Dangerous)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Create Link Token
```json
POST /link/token/create
{
  "client_id": "{{injected}}",
  "secret": "{{injected}}",
  "user": {"client_user_id": "user_123"},
  "client_name": "My App",
  "products": ["transactions"],
  "country_codes": ["US"],
  "language": "en"
}
```

### Get Accounts

```json
{
  "access_token": "{{injected}}"
}
```

### Sync Transactions
```json
POST /transactions/sync
{
  "access_token": "{{injected}}",
  "cursor": "{{last_cursor}}"
}
```

### Get Auth (Dangerous)
```json
POST /auth/get
{
  "access_token": "{{injected}}"
}
// Returns account + routing numbers
```

---

## Threat Model

### Hard Requirements
- Never log account/routing numbers
- Never log access tokens
- Never log transaction descriptions in full
- Secrets never touch disk
- Default deny for all operations

### Audit Requirements
- All data access logged
- All writes require AuditEvent
- Correlation IDs for tracing
- Retention policy compliance

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- Request construction
- Response parsing

- Error responses
- Webhook signature validation

### Integration Tests
- Mock Plaid API responses
- Transaction sync simulation
- Link flow simulation

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints (environment-specific)
- Dangerous operation approval flow
- Audit logging verification
- No credential leakage

---

- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real Plaid API calls in unit tests
- Link token creation works
- Transaction sync functional
- Balance queries work
- Auth data requires approval
- Credential injection via egress proxy

title: [FWC] Plan/do/explain intent compiler with transparent primitive workflow plans
description:
# [FWC] Plan/do/explain intent compiler with transparent primitive workflow plans

## Goal
Add a plan-first intent compiler to `fwc` so agents can express goals in natural task language and receive a deterministic, reviewable, step-by-step workflow over canonical primitive `fwc` commands.

## Why this exists
Agents usually know the goal before they know the exact connector id, operation id, payload shape, or identifier they need. `fwc` should meet agents at the intent layer without becoming a vague chatbot. The right abstraction is a compiler: infer the likely connector and workflow, surface uncertainty explicitly, and emit the exact primitive commands that would be run.

## Scope
- add `fwc plan <intent>` for side-effect-free workflow compilation
- add `fwc explain <intent>` for transparent reasoning, assumptions, matches, and ambiguities
- add `fwc do <intent>` with safe-by-default simulation and explicit approval mode
- compile intents into exact primitive `fwc` command steps instead of a parallel hidden execution path
- keep all outputs compact, TOON-friendly, and honest about scaffolded versus host-backed behavior

## Required behaviors
- infer likely connector, action family, resource noun, and risk from intent text
- extract useful literals such as quoted titles, names, zones, or candidate identifiers when possible
- surface `missing_information`, `ambiguities`, `assumptions`, `did_you_mean`, and `next_actions`
- emit exact canonical primitive commands such as `show`, `ops`, `schema`, `examples`, `status`, `simulate`, `invoke`, `config schema`, `config doctor`, `enable`, `disable`, or `restart`
- default `do` to simulation/preflight semantics unless the caller explicitly approves
- never pretend that host-backed side effects occurred when the scaffold still lacks real execution backends

## Deliverables
- intent-compiler module with deterministic heuristic inference and scoring
- top-level clap commands for `plan`, `do`, and `explain`
- structured payloads for compiled plans, explanations, and simulated execution traces
- tests for discovery-heavy intents, lifecycle intents, identifier-heavy intents, missing-info paths, and ambiguous connector/action matches

## Acceptance criteria
- `fwc` becomes goal-oriented without sacrificing transparency or safety
- the planner compounds existing discovery/config/lifecycle/invoke primitives instead of bypassing them
- agents can move from a natural-language request to an exact primitive command sequence in one turn

description:
# fcp.jira: Dual Cloud and Server/DC API support (FCP2)

## Goal
Support **Jira Cloud** and **Jira Server / Data Center** with a single connector binary, while preserving *mechanical* FCP2 guarantees (single-zone binding, default deny, sandbox + NetworkConstraints).

This bead exists because Cloud and Server/DC differ on:
- auth mechanisms
- REST base paths / API versions (v3 vs v2)
- response shapes / field availability
- rate-limit semantics

## Scope
Deliver an internal abstraction layer that makes higher-level Jira operations (issues, comments, attachments, sprints, workflows, JQL, etc.) **deployment-agnostic**.

### In scope
- `JiraDeployment = Cloud | ServerDc` configuration (manifest + provisioned config).
- A canonical `JiraBaseUrl` normalization + validation layer (used for NetworkConstraints pinning).
- Request construction differences:
  - Cloud: REST v3 endpoints where required
  - Server/DC: REST v2 endpoints where required
- Response parsing normalization:
  - unify common structs (Issue, Project, User, Comment, Attachment metadata)
  - feature-detect optional fields instead of assuming presence
- Auth strategy selection (mechanical, policy-gated):
  - Cloud: OAuth2 or API token via `CredentialId`
  - Server/DC: PAT or basic auth via `CredentialId`

### Explicitly out of scope
- Backwards compatibility with *any* legacy “FCP1” protocol or compatibility shim.
- Supporting multiple Jira instances from a single connector instance (still single-zone bound).

## FCP2 requirements to enforce
- **Single-zone binding**: deployment choice does not change ZoneId.
- **Capability IDs** MUST NOT encode hostnames or ports.
- **NetworkConstraints**:
  - allow only the configured Jira base hostname
  - forbid redirects to different hostnames by default
- **Secret hygiene**:
  - credentials are injected via `CredentialId` at invocation time
  - never log tokens, Authorization headers, cookies

## Deliverables
- `JiraHttp` facade with:
  - `send_json<TReq, TRes>(...)` with typed request/response
  - consistent error mapping to the SDK error taxonomy
  - explicit timeouts + bounded response size limits
- `JiraApiSurface` mapping table:
  - operation → (cloud endpoint, server endpoint) + method + required query params
- “Capability ↔ endpoint” mapping hooks for the manifest bead to reference.

## Test strategy (MUST)
### Unit/integration (mock-only)
- Two mock fixtures:
  1. Jira Cloud mock server
  2. Jira Server/DC mock server
- Golden request tests:
  - correct URL path + query params per deployment
  - correct auth header strategy selected
- Golden parse tests:
  - normalize issues/projects/users from both variants
  - handle missing fields gracefully

### Negative/security tests
- NetworkConstraints refusal when URL host differs (including redirects).
- Ensure no secrets appear in structured logs (log-scrub tests).

## Acceptance criteria
- Higher-level Jira feature beads can depend on a stable `JiraDeployment` abstraction.
- A single test suite can run the same operation tests against both mock variants.
- No FCP1/backwards-compat behaviors are introduced.

Comprehensive tests for CursorStore behavior and resilience.

## Details

title: fcp.redis: Redis Cache and Pub/Sub Connector
description:
# fcp.redis - Redis Cache and Pub/Sub Connector


## Goal
Provide an FCP2-compliant Redis connector for cache/storage, pub/sub, and stream operations with strict capability gating and bounded resource use.

## External surface (NetworkConstraints)
Default deny.
- Network egress MUST be restricted per-operation via manifest `NetworkConstraints` (defined in the connector’s manifest/cap map bead if present).
- Allow only the configured service host(s); HTTPS-only where applicable; deny redirects by default.
- Bound timeouts + response sizes; treat all remote responses as untrusted input; never leak secrets/PII in logs or errors.
- For DB/queue connectors, constrain raw TCP connects to explicit host:port only; deny private ranges unless explicitly allowed by policy.

## Overview
Redis connector for caching, key-value storage, pub/sub messaging, and data structure operations.

## Manifest archetypes (closed set)
- `storage`
- `operational`
- `bidirectional`

> Interaction patterns (non-archetype): Request/Response + Queue/Pub-Sub

## Key Operations

### String Operations
- `redis.get` - Get value
- `redis.set` - Set value (with TTL, NX/XX)
- `redis.mget/mset` - Multiple get/set
- `redis.incr/decr` - Atomic increment/decrement
- `redis.append` - Append to string
- `redis.getrange/setrange` - Substring operations

### Hash Operations
- `redis.hget/hset` - Single field get/set
- `redis.hmget/hmset` - Multiple fields
- `redis.hgetall` - Get all fields
- `redis.hdel` - Delete fields
- `redis.hincrby` - Increment field

### List Operations
- `redis.lpush/rpush` - Push to list
- `redis.lpop/rpop` - Pop from list
- `redis.lrange` - Get range
- `redis.llen` - List length
- `redis.lindex` - Get by index
- `redis.blpop/brpop` - Blocking pop

### Set Operations
- `redis.sadd/srem` - Add/remove members
- `redis.smembers` - Get all members
- `redis.sismember` - Check membership
- `redis.sinter/sunion/sdiff` - Set operations

### Sorted Set Operations
- `redis.zadd/zrem` - Add/remove members
- `redis.zrange/zrevrange` - Get by rank
- `redis.zscore` - Get score
- `redis.zrangebyscore` - Get by score range
- `redis.zincrby` - Increment score

### Pub/Sub Operations
- `redis.publish` - Publish message
- `redis.subscribe` - Subscribe to channels
- `redis.psubscribe` - Pattern subscribe
- `redis.unsubscribe` - Unsubscribe

### Stream Operations
- `redis.xadd` - Add to stream
- `redis.xread` - Read from stream
- `redis.xrange` - Read range
- `redis.xgroup` - Consumer groups
- `redis.xreadgroup` - Group read

### Key Operations
- `redis.del` - Delete keys
- `redis.exists` - Check existence
- `redis.expire/ttl` - TTL management
- `redis.keys/scan` - Key enumeration
- `redis.type` - Get key type

### Transaction Operations
- `redis.multi/exec` - Transactions
- `redis.watch` - Optimistic locking

## Providers Supported
- Redis OSS
- Redis Enterprise
- AWS ElastiCache
- Azure Cache for Redis
- Upstash
- Redis Cloud

## Connection Management
- Connection pooling
- Cluster mode support
- Sentinel support
- TLS connections

## Authentication
- Password authentication
- ACL users (Redis 6+)
- TLS client certificates

## Zone Architecture

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The *"zones"* described in this section are a **recommended deployment pattern** (run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies) and/or conceptual risk tiers.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

```
Zone 0 (Public):     N/A
Zone 1 (Authorized): Read operations
Zone 2 (Private):    Write operations
Zone 3 (Sensitive):  Admin operations, credentials
```

## Dependencies
- fcp-core, fcp-ratelimit, fcp-testkit, fcp-telemetry

## Acceptance Criteria
- The functionality described in this bead is implemented with typed schemas + validation (no unstructured “stringly” interfaces).
- Errors map to the FCP error taxonomy with correct retry semantics and no secret/PII leakage.
- Mock-only unit/integration tests cover success paths and common failures and emit structured JSON logs per `flywheel_connectors-1n78.35`.

title: fcp.twilio: Programmable Video API
description:
# fcp.twilio: Programmable Video API (FCP2)

## Goal
Provide a minimal, safe surface over Twilio Programmable Video:
- create/manage rooms
- list participants
- end rooms
- optionally fetch recordings

Video is high-cost and high-privacy. Treat most write operations as approval-gated.

## Scope
### Rooms
- Create room with constrained options (max participants, timeout).
- List rooms and get room status.
- End/complete a room.

### Participants
- List participants in a room.
- Optional: disconnect participant (dangerous).

### Recordings (optional; dangerous)
- List recordings for a room.
- Fetch recording metadata.

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `twilio.video.rooms.read`
- `twilio.video.rooms.write` (dangerous)
- `twilio.video.participants.read`
- `twilio.video.participants.write` (dangerous)
- `twilio.video.recordings.read` (dangerous)

## FCP2 requirements
- Single-zone binding.
- NetworkConstraints pinned to Twilio API host(s).
- For any write:
  - require approval when policy dictates
  - emit receipts + audit events with room SID and action
- Strict privacy hygiene:
  - never log participant identities or media URLs

## Deliverables
- Operation schemas:
  - `twilio.video.room.create`
  - `twilio.video.room.get`
  - `twilio.video.room.list`
  - `twilio.video.room.end`
  - `twilio.video.room.participants`
  - Optional: `twilio.video.recording.list`

## Test strategy (MUST)
- Mock-only tests for:
  - room lifecycle
  - approval gating
  - error mapping
  - log redaction

## Acceptance criteria
- Video operations are safe-by-default and auditable.

title: [SC] Attestation + SBOM object schemas
description:
# [SC] Attestation + SBOM object schemas

## Goal
Define canonical schemas and validation rules for SupplyChainAttestation and SBOM objects, including signature requirements and deterministic hashing.

## Scope
- SupplyChainAttestation schema (SLSA/in-toto style provenance) with binding to artifact digest.
- SBOM schema (CycloneDX/SPDX subset) describing components and dependencies.
- Signature requirements and trust-root binding rules.
- Canonical encoding and hash rules (stable across platforms).

## Deliverables
- Schema IDs and versions for:
  - SupplyChainAttestation: subject digest, predicate type, builder identity, buildType, materials, metadata (timestamps), slsa_level, provenance_hash.
  - SBOM: bom_format, bom_version, tool chain, component list (name, version, hashes, licenses), dependency graph.
- Canonical encoding rules (CBOR canonical + JSON canonical) and hashing algorithm selection.
- Validation rules: required fields, allowed predicate types, builder allowlist hooks.

## Tests
- Golden vectors for valid/invalid attestations and SBOMs.
- Deterministic hash tests (same semantic input -> same hash).
- Schema rejection tests for missing/extra fields.

## Logging Requirements
- Structured JSON logs for schema validation and hash determinism checks:
  - {test, schema_id, vector_id, result, duration_ms}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Schemas are versioned, deterministic, and validated by conformance tooling.
- Encoding + hash outputs are stable across runs/OSes.
- Invalid/unsigned objects fail closed with clear error codes.
notes:
[AlienArtifactPractical]

- Add deterministic vector generator with fixed seeds and algebraic edge cases.
[ExtremeOptimizationPractical]

- Avoid allocations in canonicalization using stack buffers.

# TEST: No-mock coverage + full E2E logging (FCP2)

## Goal
Establish real-component unit/integration coverage (no mocks/fakes) plus a complete E2E script suite with rich structured logging.

## Definition: No mocks/fakes
- No mocking frameworks (wiremock), stub servers, or fake clients in the target suites.
- Tests exercise real code paths (actual protocol parsing, crypto, stores, mesh/session logic, sandbox enforcement).
- For external services (LLM, social APIs), tests must use dedicated sandbox accounts and real HTTP calls OR be marked manual-only with secrets gating.

## Deliverables
- Coverage inventory + gap map.
- Real-component test suites for core crates, mesh, store/repair, host+connector subprocess, sandbox/egress.
- E2E logging schema + validator + expanded scenario runner.

## Non-goals
- Do not delete existing mock-based tests; instead add real-component suites in parallel.
- No reliance on public production accounts.

## Success Criteria
- A coherent dependency graph of tasks that yields: (1) real-component unit/integration coverage, (2) comprehensive E2E scripts with machine-parseable logs.
notes:

- Add spectral routing score (effective resistance / Laplacian) as optional metric and log chosen path.
- Set gossip TTL from measured mixing-time; add convergence test that asserts bound.

title: [IDEA-19] Structured Log Redaction + Secret Scanner
description:
## Background
Logging standards forbid secrets/PII, but enforcement is inconsistent. A mechanical scanner reduces risk and enforces compliance across tests and CI artifacts.

## Goals
- Provide a reusable log scanner that detects secrets/PII patterns in JSONL logs.
- Integrate with test harnesses and compliance runner.
- Allow explicit allowlists for safe test fixtures.

## Non-goals
- Replacing runtime redaction; this is a verification layer.

## Approach
- Add a `LogRedactionScanner` in `fcp-testkit` or `fcp-conformance`.
- Detect common secret formats (JWTs, API keys, auth headers, base64 blobs) and obvious PII.
- Expose CLI for scanning artifacts.

## Risks
- False positives; provide explicit per-test allowlists and explainable matches.

## Success Criteria
- CI fails if secrets appear in logs.
- Scanner provides actionable match locations and suggestions.

## Acceptance Criteria (Refined)
- Scanner detects JWTs, bearer tokens, and API key patterns in JSONL.
- Allowlist requires explicit justification string.
notes:
[AlienArtifactPractical]
- Add evidence ledger fields with per-check log-odds contributions and explicit loss decision.
- Add anytime-valid risk control (e-process) for approvals/denials and record epsilon in receipts.
[ExtremeOptimizationPractical]
- Compile policies to DAG/BDD and cache allow/deny results with LRU.
- Use bitset capability sets for fast subset checks.

title: fcp-discord: send_message_happy_path fails in targeted cargo test run
description:
Targeted verification failed under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/fcp-p5-r1 rch exec -- cargo test -p fcp-telegram -p fcp-discord -p fcp-slack -p fcp-whatsapp` on the remote worker.

Evidence:
- `connectors/discord/tests/integration.rs:394` expected request method `POST` for `/channels/111/messages`, but the second observed request was `GET`.
- `connectors/discord/tests/integration.rs:435` then failed with `connection failed: Connection refused (os error 111)`.
- This is the only remaining failure in the exact verification run; the command ended with `error: test failed, to rerun pass -p fcp-discord --test integration`.

Needs follow-up to determine whether the structured fake server assumptions are stale or whether `discord.send_message` is issuing an unexpected extra GET before POST.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fixed in 939cb221. Root cause: handle_handshake spawns a background gateway-connect task that issues GET /gateway/bot when no gateway_url is configured, racing the foreground POST against the sequential StructuredFakeHttpServer accept loop. Fix pins gateway_url=ws://127.0.0.1:1/ in setup_configure so the gateway task attempts a WS connect (fails fast with ECONNREFUSED, supervisor retries with backoff long enough to outlive the test) instead of hitting the REST fake server. Verified: all 63 fcp-discord integration tests pass, including previously flaky send_message_happy_path, api_401_maps_to_unauthorized, and api_429_maps_to_rate_limited.

title: [SC] Host verification pipeline + policy gate
description:
# [SC] Host verification pipeline + policy gate

## Goal
Verify attestation + SBOM before connector install/upgrade and enforce policy gates in fcp-host with deterministic evidence bundles.

## Deliverables
- Verification pipeline steps:
  - Parse manifest + binary digest.
  - Verify attestation signatures and bind to artifact digest.
  - Verify SBOM signature and hash match.
  - Enforce policy (require_attestation, min_slsa_level, trusted_builders, rekor_required, allow_unsigned).
  - Produce evidence bundle (verification steps, hashes, trust roots, timestamps).
- Policy config surface in host (zone or global).
- Evidence bundle stored as mesh object (deterministic, redacted).

## Design Notes
- Fail closed by default; allow_unsigned must be explicit and scoped to dev.
- Verification must be deterministic (ordering, canonical encoding, stable hashes).
- Redact secrets and opaque tokens in logs/evidence.
- Cache verified artifacts for offline installs; cache keyed by digest.

## Tests
- Unit tests for each verification rule and error code mapping.
- Integration tests with test connectors + signed/unsigned fixtures.
- Property tests for determinism (same inputs -> same bundle hash).
- Structured JSON logging for each verification step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Missing/invalid attestations block install unless policy allows.
- Evidence bundle is deterministic, audit-ready, and redacted.
- Clear, actionable error codes for each failure case.

# Mesh Trace Capture + Replay Debugger

## Goal
Enable deterministic capture and replay of mesh traffic for debugging and incident analysis.

## Why
- Reproduce complex mesh failures offline.
- Provide evidence bundles for audits and regressions.
- Improve developer velocity for hard-to-debug issues.

## Scope
- Trace format with redaction policy.
- Capture hooks in MeshNode (routing/admission/leases).
- Replay engine + CLI with deterministic playback.

## Non-goals
- Full production tracing UI; CLI only for now.

## Deliverables
- Trace schema + canonical encoding rules.
- Redaction policy (PII, secrets, tokens).
- MeshNode capture with sampling and size caps.
- Replay engine + `fcp trace replay` CLI.
- Unit/integration tests + E2E script with structured logs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Captures can be replayed to reproduce routing/admission decisions.
- Sensitive fields are redacted or encrypted.
- Deterministic outputs for identical traces.

title: fcp.spotify: Library Management
description:
# fcp.spotify: Library Management (FCP2)

## Goal
Enable safe access to the user’s library:
- list saved tracks/albums/shows
- save/unsave items

Library writes modify user state and must be auditable.

## Scope
- Get saved tracks/albums/shows/episodes (pagination).
- Save/unsave items.
- Check whether items are saved.

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `spotify.library.read`
- `spotify.library.write` (dangerous-ish)

## FCP2 requirements
- Single-zone binding.
- NetworkConstraints pinned.
- For writes:
  - receipts + audit events include item ids and action
  - never log track names or personal context

## Deliverables
- Operation schemas:
  - `spotify.library.tracks.list`
  - `spotify.library.tracks.save`
  - `spotify.library.tracks.remove`
  - `spotify.library.albums.list`
  - `spotify.library.albums.save/remove`
  - `spotify.library.shows.list/save/remove`

## Test strategy (MUST)
- Mock-only tests for:
  - pagination
  - save/unsave idempotency
  - audit/receipt for writes

## Acceptance criteria
- Library operations are reliable, safe, and auditable.

title: [LOW] macOS sandbox filters coarser than Linux seccomp
description:
Cross-platform sandbox parity gap surfaced during fcp-sandbox review.

Linux (crates/fcp-sandbox/src/linux.rs) uses seccomp-bpf to deny individual syscalls at the kernel boundary, with a built-per-policy allowlist including architecture validation (x86_64/aarch64) and an explicit SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS catch-all.

macOS (crates/fcp-sandbox/src/macos.rs:265-266, :459) relies on sandbox_init profiles which are coarser:
  - RLIMIT_NPROC is intentionally NOT set when deny_exec=true (NPTL threads count as procs, would starve the runtime).
  - Syscall-level denial is replaced by higher-level profile deny rules. Some denials that seccomp would KILL at the kernel the macOS profile only rejects at the Mach/BSD API layer.

Windows (crates/fcp-sandbox/src/windows.rs:134, :404) has no syscall filtering at all -- deny_exec relies on job-object process-limit. Even coarser than macOS.

Impact: a hostile connector exploiting a previously-unknown native-API path that sandbox_init does not cover may be blocked on Linux (seccomp deny-by-default) but reach kernel on macOS/Windows.

Not urgent: all three platforms still enforce the main deny_exec/deny_ptrace contract through some mechanism, and strict-profile connectors run under WASI (no host syscalls reach the kernel at all). Landing a tighter macOS profile or Windows integrity-level sandbox would raise parity but is a multi-day project.

Suggested follow-up: tighten macOS sandbox_init profile to include the specific syscall families that the Linux seccomp filter currently denies but the macOS profile does not; evaluate WinSandbox / AppContainer for Windows parity.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Shipped FilterStrength cross-platform parity metric in commit 5553845d. Linux=SyscallLevel (seccomp-bpf), macOS=ProfileLevel (sandbox_init SBPL), Windows=ProcessLimit (job objects only). Added rustdoc table explaining each tier's mechanism, why the macOS RLIMIT_NPROC skip and the Windows absence of a syscall/profile filter land us below Linux, and the strict-profile→WasiRuntime escape hatch. Added platform-matrix test suite: ordering invariant, expected_for_target_os lookup, conservative-default guard, host-sandbox assertion, per-platform cfg-gated assertions. Next step when appetite returns: AppContainer on Windows and tightening the macOS profile to hit ProfileLevel-or-better parity end-to-end.

title: Testing Completeness Program: non-mock acceptance coverage and high-signal E2E evidence
description:
Background:
- The repo already has meaningful testing assets: `crates/fcp-e2e`, `crates/fcp-host/tests/host_connector_integration.rs`, `fcp-testkit`, connector `tests/integration.rs`, and structured JSONL reporting.
- That is still not the same thing as full pure-unit coverage without mocks/fake peers or complete end-to-end acceptance coverage with operator-grade logs.
- The current 2026-03-23 inventory says the workspace has 149 connector directories and 28 core crates; 139/149 connectors show unit-test signal, 100/149 have crate-local `tests/`, 84/149 have `fcp-e2e` coverage, 0/149 expose connector-level `no_mock_integration.rs`, only 8 connectors document verification bundles, and logging/replay evidence exists for 92/149 connectors.
- The user question behind this program is therefore settled: no, the repo does not yet have full unit coverage without fake-backed confidence, and no, it does not yet have complete non-mock E2E scripts with great detailed logging across the workspace.

Program goal:
- Make pure-unit coverage explicit and truthful, with fake-backed suites demoted to `deterministic_contract` rather than silently counting as final unit evidence.
- Give every core crate and connector family an archetype-appropriate acceptance path: `local_non_mock`, `host_e2e`, `live`, or a documented combination.
- Make every E2E-capable suite emit durable, redacted, replayable artifacts that let future agents debug failures without rediscovering the whole test setup.

Definition of done for the overall program:
- The coverage matrix and acceptance taxonomy stay current and are enforced.
- Shared harnesses exist for HTTP, streaming/webhook/session, and DB/storage/queue/browser/local-process boundaries.
- Connector-family sweeps close both pure-unit floor gaps and non-mock acceptance gaps.
- Nightly/live suites have an explicit operating model for secrets, cost, cleanup, and artifact retention.
- CI and maintainer playbooks make the whole testing story executable rather than aspirational.
notes: Clarification: repo policy still forbids real external-service calls in unit tests. This program treats "no mocks/fake stuff" as a requirement for acceptance layers (`local_non_mock`, `host_e2e`, `live`) while `pure_unit` stays focused on local logic and truthful suite classification.

title: Audit current workspace test surface and publish a connector/core coverage gap matrix
description:

- Before changing test infrastructure, we need one authoritative inventory of what exists today.
- The current workspace mixes inline unit tests, `tests/integration.rs`, crate-level `no_mock_integration.rs`, `fcp-e2e` compliance suites, host subprocess tests, and many `wiremock`/`MockApiServer` suites.

Deliverables:
- Build a connector-by-connector and core-crate-by-core-crate matrix that records: unit tests present, integration tests present, `wiremock`/fake reliance, `no_mock_integration` presence, host-backed subprocess coverage, `fcp-e2e` coverage, logging/report schema validation, live/provider prerequisites, and known gaps.
- Explicitly classify which current tests are deterministic contract tests versus true non-mock acceptance tests.
- Group results by connector archetype so later waves can execute systematically instead of ad hoc.

Acceptance criteria:
- The matrix covers every current connector directory and every core crate that participates in runtime, policy, host, protocol, or observability behavior.
- Missing suites are prioritized by risk and user impact, not just by alphabetical order.
- The output is self-contained enough that future agents can plan from the matrix without repeating the archaeology pass.

title: Developer-platform and automation connectors: non-mock acceptance wave
description:
Background:
- Developer-platform and automation connectors often look easy because they are HTTP APIs, but they also have rollout, artifact, webhook, and long-running job semantics that simple mocks miss.

Scope:
- GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, CircleCI, Package Registry, DockerHub, Make, n8n, Browser, MCP Bridge, Webhook Receiver, Vercel, Netlify, and related developer-platform or automation connectors.

Deliverables:
- Add non-mock acceptance coverage for auth, polling/job-state transitions, webhook or callback flows, artifact handling, pagination, and mutation safety semantics.
- Validate host-backed operation flows end to end, including logging and receipt/approval behavior where relevant.
- Close missing compliance E2E gaps in this family and demote mock-only suites to supplemental status.

Acceptance criteria:
- Developer-platform connectors are covered by acceptance suites that exercise real workflows, not just static HTTP payload fixtures.
- Failures produce enough detail to debug CI/automation regressions without manual repro.

title: Cloud, infra, storage, and database connectors: non-mock acceptance wave
description:
Background:
- Cloud, infra, storage, and database connectors are high-risk because they often mutate external state or rely on durable local services.
- They need seeded environments, teardown discipline, and clearer acceptance evidence than mock-only request assertions.

Scope:
- AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare, Kubernetes, Terraform, Pulumi, S3, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB, Supabase, Pinecone, Qdrant, VectorDB, and related storage/infra/data-plane connectors.

Deliverables:
- Build family-wide non-mock acceptance coverage for health, discovery, read/write/mutation behavior, safety semantics, drift/repair paths, retries, and rollback or cancellation where applicable.
- Use seeded local services or truthful sandbox environments instead of relying on fake-only tests for final acceptance.
- Standardize teardown, artifact capture, and diagnostic logging for stateful services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stateful and infra-facing connectors have a credible acceptance path with deterministic cleanup and high-signal diagnostics.
- Risky mutations are verified with truthful idempotency/safety evidence rather than hand-wavy tests.

title: Cloud control-plane and infrastructure-as-code acceptance sweep
description:
Background:
- Cloud control-plane and IaC connectors are high-risk because they can mutate live infrastructure even in supposedly test-only environments.

Deliverables:
- Sweep AWS, Azure, Cloudflare, Kubernetes, Terraform, Pulumi, Firebase, and related infra connectors for truthful acceptance coverage, seeded test environments, and safety/idempotency evidence.
- Separate read-only flows from risky mutations in both tests and artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Infra connectors have a credible acceptance story with explicit cleanup and mutation controls.

title: Relational and local database connector acceptance sweep
description:
Background:
- Relational and embedded database connectors should be the easiest place to prove local_non_mock acceptance, yet the inventory still shows missing or insufficient real-engine coverage.

Deliverables:
- Sweep SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, and similar connectors against real local engines with seeded state, migration/setup discipline, and artifact capture.
- Close the gap between unit coverage and true data-plane acceptance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Relational/local database connectors have reproducible real-engine acceptance suites with deterministic cleanup.

title: Object, blob, key-value, vector, and data-plane acceptance sweep
description:
Background:
- Object/blob, key-value, vector, analytics, and broader data-plane connectors often fall between HTTP and DB categories, which is why they need an explicit dedicated sweep.

Deliverables:
- Sweep S3/object-storage, Redis, MongoDB, Supabase, BigQuery, Snowflake, Pinecone, Qdrant, and related connectors for truthful fixture/live acceptance, retries, paging, mutation safety, and recovery behavior.
- Standardize the evidence captured for uploads, downloads, queries, and destructive operations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Data-plane connectors stop relying on mock-only proof for their core mutation/read behavior.
