title: fcp.reddit: User Posting and Commenting
description:
# fcp.reddit: User Posting and Commenting (FCP2)

## Goal
Enable controlled Reddit participation:
- submit posts
- submit comments
- edit/delete own content

These are real-world side effects and must be tightly capability scoped.

## Scope
- Submit post to a subreddit (text/link).
- Submit comment.
- Edit content.
- Delete content.

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `reddit.post.write` (dangerous)
- `reddit.comment.write` (dangerous)
- `reddit.content.edit` (dangerous)

Policy guidance:
- Posting should often require ApprovalToken depending on zone policy.

## FCP2 requirements
- Single-zone binding.
- NetworkConstraints pinned.
- Content safety:
  - outbound content must be treated as a “publication” action
  - receipts + audit events include subreddit + post/comment id
  - never log post bodies

## Deliverables
- Operation schemas:
  - `reddit.post.submit`
  - `reddit.comment.submit`
  - `reddit.content.edit`
  - `reddit.content.delete`

## Test strategy (MUST)
- Mock-only tests for:
  - request formation
  - approval gating
  - audit/receipt emission
  - error mapping (subreddit rules, forbidden)

## Acceptance criteria
- Write operations are mechanically authorized, explainable, and auditable.

title: fcp.airtable: Attachment upload and download handling
description:
# fcp.airtable: Attachment Upload and Download Handling

## Goal
Handle Airtable attachments safely under strict sandboxing.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Scope
Operations (representative):
- `airtable.attachments.upload`
- `airtable.attachments.get` (fetch attachment metadata/URL)
- optional: `airtable.attachments.download` (if we choose to implement actual download)

## Key requirements
- Capability gated:
  - read vs write separated
- NetworkConstraints:
  - Airtable API host(s) allowed
  - attachment download hosts must be explicitly enumerated/pinned
  - validate URLs are HTTPS and match allowlist
- Data handling:
  - attachments move as **ObjectId references** (no local disk persistence)
  - enforce size limits and streaming bounds
- Logging:
  - never log attachment contents
  - URLs may contain opaque tokens; treat as sensitive

## Tests
- Allow/deny matrix for attachment URL hosts.
- Size limit and timeout tests.
- Redaction tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Attachment flows are safe-by-default and deterministic.
- Non-allowed hosts are blocked by Network Guard.

description:
# fcp.airtable: Full CRUD Operations on Records

## Goal
Implement record CRUD with batching, pagination, and strict safety controls.

## External surface (NetworkConstraints)
Default deny.
- Network egress MUST be restricted per-operation via manifest `NetworkConstraints`.
- Allow only the configured service host(s); HTTPS-only where applicable; deny redirects by default.
- Bound timeouts + response sizes; treat all remote responses as untrusted input; never leak secrets/PII in logs or errors.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Scope
Operations (representative):
- `airtable.records.list` (pagination, filter/sort)
- `airtable.records.get`
- `airtable.records.create` / `airtable.records.create_batch`
- `airtable.records.update` / `airtable.records.update_batch`
- `airtable.records.upsert`
- `airtable.records.delete` / `airtable.records.delete_batch` (Dangerous)

## Key requirements
- Capability gated:
  - read vs write vs delete are separate capabilities
- Rate limiting and backpressure are mechanical.
- Pagination:
  - support continuation tokens
  - bound page sizes
- Batch operations:
  - handle partial failures deterministically
  - stable error mapping per record
- Idempotency / retries:
  - upsert is preferred for retry-safe workflows
  - deletes and schema writes must be treated as Dangerous (policy + receipts)

## Tests
- Mock-only tests cover:
  - pagination edge cases
  - batch partial failure semantics
  - upsert conflict handling
  - redaction: never log record bodies by default

## Acceptance Criteria
- CRUD operations behave deterministically under retries.
- Dangerous operations are properly gated and audited.

title: fcp-slack: ok=true responses can panic on missing payload data
description:
## Finding
`SlackApiResponse<T>` stores the flattened success payload as `Option<T>` ([connectors/slack/src/types.rs:123-129](connectors/slack/src/types.rs:123)). `check_response()` only checks `ok` ([connectors/slack/src/client.rs:447-458](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:447)). Multiple client paths then call `resp.data.expect("ok response has data")` ([connectors/slack/src/client.rs:162](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:162), [209](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:209), [228](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:228), [238](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:238), [257](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:257), [270](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:270), [282](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:282), [302](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:302), [312](connectors/slack/src/client.rs:312)).

A malformed or partial `ok:true` body therefore becomes a process panic instead of an `FcpError`/`SlackError`. The crate already documents the `None` case in tests (`slack_api_response_error_has_no_data`), so this is not theoretical parser behavior.

## Repro shape
Return `{"ok":true}` or `{"ok":true,"channel":"C1"}` from `chat.postMessage`. `check_response()` accepts it and the subsequent `.expect(...)` aborts the connector.

## Recommendation
Replace each `.expect("ok response has data")` with an error-mapped `ok_or_else(...)` path that preserves the operation context and treats malformed success envelopes as API/protocol errors, not panics.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fixed in 2dd92d08. Root cause: 9 client paths called .expect("ok response has data") on a flattened Option<T> payload — a partial {"ok":true} envelope therefore panicked the connector instead of surfacing as an error. Fix: added Self::expect_data(data, method) helper that maps None to a terminal SlackError::Api { ok: true, error: "Slack API method \`X\` returned ok=true with no payload", .. }, and migrated all 9 call sites through it. The ok:true discriminator preserves the partial-envelope case as distinct from classic ok=false errors. Regression test ok_true_with_missing_payload_is_mapped_to_api_error_not_panic asserts the method name and 'ok=true' phrase appear in the error, and that to_fcp_error() maps to FcpError::External. Verified: 210 lib tests + 51/52 integration tests pass (the one pre-existing failure list_channels_happy_path is an unrelated URL-encoding bug confirmed by bisect).

title: [FCP3/P3.2] Define canonical FCPS durable object schemas for runtime truth
description:
Background: a mesh first platform needs durable forms for the facts that survive process death and justify later decisions. Receipts, checkpoints, lease state, revocations, connector runtime state, and operator explanations cannot remain host local conventions.

Scope: define canonical FCPS object schemas for durable state, including connector identity and state, receipts, checkpoints, lease and fencing records, revocation records, and explanation bundles. Design them for replay, repair, inspection, and failover rather than as opaque storage details. Provide deterministic object examples, snapshot formats, explanation bundle shapes, schema unit tests, replay integration tests, and detailed inspection logs that later conformance and end to end harnesses can diff and diagnose.

Acceptance: the platform has a durable object vocabulary for the facts it must remember, those facts no longer depend on one host memory image to exist, and the schemas are concrete enough for fixture driven validation, replay, operator inspection, and regression tests.

title: fuzz/fcps_frame: target only decodes frames/symbols without checking accepted-state invariants
description:
File: fuzz/fuzz_targets/fcps_frame.rs:18-37

Finding: the fuzz body only calls `FcpsFrameHeader::decode`, `FcpsFrame::decode`, `SymbolRecord::decode`, and `FrameFlags::from_bits_truncate`, then drops all successful results.

Why this matters: the target is good for panic discovery but weak for semantic coverage. It never checks that successfully decoded frames and symbol records obey internal size/header invariants.

Suggested follow-up: when decode succeeds, assert header/frame consistency, record bounds consistency, and stable behavior across repeated decode paths.
close_reason: Verified: commit fe65bacc — fuzz/fcps_frame.rs now asserts (a) structural round-trip equality, (b) flags-truncation conditional header byte-equality, (c) length-field consistency, plus header-vs-frame agreement and encode determinism. Mirrors br-j5iby fcpc_frame pattern.

title: fcp-raptorq: encode_all/into_encode_all ESI arithmetic uses wrapping add, not checked_add
description:
In `crates/fcp-raptorq/src/encode.rs:141-144` (`encode_all`) and `crates/fcp-raptorq/src/encode.rs:162-166` (`into_encode_all`), the repair symbol ESI is computed as `k_prime + i` where both are u32. In debug builds, overflow panics; in release, it wraps into the source-symbol ESI range and silently collides with existing source symbols.

**Bounded in practice.** `config.repair_symbols(source_symbols)` saturates to `u32::MAX`, but `source_symbols` comes from `payload_len.div_ceil(symbol_size)` where `payload_len ≤ config.max_object_size` (typically 64 MiB) and `symbol_size >= 1`. So `source_symbols ≤ 64 MiB`, well under u32::MAX. The current config bounds keep the arithmetic safe.

**Brittle.** The rest of the crate uses `saturating_add` / `checked_add` consistently (see `config.rs:155`, `decode.rs:585`, `decode.rs:598`). `encode.rs:142` and `encode.rs:164` are the only sites that use raw `+` on user-derived-ish arithmetic with no bound check.

**Suggested fix**: `let esi = k_prime.checked_add(i).ok_or(EncodeError::SymbolCountOverflow)?;` (or saturating_add). Mirror the `decode.rs:585` pattern.

Severity: LOW. Not currently exploitable; filed as a defensive-depth bead to keep the saturating/checked arithmetic discipline uniform across the crate.

title: [FCP2] Rate Limiting: ThrottleViolation, Backpressure Signals, Quota Enforcement
description:
# [FCP2] Rate Limiting: ThrottleViolation, Backpressure Signals, Quota Enforcement

## Goal
Implement rate limiting at multiple layers: per-connector, per-operation, per-zone, and mesh-wide.

## Why This Matters
Without rate limiting:
- A runaway connector can exhaust external API quotas
- A compromised node can DoS the mesh
- Resource exhaustion becomes undetectable until failure

## Rate Limit Layers

### Layer 1: Connector Manifest Limits
Declared in connector manifest:
```toml
[rate_limits]
requests_per_minute = 60
requests_per_hour = 1000
concurrent_operations = 5
```

### Layer 2: Zone Policy Limits
```
ZonePolicy.rate_limits {
  per_connector_rpm: u32,
  per_zone_rpm: u32,
  burst_allowance: f32,  // multiplier for burst
}
```

### Layer 3: Capability Limits
Capabilities can include rate constraints:
```
CapabilityGrant.constraints.rate_limit {
  max_per_minute: 10,
  max_concurrent: 2,
}
```

### Layer 4: MeshNode Admission Control
Global limits per peer node (covered in admission control bead).

## ThrottleViolation Object
When rate limit is exceeded:
```
ThrottleViolation {
  violation_id: ObjectId,
  timestamp: u64,
  zone_id: ZoneId,
  connector_id: Option<ConnectorId>,
  operation_id: Option<SchemaId>,
  limit_type: LimitType,  // RPM, Concurrent, Burst, Quota
  limit_value: u32,
  current_value: u32,
  retry_after_ms: u64,
}
```

ThrottleViolation is:
- Recorded in audit chain
- Returned in InvokeResponse error
- Triggers backpressure signals

## Backpressure Protocol
When approaching limits:
1. **Warning Zone (80%)**: Emit metric, log warning
2. **Soft Limit (95%)**: Return `retry_after_ms` in responses
3. **Hard Limit (100%)**: Reject with FCP-4290 (RateLimited)

For streaming operations:
- Flow control via FCPC backpressure frames
- Connector can request pause/resume

## Token Bucket Implementation
Use token bucket algorithm with:
- `capacity`: max burst size
- `refill_rate`: tokens per second
- `current_tokens`: available tokens

Tokens are consumed per-operation based on:
- Base cost (1 token)
- Size cost (for data transfer)
- Compute cost (for expensive operations)

## Tests
- Unit tests: token bucket refill and consumption
- Property tests: rate limit never exceeds declared max
- Integration tests: concurrent requests properly limited
- Adversarial tests: burst exhaustion followed by gradual recovery
- E2E tests: ThrottleViolation appears in audit chain

## Acceptance Criteria
- Rate limits are enforced at all layers
- ThrottleViolation objects are recorded for audit
- Backpressure signals enable graceful degradation
notes:
Progress: implemented core rate-limit artifacts + enforcement primitives.

- fcp-core: added ThrottleViolation (+ ThrottleViolationInput), LimitType, BackpressureLevel/Signal; extended FcpError::RateLimited to carry optional boxed ThrottleViolation and include it in structured error details.
- fcp-ratelimit: added FCP glue (config_from_core, enforce() -> EnforcementOutcome w/ backpressure + violation); token cost model (base + bytes ceil-div + compute); ConcurrencyLimiter with try_acquire_or_violation(); RateLimiter::try_acquire_n and atomic multi-permit TokenBucket consumption.
- Tests: new unit tests for backpressure thresholds, violation propagation into FcpErrorResponse.details, token cost, concurrency limiter, and atomic multi-permit consumption.
- Quality gates: cargo fmt/check/clippy/test all green.

Remaining (blocked by other beads): integrate with policy engine + audit chain storage, and mesh-wide admission control + E2E scenarios.
close_reason: Core rate-limit artifacts + enforcement primitives complete: ThrottleViolation, BackpressureLevel/Signal, TokenBucket, ConcurrencyLimiter, FCP glue (config_from_core, enforce). Unit tests pass (oz1v closed). Remaining mesh-wide admission control + E2E integration blocked on MeshNode (1n78.17).

title: fcp-registry: MockTufVerifier/MockSigstoreVerifier/MockTransparencyVerifier exported publicly from src/ (trust-bypass footgun)
description:
## Finding

Three \"Mock\" verifiers that short-circuit supply-chain trust are declared as \`pub struct\` in \`crates/fcp-registry/src/lib.rs\` with no \`#[cfg(test)]\` or feature gate. They ship in every downstream binary that depends on \`fcp-registry\`:

* \`MockTransparencyVerifier\` — lib.rs:583  (returns \`verified: true\` for any \`entry_hash\` inserted into an in-memory \`HashMap\`)
* \`MockTufVerifier\` — lib.rs:625  (returns \`verified: true\` for any target inserted via \`add_valid_target\`)
* \`MockSigstoreVerifier\` — lib.rs:693  (same pattern — pure in-memory allow-list)

Each implements the real verifier trait (\`TransparencyLogVerifier\`, \`TufVerifier\`, \`SigstoreVerifier\`) so they are drop-in substitutes anywhere the host expects a verifier. A single misconfigured \`RegistryBuilder\` call accepts arbitrary signatures.

Grep confirms they are currently only consumed by \`crates/fcp-registry/tests/no_mock_integration.rs\`, so the footgun has not fired yet. The problem is that nothing in the compiler or lint layer prevents it from firing.

## Why it matters (P2)

1. **Trust-bypass path is one import away.** A downstream developer who writes \`use fcp_registry::MockSigstoreVerifier;\` gets a verifier that accepts any bundle. There is no compile-time error and no runtime warning.

2. **\`impl SigstoreVerifier for MockSigstoreVerifier\` means the mock is interchangeable** with the real verifier in every code path that takes \`Arc<dyn SigstoreVerifier>\`. That is precisely the surface the registry uses to gate signed-artifact installs.

3. **Unrelated bug surface inside the mocks.** Lines 594, 605, 641, 672, 706, 720 all call \`.lock().unwrap()\` on \`std::sync::Mutex\` — a panic on poison, inside async handler code. If the mock is ever plugged into an async code path, a single panic-while-holding poisons the mutex and the next request crashes the handler. Lines 652, 750, 942, 1035 \`expect(\"system clock before year 2262\")\` on \`Utc::now().timestamp()\` — the real panic condition is a \*negative\* timestamp (pre-1970), not year 2262; message is wrong AND the path is unhandled.

## Fix (pick one)

**Option A — feature gate (smallest diff).** Add

    [features]
    test-mocks = []

    [[test]]
    name = \"no_mock_integration\"
    required-features = [\"test-mocks\"]

Then prefix each mock with \`#[cfg(any(test, feature = \"test-mocks\"))]\`. Existing \`cargo test\` callers must pass \`--features test-mocks\` (or the workspace \`[alias]\` in \`.cargo/config.toml\` does it).

**Option B — separate test-support crate.** Move the three mocks to \`fcp-registry-testkit\` (mirroring the \`fcp-testkit\` pattern in this repo). Integration tests \`use fcp_registry_testkit::MockSigstoreVerifier;\`. Zero risk of production imports.

**Option C (NOT recommended) — \`#[cfg(test)]\`.** Breaks integration tests because \`tests/\*.rs\` compiles the lib in non-test configuration.

## Verification

After the fix:

  * \`cargo build -p fcp-registry --release\` MUST NOT expose \`Mock*Verifier\` in the public API. Confirm via \`cargo public-api\`.
  * \`cargo test -p fcp-registry\` MUST still pass (tests access the mocks through whichever gate is chosen).
  * Add a \`#[deny(missing_docs)]\` or a \`/// # Safety: test-only — MUST NOT reach production\` docstring to each type for belt-and-braces.

## Related (same pattern, other crates)

Scan hit exact pattern in \`crates/fcp-tailscale/src/client.rs:337 MockTailscaleClient\` — same public-from-lib.rs shape, same remediation. Separate bead not filed here to keep this one focused on the registry trust-anchor surface, but the fix pattern is identical.
close_reason: Verified: commit cdcf712f implements Option A — Mock*Verifier in fcp-registry and MockTailscaleClient in fcp-tailscale gated on cfg(any(test, feature="test-mocks")) with required-features on the integration test binary. Downstream consumers cannot import the types without explicit feature opt-in.

title: Connector timeout sweep: extract Duration::from_secs(30) pattern into manifest-driven configuration

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EPIC: Connector Timeout Sweep

~80+ connectors hard-code Duration::from_secs(30) in their ConnectorRuntimeConfig construction:
  ConnectorRuntimeConfig::default().with_request_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))

This is the single most repeated hard-coded constant in the entire codebase. While 30s is reasonable for most REST APIs, it's wrong for:
- Long-running operations (Anthropic inference: 300s, video transcription: 600s+)
- Fast operations (key-value lookups: 5s is generous)
- Unreliable networks (need longer timeouts)

CURRENT STATE:
Connectors already use ConnectorRuntimeConfig which has a with_request_timeout() builder. The problem is that the *value* is compiled in rather than loaded from the connector's manifest.toml or an environment variable.

FIX APPROACH:
1. Add a [timeouts] section to manifest.toml schema:
   [timeouts]
   request_timeout_ms = 30000
   connect_timeout_ms = 5000

2. Update ConnectorRuntimeConfig::from_manifest() to load timeout from manifest
3. Support FCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS env var as a global override
4. Support per-connector env var: FCP_{CONNECTOR_ID}_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
5. Hierarchy: explicit code > per-connector env > global env > manifest > compiled default

This is a mechanical sweep that can be done per-connector-family. The manifest.toml schema change is the foundation that unblocks all per-connector work.

NOTE: Not every connector needs individual attention. The pattern change happens once in the SDK/manifest layer, then connectors pick it up automatically. Individual connector beads below are only needed for connectors that need NON-default timeouts (Anthropic, whisper, terraform, etc.).

title: fcp.kubernetes connector - Container orchestration integration
description:
# fcp.kubernetes - Container Orchestration Integration Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Deliver the FCP2 Kubernetes connector epic plan for safe cluster introspection and controlled mutations under strict NetworkConstraints, credential handling, and policy-gated dangerous operations.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 82/100** — Important Tier 3 connector (Infrastructure family).

**Why Critical**: Kubernetes is the **dominant container orchestration platform**, running production workloads at most tech companies. Enables agents to manage deployments, investigate pod issues, scale services, and automate DevOps workflows. Essential for cloud-native operations.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Specialized Investment (Infrastructure + High Complexity)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 3 Enterprise (weeks 9-12)

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Workload Management
- Deploy and update applications
- Scale deployments
- Rollback deployments
- Restart pods

### Investigation
- Pod logs access
- Event monitoring
- Resource status checks
- Container exec (with restrictions)

### Configuration
- ConfigMap management
- Secret access (controlled)
- Service and ingress inspection
- Namespace operations

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"What pods are crashing in production?"
"Scale the API deployment to 5 replicas"
"Show logs from the failing pod"
"Rollback the frontend to previous version"
"What's using the most memory?"
"Check events for this deployment"
"Apply this manifest to staging"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Grafana/Datadog Integration
**Full observability stack:**
- K8s metrics via Prometheus
- Pod logs via Loki/Datadog
- Container traces
- Agent correlates infrastructure state with metrics

### Sentry Integration
- Link crashes to pod restarts
- Correlate errors with deployments
- Resource exhaustion → error patterns

### GitHub Integration
**GitOps workflows:**
- Git changes → K8s manifests
- ArgoCD/Flux integration
- Deployment tracking

### Terraform Integration
- Cluster infrastructure via Terraform
- Workloads via Kubernetes connector
- Full infrastructure automation

### Agent Mail Integration
- Incident alerts → agent investigation
- Deployment coordination
- On-call handoff workflows

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **Core API** — Pods, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets
- **Apps API** — Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets
- **Batch API** — Jobs, CronJobs
- **Networking API** — Ingress, NetworkPolicies

### Authentication Modes
| Mode | Use Case |
|------|----------|
| Kubeconfig | Local/development |
| ServiceAccount | In-cluster |
| OIDC | Enterprise SSO |
| Cloud Provider | EKS/GKE/AKS auth |

### Recommended Crates
- `kube` — Kubernetes client for Rust
- `k8s-openapi` — Type-safe K8s API bindings
- `tokio` — Async runtime

### Resource Hierarchy
```
Namespace
├── Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet
│   └── ReplicaSet
│       └── Pod
│           └── Container
├── Service
├── ConfigMap
├── Secret
└── Ingress
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:infra:k8s:full` | Full cluster access | All operations |
| `z:infra:k8s:readonly` | Read-only | Queries and logs |
| `z:infra:k8s:namespace:<name>` | Namespace-scoped | Single namespace |
| `z:infra:k8s:deploy` | Deployment only | Scale, rollback |

### Safety Tiers
- **Read**: Logs, status, events — low risk
- **Deploy**: Scale, rollback — moderate risk
- **Write**: Apply manifests — high risk
- **Exec**: Container access — very high risk

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — API operations
- `streaming` — Watch events, log streaming

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Varies by deployment:
- In-cluster: `kubernetes.default.svc:443`
- Cloud: EKS/GKE/AKS API endpoints
- Self-hosted: configured API server

### Credential Injection
- Kubeconfig via file reference
- ServiceAccount token via mounted secret
- Cloud credentials via `CredentialId`
- Never write credentials to disk

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `k8s.pods.read` — List/get pods
- `k8s.pods.logs` — Stream logs
- `k8s.deployments.read` — Deployment status
- `k8s.events.read` — Cluster events
- `k8s.services.read` — Service info
- `k8s.configmaps.read` — Config data
- `k8s.secrets.read` — Secret metadata (not values by default)

### Write Operations
- `k8s.deployments.scale` — Scale replicas
- `k8s.deployments.rollback` — Rollback version
- `k8s.pods.delete` — Restart pods
- `k8s.configmaps.write` — Update configs

### Administrative (Dangerous)
- `k8s.manifests.apply` — Apply arbitrary YAML
- `k8s.pods.exec` — Execute in container
- `k8s.secrets.values` — Read secret values
- `k8s.namespaces.delete` — Delete namespace

---

## Operations (Representative)

### List Pods
```rust
let pods: Api<Pod> = Api::namespaced(client, "production");
let list = pods.list(&ListParams::default()).await?;
```

### Get Pod Logs
```rust
let pods: Api<Pod> = Api::namespaced(client, "production");
let logs = pods.logs("api-pod-abc123", &LogParams {
    container: Some("api".into()),
    tail_lines: Some(100),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
```

### Scale Deployment
```rust
let deployments: Api<Deployment> = Api::namespaced(client, "production");
let patch = json!({
    "spec": {
        "replicas": 5
    }
});
deployments.patch_scale("api", &PatchParams::default(), &Patch::Merge(&patch)).await?;
```

### Watch Events
```rust
let events: Api<Event> = Api::all(client);
let watcher = watcher(events, Config::default());
// Stream events as they occur
```

---

## Safety Considerations

### Blast Radius Control
- Prefer namespace-scoped access
- Avoid cluster-admin by default
- Rate limit write operations

### Sensitive Operations
| Operation | Risk | Mitigation |
|-----------|------|------------|
| `exec` | Very High | Disabled by default, audit all uses |
| `delete namespace` | High | Require explicit confirmation |
| `apply manifest` | Medium | Validate against schema |
| `read secrets` | Medium | Mask values, log access |

### Audit Requirements
- All K8s API calls logged
- Secret access specially flagged

title: [IDEA-27] Connector State Fork Resolution Workflow
description:
## Background
Stateful connectors must be single-writer; forks are safety incidents. We need detection and a structured resolution workflow.

## Goals
- Detect forked ConnectorStateObject chains.
- Pause connector execution and emit audit evidence.
- Provide tooling to resolve/merge or choose a head.

## Non-goals
- Automatic conflict resolution without operator input.

## Approach
- Add fork detection in state manager (same prev, divergent heads).
- Emit `ConnectorStateFork` audit event.
- Add CLI `fcp connector state resolve` to select resolution strategy.

## Risks
- Incorrect resolution could lose state; require explicit approval.

## Success Criteria
- Forks are detected deterministically and block further writes.
- Resolution workflow is auditable and reversible.

## Acceptance Criteria (Refined)
- Fork detection pauses connector writes immediately.
- Resolution emits audit event referencing chosen head.
notes:

- Add evidence ledger fields with per-check log-odds contributions and explicit loss decision.
- Add anytime-valid risk control (e-process) for approvals/denials and record epsilon in receipts.
[ExtremeOptimizationPractical]
- Compile policies to DAG/BDD and cache allow/deny results with LRU.
- Use bitset capability sets for fast subset checks.

title: TEST: Connector Performance Benchmark Suite
description:
# TEST: Connector Performance Benchmark Suite (FCP2)


## Goal
Establish a benchmark suite to measure and guard connector performance budgets (latency, memory, allocations) with regression tracking.

## Overview
Performance benchmarks ensuring the platform meets the README/spec targets.

Benchmarks must be:
- repeatable
- machine-readable
- diagnostic (logs + environment metadata)

## Benchmarks (README-aligned)
### `fcp bench connector-activate`
- cold start time (p50/p99)
- warm start time (optional)

### `fcp bench invoke-local`
- end-to-end invoke latency when caller/executor are the same node

### `fcp bench invoke-mesh --path=direct|derp`
- end-to-end invoke latency across the mesh for:
  - direct/LAN
  - DERP

### `fcp bench raptorq --size=1mb`
- encode/decode throughput and wall time
- memory high-water mark if available

### `fcp bench secrets --k=3 --n=5`
- secret reconstruction wall time + overhead

### Microbenches (hot primitives)
- canonical CBOR encode/decode
- ObjectId derivation
- CapabilityToken verify
- FCPS frame parse + session MAC verify

## Output
- JSON results with:
  - benchmark name + parameters
  - p50/p90/p99
  - environment (os/arch/cpu)
  - versions + commit hash
- Regression detection policy:
  - start with “report-only”
  - later enforce thresholds once baselines stabilize

## Logging Requirements
Per `flywheel_connectors-1n78.35`, logs must include:
- bench name/params
- sample counts
- any detected outliers

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite produces stable JSON shapes suitable for snapshot testing.
- Results are reproducible enough to catch real regressions (not noise).
close_reason:
Completed benchmark suite implementation:

IMPLEMENTED:
- Core benchmark runner with statistical analysis (percentiles, outlier detection)
- CBOR benchmarks: schema-hash, serialize, deserialize (small/medium objects)

- RaptorQ encode/decode benchmarks
- JSON and human-readable output formats
- Environment metadata collection (OS, arch, CPU, git commit, rustc version)
- Target threshold tracking with pass/fail determination

PLACEHOLDERS (awaiting dependencies):
- connector-activate (needs fcp-sdk)
- invoke-local (needs fcp-mesh)
- invoke-mesh (needs fcp-mesh)

All tests pass. Benchmarks produce stable JSON suitable for regression tracking.

title: fuzz/fcps_datagram: target only decodes datagrams at a few MTU limits
description:
File: fuzz/fuzz_targets/fcps_datagram.rs:14-25

Finding: the fuzz body only calls `FcpsDatagram::decode(data, mtu)` across a few constants and discards the result each time.

Why this matters: this is effectively parse-and-drop fuzzing. It does not assert any invariant about accepted datagrams, transport-limit handling, or consistency between successful decode paths.

Suggested follow-up: when decode succeeds, assert length/header invariants and compare outcomes across tighter vs looser MTU limits where success should be monotonic.
close_reason: Added FCPS datagram fuzz invariants for byte-stable round-trips, MTU-boundary monotonicity, and payload-length consistency.

title: STANDARD: Connector Testing Requirements and Quality Gates
description:
# STANDARD: Connector Testing Requirements and Quality Gates

## Goal
Define mandatory connector testing quality gates (mock-only unit tests + E2E compliance runs) so every connector is mechanically verifiable.

## Overview
Defines mandatory testing requirements and quality gates that ALL FCP connectors must pass before release.

This standard is connector-focused and builds on the platform-wide test/logging standard `flywheel_connectors-1n78.35`.

## Recommended Testing Stack (2025-2026)

| Category | Tool | Version | Notes |
|----------|------|---------|-------|
| Unit framework | `cargo test` | built-in | Standard Rust testing |
| Snapshot | `insta` | 1.40+ | JSON + terminal snapshots |
| Property | `proptest` | 0.11+ | Invariant/fuzzy testing |
| Mutation | `cargo-mutants` | 25.1+ | Mutation coverage |
| Fuzzing | `cargo-fuzz` | 0.12+ | Fuzz targets for parsing |
| HTTP mock | `wiremock` | 0.6+ | Async HTTP mocking |
| Assertions | `assert2` | 0.3+ | Better error messages |
| Coverage | `cargo-llvm-cov` | 0.6+ | LLVM-based coverage |
| Security | `cargo-audit` | 0.21+ | Dependency audit |
| Benchmarks | `criterion` | 0.6+ | Statistical benchmarks |

## Unit Test Requirements

### Coverage Thresholds
- Overall: >80% line coverage
- Critical paths: >95% coverage
- Security code: >98% coverage
- **Mutation score**: >70% (cargo-mutants)

### Required Test Categories
- [ ] All connector standard methods (`--manifest`, handshake/describe/introspect/capabilities/configure/invoke/health/shutdown)
- [ ] Configuration validation (valid/invalid)
- [ ] Handshake success/failure scenarios
- [ ] Capability token validation
- [ ] Each operation (success, common errors, edge cases)
- [ ] Rate limit handling
- [ ] Timeout behavior
- [ ] Error recovery
- [ ] **Property tests**: Random inputs for all string/struct parsing

### Mocking Requirements
- NEVER make real API calls in unit tests
- Use wiremock or similar for HTTP mocking
- Mock external service responses
- Test error injection (network, auth, rate limit)

### Property Testing Patterns
```rust
proptest\! {
    #[test]
    fn parse_config_doesnt_panic(input in ".*") {
        // Should never panic, only return Ok/Err
        let _ = ConnectorConfig::parse(&input);
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn roundtrip_serialization(config in arb_connector_config()) {
        let serialized = serde_json::to_string(&config)?;
        let deserialized: ConnectorConfig = serde_json::from_str(&serialized)?;
        prop_assert_eq\!(config, deserialized);
    }
}
```

## Fuzz Testing Requirements (Security-Critical)

### Required Fuzz Targets
Every connector MUST have fuzz targets for:
- [ ] Configuration parsing
- [ ] Protocol message parsing
- [ ] Credential/token handling
- [ ] Event payload parsing

### Fuzz Target Template
```rust
#\![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;

fuzz_target\!(|data: &[u8]| {
    // Should never panic, only return valid error
    let _ = connector::parse_message(data);
});
```

### CI Fuzz Integration
```yaml
- name: Fuzz for 60s per target
  run: cargo +nightly fuzz run --release --sanitizer=address -- -max_total_time=60
```

## Integration Test Requirements
- [ ] Real handshake flow (with test credentials) OR fully deterministic harness
- [ ] Basic operation execution
- [ ] Event subscription lifecycle
- [ ] Reconnection handling

## E2E Test Requirements (Mechanical Compliance)
Every connector MUST pass the platform E2E/compliance harness:
- [ ] Mechanical compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- [ ] Zone binding enforcement
- [ ] Default deny (no cap token → denial + DecisionReceipt)
- [ ] No secret leakage in logs
- [ ] Sandbox/network constraints enforced
- [ ] **Tool descriptor validation** (SEP-1382 compliance)

## Security Testing Requirements

### cargo-audit Gate
```yaml
- name: Security audit
  run: cargo audit --deny warnings --ignore RUSTSEC-XXXX
```

### Secret Leakage Detection
```rust
#[test]
fn no_secrets_in_logs() {
    let logs = capture_connector_logs();
    assert\!(\!logs.contains("api_key="));
    assert\!(\!logs.contains("Authorization:"));
    assert\!(\!logs.contains("Bearer "));
}
```

### Zeroize Verification
```rust
#[test]
fn credentials_are_zeroized_on_drop() {
    let cred = Credential::new("secret");
    let ptr = cred.as_ptr();
    drop(cred);
    // Memory should be zeroed
    unsafe { assert\!(std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, 6).iter().all(|&b| b == 0)); }
}
```

## Quality Gates (CI/CD)
1. `cargo check --all-targets` - No errors
2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` - No warnings
3. `cargo fmt --check` - Properly formatted
4. `cargo test` - All tests pass
5. `cargo test --release` - Release tests pass
6. Coverage threshold met (>80%)
7. `cargo audit --deny warnings` - Security scan clean
8. `cargo mutants --timeout-multiplier=2` - Mutation score >70%
9. Fuzz targets run without crash

## Connector Plan Template
For connector planning/bead structure (manifest/provisioning/tests/e2e), use:
- `flywheel_connectors-lszk.5` — STANDARD: Connector Spec Template (FCP2)

## CRITICAL: Detailed Logging Requirements

### All Tests MUST Include Comprehensive Logging

#### Log Levels by Test Phase
- **Setup**: INFO - test initialization, mock configuration
- **Execution**: DEBUG - every significant action
- **Assertions**: INFO - expected vs actual values
- **Teardown**: DEBUG - cleanup operations
- **Errors**: ERROR with full context

#### Required Log Fields (Structured JSON)
Every log entry MUST include:
- `timestamp` - ISO 8601 with milliseconds
- `test_name` - Full test path (module::test_fn)
- `phase` - setup|execute|assert|teardown
- `correlation_id` - Unique per test run
- `duration_ms` - Time since test start
- `operation` - Current operation being tested

When applicable, also include:
- `connector_id`, `zone_id`, `session_id`
- `decision`, `reason_code`, and evidence object IDs for denials

#### Log Format Example
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-11T12:00:00.123Z",
  "test_name": "discord::gateway::test_heartbeat_mechanism",
  "phase": "execute",
  "correlation_id": "a1b2c3d4",
  "duration_ms": 45,
  "operation": "send_heartbeat",
  "level": "DEBUG",
  "message": "Sending heartbeat frame",
  "details": {
    "sequence": 42,
    "interval_ms": 41250,
    "last_ack_at": "2026-01-11T11:59:58.500Z"
  }
}
```

#### Test Output Capture
- All tests run with `--nocapture` in CI for full visibility
- Failed tests include complete log history in reports
- Logs retained for 30 days for debugging
- Performance metrics extracted from logs for trending

## Documentation Requirements
- [ ] All public APIs documented
- [ ] AI hints for each operation
- [ ] Configuration schema documented
- [ ] Error codes documented

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI enforces the quality gates.
- The E2E compliance harness rejects non-compliant connectors.
- Mutation testing catches weak test suites.
- Fuzz testing runs on every merge to main.

title: [FCP3/P1.3] Lock transition principles and guardrails against architectural backslide
description:
Background: migration work can silently backslide if contributors keep adding host local truth, compatibility wrappers, or new direct semantic edges while the refactor is in progress. V3 needs explicit anti regression rules, not just good intentions.

Scope: define guardrails for the transition period: no new compatibility first APIs, no new broad semantic buckets, no new fwc reach through into low level meaning, no new host only truth for facts that should be durable and evidence backed, and no new runtime compatibility debt that conflicts with the target architecture.

Acceptance: future implementation work has a clear list of prohibited shortcuts and review criteria for rejecting them.

title: fcp.cron: Scheduled Task Runner
description:
# Scheduled Task Runner Meta-Connector

**Force Multiplier:** Time-based automation for FCP zones.

## Overview

Many automation workflows require scheduled execution: daily reports, periodic syncs, cleanup jobs, reminder systems. This meta-connector provides a robust scheduling infrastructure that triggers FCP actions on time-based schedules.

## Core Components

### 1. Cron Expression Scheduling
- Standard cron syntax (5-field and 6-field)
- Extended syntax with seconds precision
- Timezone-aware scheduling
- Named schedules for common patterns
- Cron expression validation and preview

```
# Standard patterns
@hourly    = 0 * * * *
@daily     = 0 0 * * *
@weekly    = 0 0 * * 0
@monthly   = 0 0 1 * *

# Custom patterns
*/15 * * * *     = Every 15 minutes
0 9 * * 1-5      = 9 AM on weekdays
0 0 1,15 * *     = 1st and 15th of month
```

### 2. One-Time Scheduled Tasks
- Schedule task for specific datetime
- Support for relative scheduling ("in 30 minutes")
- Cancellation before execution
- Rescheduling capability
- Batch scheduling (multiple one-time tasks)

### 3. Interval-Based Triggers
- Fixed interval execution (every N minutes/hours/days)
- Sliding window intervals
- Jitter support for load distribution
- Minimum interval enforcement
- Pause/resume capability

### 4. Task History and Logs
- Complete execution history
- Stdout/stderr capture
- Execution duration tracking
- Success/failure status
- Searchable log storage
- Log retention policies

### 5. Failure Alerting
- Configurable alert channels (email, Slack, PagerDuty)
- Alert on:
  - Task failure
  - Task timeout
  - Consecutive failures
  - Missed schedules
- Alert suppression/snooze
- Escalation policies

## Configuration Example

```toml
[[schedules]]
name = "daily-backup"
cron = "0 2 * * *"
timezone = "America/New_York"
action = "zone.backup.run_backup"
params = { full = true }
timeout = "1h"
alert_on_failure = true

[[schedules]]
name = "hourly-sync"
interval = "1h"
jitter = "5m"
action = "zone.sync.pull_updates"
retry_on_failure = 3

[[one_time]]
name = "migration-task"
run_at = "2024-02-01T03:00:00Z"
action = "zone.db.run_migration"
params = { version = "v2.0" }
```

## Task State Machine

```
PENDING → RUNNING → COMPLETED
              ↓
           FAILED → RETRYING → COMPLETED/FAILED
              ↓
         DEAD (max retries exceeded)
```

## Dashboard Features

- Calendar view of scheduled tasks
- Next N upcoming executions
- Recent execution history
- Live execution monitoring
- Manual trigger capability
- Bulk operations (pause all, resume all)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Sub-second scheduling precision
- [ ] Support 1000+ concurrent schedules
- [ ] Missed task detection and alerting
- [ ] Distributed execution (no single point of failure)
- [ ] Complete audit trail
- [ ] Hot-reload of schedule configurations

## Dependencies

- Persistent storage for schedules and history
- Time synchronization (NTP)
- Alert channel integrations
- Zone action invocation system

## Considerations

- Handle daylight saving time transitions
- Cluster-safe (only one instance executes)
- Graceful shutdown (complete running tasks)
- Clock skew tolerance
- Long-running task support

title: Threshold Secrets (Shamir Secret Sharing)
description:
## Overview

Implement cryptographic threshold secret sharing using Shamir's Secret Sharing Scheme (SSS) over GF(2^8) as mandated by V2 spec §17.3. This is a DISTINCT system from RaptorQ symbol distribution - secrets use real cryptographic secret sharing because RaptorQ symbols can leak structure.

## Background & Justification

**Why This Matters:**
The V2 spec explicitly states: "Secrets use real cryptographic secret sharing (Shamir), not just RaptorQ symbols. RaptorQ symbols are NOT a secret sharing scheme—a single symbol can leak structure."

Key differences from RaptorQ:
- RaptorQ symbols can leak structure (not semantically secure)
- Single RaptorQ symbol may reveal partial information
- Shamir shares reveal NOTHING until k shares collected
- Wrapped shares ensure a node cannot decrypt other nodes' shares

**Design Philosophy:**
"Secrets are never complete anywhere" - the secret is only reconstructed ephemerally during use and immediately zeroized. No single device ever stores the complete secret.

## Normative Types (V2 Spec §17.3)

### SecretObject
```rust
pub struct SecretObject {
    pub header: ObjectHeader,
    pub secret_id: SecretId,        // Unique identifier
    pub zone_id: ZoneId,            // Zone binding
    pub k: u8,                      // Threshold (need k shares)
    pub n: u8,                      // Total shares distributed
    pub scheme: SecretSharingScheme,
    pub wrapped_shares: HashMap<TailscaleNodeId, Vec<u8>>,
    pub rotation: SecretRotationPolicy,
}
```

### SecretSharingScheme
```rust
pub enum SecretSharingScheme {
    ShamirGf256,  // Shamir's Secret Sharing over GF(2^8)
}
```

### SecretRotationPolicy
```rust
pub struct SecretRotationPolicy {
    pub rotate_after_secs: u64,    // Auto-rotate interval
    pub overlap_secs: u64,         // Both old and new valid
}
```

### SecretAccessToken
```rust
pub struct SecretAccessToken {
    pub jti: Uuid,                  // Unique token ID
    pub secret_id: SecretId,        // Which secret
    pub purpose: String,            // For audit trail
    pub requested_by: PrincipalId,  // Requester identity
    pub iat: u64,                   // Issued at
    pub exp: u64,                   // Expires at (short-lived!)
    pub signature: Signature,       // Approver signature
}
```

## Implementation Requirements

### 1. Shamir Secret Sharing Implementation
- Implement Shamir SSS over GF(2^8) with constant-time operations
- Support configurable k-of-n thresholds
- Each share MUST be wrapped (encrypted) so nodes cannot decrypt other nodes' shares
- Use per-node Tailscale keys for share wrapping

### 2. SecretObject Management
- Create/store secrets with proper threshold configuration
- Distribute wrapped shares to mesh peers
- Track share locations for reconstruction
- Implement zone-scoped access control

### 3. Secret Reconstruction (Ephemeral)
```rust
impl SecretObject {
    pub async fn use_secret<F, R>(&self, access_token: &SecretAccessToken, f: F) -> Result<R>
    where F: FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R
    {
        // 1. Verify access token
        access_token.verify()?;
        
        // 2. Create audit event BEFORE reconstruction
        self.audit_secret_access(access_token).await?;
        
        // 3. Collect k wrapped shares from peers
        let shares = self.collect_k_wrapped_shares(access_token).await?;
        
        // 4. Reconstruct using Shamir
        let secret = reconstruct_shamir_secure(&shares)?;
        
        // 5. Execute closure with ephemeral secret
        let result = f(&secret);
        
        // 6. Zeroize IMMEDIATELY after use
        secure_zero(secret);
        
        Ok(result)
    }
}
```

### 4. SecretAccessToken Workflow
- Token issuance requires owner or delegated approver signature
- Tokens MUST be short-lived (minutes, not hours)
- Purpose field required for audit trail
- Verify before any secret operation

### 5. Secret Rotation
- Implement automatic rotation based on SecretRotationPolicy
- Support overlap period where both old and new secrets valid
- Coordinate rotation across mesh peers
- Maintain audit trail of rotation events

### 6. Integration with Credentials
The CredentialObject (§10.4) references secrets via SecretId:
- CredentialObject.secret_ref: Option<SecretId>
- Secret materialization requires SecretAccessToken
- Audit every secret access for credential injection

## Security Considerations

1. **Constant-time operations**: All Shamir math MUST be constant-time to prevent timing attacks
2. **Zeroization**: Use zeroize crate; secrets never persist in memory longer than closure execution
3. **Share isolation**: Wrapped shares use per-node keys; compromise of one node doesn't leak other shares
4. **Audit trail**: Every secret access creates AuditEvent BEFORE reconstruction
5. **Token validation**: SecretAccessToken signature and expiry verified before any operation

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shamir GF(2^8) implementation with constant-time polynomial evaluation
- [ ] SecretObject with k-of-n threshold configuration
- [ ] Per-node share wrapping using Tailscale node keys
- [ ] SecretAccessToken creation and validation
- [ ] Ephemeral reconstruction with immediate zeroization
- [ ] SecretRotationPolicy with overlap period support
- [ ] Integration with CredentialObject for secret-backed credentials
- [ ] Comprehensive audit events for all secret operations
- [ ] Unit tests for Shamir math, threshold edge cases, rotation
- [ ] Integration tests for multi-node secret reconstruction

## Dependencies

This feature depends on:
- Core Types (ObjectHeader, ZoneId, etc.)
- Zone Architecture (zone-scoped access)
- Capability System (for SecretAccessToken authorization)
- MeshNode (for peer share collection)
- Observability (for audit events)

title: fcp-audit: verify_chain accepts arbitrarily-future timestamps (no upper-bound sanity)
description:
## Finding
verify_chain (crates/fcp-audit/src/lib.rs:1081-1095) detects backward timestamp regressions: `if entry.occurred_at < prev.occurred_at { issues.push(... "audit.timestamp_regression" ...) }`. It accepts any forward-dated timestamp, including absurd futures (year 2096+ or u64::MAX).

## Consequences
1. **Freshness SLA poisoning.** FreshnessLevel + AuditStatus (lib.rs:1226-1302) compute freshness from the head timestamp. A single forged future-dated entry renders the chain "fresh" forever.
2. **Audit-query time-range poisoning.** Time-range filters return unexpected results.
3. **Monotonicity is preserved but meaningless.** An attacker who can inject one future entry can append arbitrarily many more with same-or-later timestamps and pass the regression check.

## Why this is a missing invariant
The current check establishes a lower bound (non-decreasing) but no upper bound. Calendar times outside a plausible window should be rejected. The verifier has no wall-clock input today.

## Recommendation
Add an optional `now_ceiling: Option<u64>` parameter (or a VerifyOptions struct) to verify_chain. When Some(now), reject entries with `occurred_at > now + clock_skew_grace` (e.g., 300 seconds). Emit "audit.timestamp_future" as a critical VerifyIssue. Leave None for offline audit replays with no wall clock.

Alternative minimum: add a static hard cap (`FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_HARD_CAP = 4_000_000_000` = year 2096) and reject anything beyond that statically. Crude but catches absurd cases.

## Evidence
- crates/fcp-audit/src/lib.rs:1081-1095 (regression check only)
- crates/fcp-audit/src/lib.rs:1226-1302 (FreshnessLevel / AuditStatus consumers)
- No future-dated-entry rejection test exists (grep of lib.rs + tests/ for "timestamp_future" / "future_timestamp" returns zero hits).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fixed in 480020af. Added MAX_FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_SECS=300 (Kerberos convention) and verify_chain_with_clock(entries, head, zone_id, now). Flags audit.timestamp_future as critical when occurred_at > now+skew. Uses saturating_add so u64::MAX is handled. Offline replays keep verify_chain. 368 lib tests pass; 4 new tests cover far-future, within-skew boundary, u64::MAX, and clean-chain agreement.

title: [IDEA-17] Schema Hash + Canonical CBOR Vector Generator
description:
## Background
Spec and docs require deterministic CBOR + schema hash vectors, but maintaining them manually is error-prone. We need a generator to keep vectors and schema hashes in sync with the authoritative definitions.

## Goals
- Generate schema hashes and canonical CBOR vectors from source schemas.
- Emit stable JSON/CBOR fixtures for conformance tests.
- Integrate with CI to detect drift.

## Non-goals
- Auto-modify spec text or accept non-canonical encodings.

## Approach
- Add a generator tool in `fcp-conformance` (CLI subcommand).
- Parse schema definitions (CDDL/JSON schema or Rust type registry).
- Compute schema hash via existing canonicalization routines.
- Write vector files with deterministic ordering.

## Risks
- Schema evolution could break determinism; add fixtures and strict ordering rules.

## Success Criteria
- Generator produces identical outputs across runs/platforms.
- CI can regenerate and diff vectors without noise.

## Acceptance Criteria (Refined)
- Regenerated vectors are byte‑for‑byte stable across two consecutive runs.
- Schema hash changes when a schema field definition changes.
- CI diff check fails on any vector drift.

Preserve machine readable user facing surfaces where they are intentionally supported, add explicit provenance and evidence handle fields so humans and scripts can see whether a claim is offline, node local, mesh backed, degraded, or fallback derived, and keep operator workflows truthful without forcing them to scrape prose. title: fcp.linear - Linear Issue Tracking Connector
description:
# fcp.linear - Linear Issue Tracking Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Provide an FCP2-compliant Linear connector for issue/project automation (and optional bidirectional Beads sync) with deterministic, idempotent, auditable behavior.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 97/100** — Critical Tier 1 connector.

**Why Critical**: Linear is the dominant issue tracker for modern engineering teams. Direct integration enables seamless human↔agent task handoff and creates the bridge between "human project management" and "agent task execution." This is the task coordination backbone.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Strategic Investment (High Value + Moderate Effort)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 1 Foundation (immediate)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,
    ConnectorArchetype::Streaming,
    ConnectorArchetype::Bidirectional
]
```
- **Operational**: GraphQL CRUD operations
- **Streaming**: Webhook event ingestion
- **Bidirectional**: If Beads↔Linear sync implemented

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Required for bidirectional sync and webhook dedupe
- State tracked: `{ sync_cursor: Option<SyncToken>, webhook_event_ids: Vec<EventId> }`
- Lease required for writer fencing during sync operations

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI recommended**: External API connector with OAuth credentials
- Memory isolation prevents token extraction
- Cross-platform consistent behavior

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    host_allow: vec\![
        "api.linear.app".into(),
        "linear.app".into(),
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
Issue tracking data handling:
```rust
// Webhook events are externally sourced
webhook_event.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT;

// Issue content may contain user-supplied data
issue_content.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// If issues contain URLs:
if issue.contains_urls {
    issue_content.provenance.taint |= TaintFlags::UNVERIFIED_LINK;
}
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `linear.issues.read` | Safe | Read-only listing |
| `linear.comments.read` | Safe | Read-only data |
| `linear.projects.read` | Safe | Read-only data |
| `linear.issues.write` | Risky | Creates/modifies work items |
| `linear.comments.write` | Risky | Public communication |
| `linear.webhooks.manage` | Dangerous | Inbound vector config |
| `linear.beads.sync` | Dangerous | Bidirectional data sync |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Issue Management
- Full issue CRUD with metadata (priority, labels, assignees)
- Comment threads and discussions
- Label and status automation
- Team workload visibility
- Sprint/cycle management

### Project & Roadmap
- Project and roadmap access
- Milestone tracking
- Team capacity planning
- Cross-project dependency tracking

### Webhook Events
- Real-time event processing for automation triggers
- Status change notifications
- Assignment alerts

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Create a Linear issue for this bug I found"
"Whats blocking the current sprint?"
"Assign this task to the frontend team"
"Update issue status when PR is merged"
"Generate weekly sprint summary"
"Auto-triage incoming issues using BV algorithms"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### BV (Beads Viewer) — Bidirectional Sync
**This is the killer feature.**
- Linear issues ↔ Beads (agent-native tasks)
- Sync status, priority, and dependencies bidirectionally
- Use BV's graph algorithms for Linear triage:
  - PageRank for issue importance
  - Critical path analysis
  - Blocker detection

### Agent Mail Integration
- Auto-assign issues based on file reservations
- Route issue updates as mail notifications
- Thread Linear comments with agent discussions

### NTM (Neural Task Manager)
- Spawn agents for Linear issues automatically
- Break down Linear epics into agent-executable subtasks
- Report progress back to Linear

### CASS (Context-Aware Semantic Search)
- Link code sessions to Linear issues
- Semantic search across issue history
- Learn from resolution patterns

### UBS (Ultimate Bug Scanner)
- Create Linear issues from UBS findings automatically
- Link bug reports to specific code locations
- Track fix status through issue lifecycle

---

## Automation Unlocks

### Auto-Triage Pipeline
```
UBS finding → Create Linear issue → BV ranks priority → Agent Mail assigns → Agent works → PR links back
```

### Implementation Plan Generation
```
Linear issue description → Agent generates implementation plan → Creates subtasks → Links to codebase
```

### Status Sync
```
Git commit → Linked issue → Update Linear status → Notify stakeholders
```

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **GraphQL API** with full query/mutation support
- **Subscription support** for real-time updates (optional)
- **Webhook handler** for event-driven automation

### Recommended Crates
- `graphql_client` or `cynic` — GraphQL client
- `reqwest` — HTTP transport
- `serde_json` — JSON handling
- `tokio` — Async runtime

### Bidirectional Beads Sync Protocol
If enabled, this is a high-risk side effect requiring:
- Explicit capability token
- OperationIntent/Receipt to avoid duplicate writes
- AuditEvents for every sync operation
- Stable reason codes on denials
- Conflict resolution strategy (last-write-wins or manual)

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:work:linear:<workspace>` | Full workspace access | All CRUD operations |
| `z:project:<name>:linear` | Project-scoped access | Issues in specific project |
| `z:work:linear:readonly` | Read-only monitoring | List/get only |

### Single-Zone Binding
- One connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId`
- Cross-workspace sync requires separate instances
- Beads sync is per-zone; cannot sync across workspaces

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — GraphQL CRUD operations
- `streaming` — Webhook/event ingestion (if enabled)
- `bidirectional` — If Beads↔Linear sync implemented

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `api.linear.app:443`
- `linear.app:443` (OAuth flows)

### Credential Injection
- API key via `CredentialId` (simpler, personal use)
- OAuth token via `CredentialId` (team/workspace access)
- Never write credentials to disk

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `linear.issues.read` — List, get, search issues
- `linear.comments.read` — Read issue comments
- `linear.projects.read` — List projects, roadmaps
- `linear.teams.read` — Team information
- `linear.users.read` — User profiles

### Write Operations
- `linear.issues.write` — Create, update, move, assign
- `linear.comments.write` — Create, update, delete comments
- `linear.projects.write` — Modify project settings
- `linear.labels.write` — Manage labels

### Dangerous Operations
- `linear.webhooks.manage` — Webhook configuration
- `linear.beads.sync` — Bidirectional Beads sync (if enabled)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Issue Operations
- `issue.create` — Create new issue
- `issue.update` — Update issue fields
- `issue.get` — Get issue by ID
- `issue.list` — List issues with filters
- `issue.search` — Full-text search
- `issue.move` — Move between projects/teams
- `issue.assign` — Assign to user
- `issue.relations` — Manage issue relationships

### Comment Operations
- `comment.create` — Add comment to issue
- `comment.update` — Edit comment
- `comment.delete` — Remove comment
- `comment.list` — List issue comments

### Project/Cycle Operations
- `project.list` — List projects
- `project.get` — Get project details
- `cycle.list` — List sprints/cycles
- `cycle.get` — Get cycle details

### Optional: Beads Sync
- `beads.sync.pull` — Import Linear issues to Beads
- `beads.sync.push` — Export Beads to Linear
- `beads.sync.bidirectional` — Full two-way sync

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- GraphQL query construction
- Response parsing
- Sync conflict resolution logic
- Rate limit handling

### Integration Tests
- wiremock-based GraphQL simulation
- Webhook event simulation
- Bidirectional sync scenarios

### E2E Compliance
- Validates default deny + NetworkConstraints
- Verifies receipts for write operations
- Confirms audit trail for sync operations

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- Deterministic tests; no live Linear calls in unit tests
- GraphQL operations work correctly
- Webhook events processed reliably (if enabled)
- Beads sync maintains data integrity (if enabled)
- All V2 NORMATIVE requirements satisfied

description:
# fcp.hubspot - HubSpot CRM & Marketing Platform Connector (FCP2)

## Success Criteria
- `flywheel_connectors-hy8v.1` (Manifest + Capability Map) is complete and passes static validation (IDs, schemas, NetworkConstraints, safety tiers).
- `flywheel_connectors-hy8v.2` (Provisioning Automation) is complete, minimizes human prompts, and is fully mockable for tests.
- `flywheel_connectors-hy8v.3` (Unit/Integration Tests) are mock-only, include success + denial paths, and assert log redaction (no secrets/PII).
- `flywheel_connectors-hy8v.4` (E2E Compliance Run) passes the shared compliance runner and emits an evidence bundle (logs + receipts + audit checks).
- Connector is V2-only: single-zone binding, default deny, constrained egress, audited risky/dangerous ops.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 87/100** — High priority Tier 2 connector (CRM family).

**Why Critical**: HubSpot is the **leading mid-market CRM and marketing platform**. Enables agents to manage sales pipelines, automate marketing, and handle customer relationships. Essential for revenue operations automation.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Strategic Investment (High Value + Revenue Operations)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 2 Productivity (weeks 5-8)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,  // CRM CRUD operations
    ConnectorArchetype::Streaming,    // Webhook events
]
```
- **Operational**: Contact/company/deal CRUD, marketing actions
- **Streaming**: Webhooks for CRM events, form submissions

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Sync cursors for incremental updates
- State tracked: `{ sync_cursors: HashMap<ObjectType, Cursor>, webhook_state: WebhookState }`
- Lease required for writer fencing

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI recommended**: Handles OAuth tokens, PII data
- Memory isolation for credential protection
- Capability-gated hostcalls

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // HubSpot API endpoints
    host_allow: vec\![
        "api.hubapi.com".into(),
        "api.hubspot.com".into(),
        "app.hubspot.com".into(),  // OAuth
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// Contact data contains PII
contact_data.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// Form submissions are external input
form_submission.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// Email content is user-generated
email_content.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED
    | TaintFlags::PROMPT_SURFACE;
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `hubspot.contacts.read` | Risky | PII data |
| `hubspot.companies.read` | Safe | Business data |
| `hubspot.deals.read` | Safe | Sales data |
| `hubspot.contacts.write` | Risky | Creates PII records |
| `hubspot.deals.write` | Risky | Modifies pipeline |
| `hubspot.email.send` | Dangerous | External communication |
| `hubspot.contacts.delete` | Dangerous | Irreversible |
| `hubspot.marketing.manage` | Dangerous | Campaign automation |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Contact & Company Management
- Create/update contacts and companies
- Association management (contacts ↔ companies ↔ deals)
- Custom property handling
- List segmentation

### Deal Pipeline
- Create and update deals
- Pipeline stage progression
- Revenue forecasting data
- Deal associations

### Marketing Automation
- Email campaign management
- Form submission handling
- Landing page data
- Marketing analytics

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Create a contact for this new lead"
"Update the deal stage to Closed Won"
"Find all contacts at this company"
"Add this lead to the nurture campaign"
"Get pipeline value for this quarter"
"Log this email to the contact record"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Stripe Integration
**Revenue operations:**
- Payment data → deal updates
- Subscription status → contact records
- Revenue attribution

### Slack/Teams Integration
- Deal notifications to sales channel
- Lead alerts
- Pipeline updates

### Agent Mail Integration
- CRM notifications → agent threads
- Customer context in conversations

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **CRM API v3**: Primary CRUD operations
- **Marketing API**: Campaigns, forms
- **Webhooks**: Event notifications

### Recommended Crates
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `serde_json` — JSON handling
- `oauth2` — Authentication

### Authentication
| Mode | Use Case |
|------|----------|
| Private App | Internal integrations |
| OAuth 2.0 | External integrations |
| API Key | Legacy (deprecated) |

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:work:hubspot:full` | Full access | All CRM + marketing |
| `z:work:hubspot:crm` | CRM only | Contacts, deals |
| `z:work:hubspot:readonly` | Read-only | Safe operations |

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — CRM CRUD
- `streaming` — Webhook events

## External Surface

Default-deny; allow only:
- `api.hubapi.com:443`
- `api.hubspot.com:443`

### Credential Injection

- Private app tokens via CredentialId

## Capability Model

### CRM Read Operations
- `hubspot.contacts.read` — Contact data (Risky/PII)

### CRM Write Operations

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real HubSpot API calls in unit tests

title: fcp.slack: Slack Workspace Integration Connector
description:
# fcp.slack - Slack Workspace Integration Connector (FCP2)

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 92/100** — Critical Tier 1 connector (Communication family).

**Why Critical**: Slack is **the dominant enterprise messaging platform**. Enables agents to participate in team conversations, automate workflows, and bridge communication across tools. Essential for enterprise agent deployments.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Strategic Investment (Communication + Automation)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 1 Foundation (immediate)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Bidirectional,  // Send + receive messages
    ConnectorArchetype::Streaming,      // Real-time events via Socket Mode
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,    // Web API actions
]
```
- **Bidirectional**: Two-way messaging in channels/DMs
- **Streaming**: Real-time event subscription (Socket Mode preferred)
- **Operational**: CRUD on channels, users, files

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Event cursor for Socket Mode or pagination state
- State tracked: `{ cursor: Option<String>, last_event_ts: Timestamp }`
- Lease required for writer fencing

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI**: Contains Dangerous operations (channel archive, DM access)
- Memory isolation for token handling
- Capability-gated hostcalls

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // Slack API endpoints
    host_allow: vec\![
        "slack.com".into(),
        "api.slack.com".into(),
        "files.slack.com".into(),
        "wss-primary.slack.com".into(),  // Socket Mode
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// All Slack messages are adversarial prompt surfaces
message.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::PROMPT_SURFACE
    | TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// URLs in messages are unverified
if message.contains_urls() {
    message.provenance.taint |= TaintFlags::UNVERIFIED_LINK;
}

// File attachments need scanning
file.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::UNVERIFIED_LINK;
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `slack.messages.read` | Safe | Read-only |
| `slack.channels.read` | Safe | Read-only listing |
| `slack.users.read` | Risky | Contains PII |
| `slack.messages.send` | Risky | Creates content |
| `slack.channels.write` | Dangerous | Org-level changes |
| `slack.files.write` | Dangerous | Data upload |
| `slack.search.read` | Dangerous | Broad data access |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Messaging Operations
- Send/update/delete messages
- React with emoji
- Reply in threads
- Schedule messages

### Channel Management
- List/create channels
- Archive/rename channels
- Set topic/purpose
- Manage membership

### User Information
- List workspace users
- Get user profiles
- Check presence status

### File Operations
- Upload/download files
- Share files in channels
- List file history

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Post a summary in #team-updates"
"Reply to this thread with the analysis"
"Create a channel for this project"
"Search for messages about the deployment"
"Upload this report to #reports"
"Notify @oncall about the incident"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Agent Mail Integration
- Slack threads ↔ Agent Mail threads
- Cross-platform notifications
- Unified conversation history

### GitHub/Linear Integration
- PR/issue notifications to channels
- Command-triggered workflows
- Status updates on commits

### Sentry/Datadog Integration
- Alerts routed to Slack
- Incident channels auto-created
- On-call notifications

### HubSpot Integration
- Deal updates in sales channels
- Customer mentions trigger CRM lookup

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **Web API**: CRUD operations
- **Socket Mode**: Real-time events (recommended)
- **Events API**: Webhook-based events (fallback)

### Recommended Crates
- `slack_morphism` — Slack API client
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `tokio-tungstenite` — WebSocket for Socket Mode
- `hmac` / `sha2` — Request signing

### Authentication Modes
| Mode | Use Case | Recommendation |
|------|----------|----------------|
| Bot Token | Standard automation | **Preferred** |
| User Token | User-delegated access | Limited use |
| App-Level Token | Socket Mode | Required for events |

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:work:slack:<workspace>` | Workspace-scoped | Full workspace access |
| `z:work:slack:readonly` | Read-only | Safe operations only |
| `z:project:<name>:slack` | Channel-scoped | Limited channels |

### Threat Model
- Slack messages are adversarial prompt surfaces
- DMs contain sensitive enterprise data
- No token/PII leakage in logs

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `bidirectional` — Send + receive messages
- `streaming` — Real-time event ingestion
- `operational` — Web API actions

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `api.slack.com:443`
- `files.slack.com:443`
- `wss-primary.slack.com:443` (Socket Mode)

### Credential Injection
- Bot token via egress proxy
- App-level token for Socket Mode
- Signing secret for Events API

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `slack.messages.read` — Read messages
- `slack.channels.read` — List channels
- `slack.users.read` — User info (PII)
- `slack.files.read` — File access

### Write Operations
- `slack.messages.send` — Post messages
- `slack.channels.write` — Create/modify channels
- `slack.files.write` — Upload files

### Admin Operations
- `slack.search.read` — Workspace-wide search (Dangerous)
- `slack.interactive.manage` — Modals/actions (Dangerous)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Post Message
```json
POST /chat.postMessage
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Hello from the agent\!",
  "thread_ts": "1234567890.123456"
}
```

### List Channels
```
GET /conversations.list?types=public_channel,private_channel
```

### Get User Info
```
GET /users.info?user=U1234567890
```

### Upload File
```
POST /files.upload
(multipart form with file + channel)
```

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- API request construction
- Response parsing
- Socket Mode event handling
- Rate limit handling
- Signing verification

### Integration Tests
- Mock Slack API responses
- Multi-step workflows
- Socket Mode connection simulation

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Dangerous operation approval flow
- Audit logging for writes

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real Slack API calls in unit tests
- Socket Mode connection functional
- All message operations work
- Channel CRUD functional
- File upload/download works
- All V2 NORMATIVE requirements satisfied

## Goal
Provide an FCP2-compliant Mailchimp connector for email marketing automation (campaigns/lists/segments) with strict capabilities and auditability.

## External surface (NetworkConstraints)
Default deny.
- Network egress MUST be restricted per-operation via manifest `NetworkConstraints` (defined in the connector’s manifest/cap map bead if present).
- Allow only the configured service host(s); HTTPS-only where applicable; deny redirects by default.
- Bound timeouts + response sizes; treat all remote responses as untrusted input; never leak secrets/PII in logs or errors.

## Manifest archetypes (closed set)

- `operational`
- `streaming`

> Interaction patterns (non-archetype): Request/Response + Webhook

## Summary
Implement FCP connector for Mailchimp Marketing API - an email marketing automation platform. This connector enables audience/list management, campaign creation, template management, automation workflows, and analytics reporting.

## Value Assessment
- **Value Score**: 59/100 (Tier 4)
- **Archetype**: Request-Response + Webhook
- **Priority**: P3

## API Integration
- **Primary API**: Mailchimp Marketing API v3
- **Base URL**: https://{dc}.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/
- **Authentication**: OAuth 2.0 (API key also supported)
- **Rate Limits**: 10 concurrent connections, varies by plan

## Operations

### Audience Management
- List/create/update/delete audiences (lists)
- Manage audience members (subscribers)
- Batch subscribe/unsubscribe operations
- Member activity and history
- Interest categories and interests
- Merge fields management

### Campaign Management
- Create/send/schedule campaigns
- Campaign content editing
- A/B testing campaigns

### Templates

- Default content blocks

### Automations
- List automation workflows
- Start/pause automations
- Automation emails and queues
- Subscriber workflow management

### Segments & Tags
- Create/manage segments
- Segment conditions and logic
- Tag management
- Batch tagging operations

### Reports & Analytics
- Campaign reports
- Open/click reports
- Subscriber activity
- E-commerce reports
- Automation reports
- Comparative reports

## Zone Architecture

### Zone 1: Audience Read (Low Risk)
- Read audience/list information
- Get subscriber data
- View segments and tags
- Access reports and analytics

### Zone 2: Campaign Management (Medium Risk)
- Create and edit campaigns
- Manage templates
- Configure automations
- Manage segments

### Zone 3: Admin (High Risk)
- Send campaigns
- Delete audiences/subscribers
- Modify automation workflows
- Batch operations

## Dependencies
- fcp-core: Core connector framework
- fcp-oauth: OAuth 2.0 authentication flow
- fcp-webhook: Real-time event notifications
- fcp-ratelimit: Rate limiting and throttling
- fcp-telemetry: Observability and metrics

## Webhook Events
- Subscribe events
- Unsubscribe events
- Profile updates

- Cleaned (bounced) emails

- Member (Subscriber)

- Automation

- Mailchimp uses data center-specific URLs (us1, us2, etc.)
- API key contains datacenter suffix (key-dc)
- Batch operations available for bulk subscriber management
- Webhook verification via secret key
- Pagination uses offset/count pattern
- Some endpoints have specific rate limits

## Testing Strategy
- Unit tests for data transformations
- Integration tests with Mailchimp sandbox
- Webhook signature verification tests
- Rate limit handling tests
