title: TEST: Capabilities Unit/Adversarial Tests (Token Verification, Grant Enforcement, Holder Proof)
description:
# TEST: Capabilities Unit/Adversarial Tests

## Goal
Prove that the capability system is airtight - no unauthorized operations can execute.

## Test Categories

### COSE_Sign1 Token Parsing
- [ ] Valid token parses and verifies
- [ ] Malformed CBOR rejected
- [ ] Invalid signature rejected
- [ ] Wrong issuer key rejected
- [ ] Missing protected headers rejected
- [ ] KID extraction and lookup works

### Token Field Validation
- [ ] Missing required fields rejected (jti, sub, iss_zone, iss_node, aud, iat, exp)
- [ ] Invalid field types rejected
- [ ] Time validation: expired token rejected
- [ ] Time validation: future iat beyond skew rejected
- [ ] aud mismatch rejected (wrong connector_id)
- [ ] aud_binary required for Risky/Dangerous - rejected if missing
- [ ] holder_node required for Risky/Dangerous - rejected if missing

### Grant Verification (grant_object_ids)
- [ ] Empty grant_object_ids rejected
- [ ] Referenced grant object not found → rejection
- [ ] Revoked grant object → rejection
- [ ] Token caps NOT subset of grant union → rejection
- [ ] Token caps IS subset of grant union → allow
- [ ] Attenuation that EXPANDS authority → rejection
- [ ] Attenuation that RESTRICTS authority → allow

### Checkpoint Freshness (chk_id/chk_seq)
- [ ] Missing chk_id/chk_seq rejected (for Risky/Dangerous)
- [ ] chk_id mismatch (wrong checkpoint) → rejection
- [ ] chk_seq > local checkpoint_seq → degraded mode or rejection per policy
- [ ] chk_seq <= local checkpoint_seq → allow

### Holder Proof Verification
- [ ] holder_node present but holder_proof missing → rejection
- [ ] holder_proof with wrong signable bytes → rejection
- [ ] holder_proof signed by wrong key → rejection
- [ ] holder_proof valid → allow
- [ ] Signable bytes include: request_id, operation_id, token.jti

### Issuer Verification
- [ ] Issuer node has valid NodeKeyAttestation → allow
- [ ] Issuer attestation expired → rejection
- [ ] Issuer attestation revoked → rejection
- [ ] Issuer not authorized for iss_zone → rejection

### Role Resolution
- [ ] RoleAssignment resolves to effective capabilities
- [ ] Role inheritance traverses DAG correctly
- [ ] Cyclic role inheritance detected and rejected
- [ ] Role attenuation restricts correctly

### Attack Scenarios (Adversarial)
- [ ] Token replay from different request_id rejected (via holder_proof)
- [ ] Token from revoked issuer rejected
- [ ] Token referencing revoked grant rejected
- [ ] Stale checkpoint attack: old token with old checkpoint accepted/rejected per policy
- [ ] Audience confusion: token for connector A used against connector B rejected
- [ ] Binary binding: token without aud_binary used for Dangerous op rejected

## Golden Vectors
- Valid token bytes with all fields → successful verification
- Each attack scenario → specific reason_code

## Fuzz Targets
- COSE_Sign1 parsing
- Grant subset verification
- Role inheritance resolution

## Logging Requirements
```json
{
  "test_name": "...",
  "token_jti": "...",
  "verification_step": "signature|grants|freshness|holder|issuer",
  "result": "pass|fail",
  "reason_code": "...",
  "evidence_ids": [...]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every verification step has both positive and negative tests
- Attack scenarios are documented and tested
- Fuzz targets find no bypasses
close_reason: Completed 82 capability tests: COSE_Sign1 parsing, token field validation, grant verification, checkpoint freshness, holder proof, issuer verification, and adversarial attack scenarios. Role resolution tests can be a follow-up.

title: [MOR/C1.5] Reduce revocation gossip propagation latency with priority gossip channel

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: WHAT: Implement priority gossip channel for revocation events. When a revocation is issued, gossip it at higher frequency (100ms vs standard 300ms gossip interval) and use direct push to known online peers in addition to epidemic gossip. WHY: F4 Failure-Mode scored revocation cache lag as RPN=240. The current gossip propagation can take 5-300 seconds depending on mesh size and connectivity. For Critical operations, this window is unacceptable — a compromised credential can be exploited for up to 5 minutes after revocation. Direct push reduces this to single round-trip time. WHERE: (1) crates/fcp-mesh/src/gossip.rs — add priority_gossip_interval for revocation events. (2) crates/fcp-mesh/src/coordinator.rs or new module — add direct_push_revocation() that sends revocation to all known online peers immediately. (3) Wire into RevocationObject creation flow. ACCEPTANCE: (1) Revocation events gossip at 100ms intervals (configurable). (2) Direct push to online peers on revocation creation. (3) Revocation propagation time reduced from 5-300s to <2s for online peers. (4) Latency benchmark: measure propagation time across 3-node and 5-node simulated meshes. (5) No amplification: direct push is bounded by peer count, not by retries. ESTIMATED EFFORT: 2-3 days. DEPENDS ON: C1.2 (exact membership) — the push delivers the exact revocation set, not XOR filter summaries.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: C1.5 done: RevocationPushMessage for direct peer push, PriorityGossipPolicy enum, priority_gossip_interval_ms (100ms) + max_revocation_push_peers (32) in GossipConfig. Uses exact ID sets. 6 tests, clippy clean. Commit 39f6488a.

title: TEST: Credential Injection Unit Tests (SecretObject, CredentialObject, Egress Injection, Zeroize)
description:
# TEST: Credential Injection Unit Tests (SecretObject, CredentialObject, Egress Injection, Zeroize)

## Goal
Prove (mechanically) that the platform’s credential model is safe and enforceable:
- secret bytes do not leak
- credential usage is capability-gated
- egress proxy injection is correct
- audits/DecisionReceipts are emitted and actionable

This bead is the test owner for `flywheel_connectors-kt9r`.

## Scope
Tests cover:
- `SecretObject` + `SecretAccessToken` semantics (authorization, reconstruction hooks, audit)
- `CredentialObject` validation + host binding
- `CapabilityConstraints.credential_allow` enforcement
- Egress proxy credential injection behavior (HTTP headers, optional TCP/TLS)

## Test Categories

### 1) CredentialObject validation (unit)
- [ ] `CredentialId` format constraints (canonical, stable)
- [ ] `CredentialApply` modes validated (HttpHeader/QueryParam) and reject invalid combinations
- [ ] Optional `host_allow` binding:
  - accept canonical hostnames only
  - reject IP literals when policy requires
  - enforce canonicalization rules consistent with NetworkConstraints

### 2) Capability gating (unit)
- [ ] Allowed: invoking capability includes `CredentialId` in `credential_allow`
- [ ] Denied: missing `credential_allow` entry -> DecisionReceipt with reason_code + evidence
- [ ] Denied: credential present but destination host not allowed by CredentialObject binding

### 3) Egress proxy injection (integration, deterministic)
- [ ] HTTP header injection:
  - proxy injects `Authorization` (or configured header) only when allowed
  - connector never sees secret bytes
- [ ] Host mismatch deny:
  - correct denial at the proxy boundary
  - structured logs include correlation_id + reason_code
- [ ] Replay/nonce safety when applicable (e.g., timestamped signatures)

### 4) SecretObject access + zeroize discipline (adversarial)
- [ ] Secret access requires a valid `SecretAccessToken`
- [ ] Every access emits `AuditEvent` `event_type="secret.access"` with redacted metadata
- [ ] Verify zeroization discipline:
  - no secret bytes in logs
  - no secret bytes in error strings
  - panic-safe zeroization paths (Drop-based)

## Golden Vectors
Location: `tests/vectors/credentials/`
- `credential_object_valid.cbor`
- `credential_object_invalid.cbor`
- `credential_allow_allow.cbor`
- `credential_allow_deny.cbor`

## Logging Requirements
- MUST use structured JSON logs per `flywheel_connectors-1n78.35`.
- MUST NOT log secret bytes; log only stable IDs (`SecretId`, `CredentialId`) and redacted metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Test suite is deterministic and runs in CI.
- Denials produce DecisionReceipts with correct reason codes and evidence.
- Secret bytes never appear in logs, errors, or artifacts.

title: fcp.twilio: Verify 2FA authentication service
description:
# fcp.twilio: Verify 2FA authentication service (FCP2)

## Goal
Expose Twilio Verify to support 2FA/verification workflows:
- send verification codes
- check verification codes

This surface is security-sensitive and must be tightly capability scoped.

## Scope
- Create a verification (send code via SMS/call/etc).
- Check a verification (validate code).
- Optional: cancel verification.

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `twilio.verify.send` (dangerous-ish: sends messages)
- `twilio.verify.check` (auth-sensitive)
- Optional: `twilio.verify.cancel`

## FCP2 requirements
- Single-zone binding.
- NetworkConstraints pinned.
- PII hygiene:
  - phone numbers are sensitive (never log)
  - verification codes are secrets (never log)
- For sends:
  - receipts/audit events include verification SID and destination hash only

## Deliverables
- Operation schemas:
  - `twilio.verify.send`
  - `twilio.verify.check`
  - Optional: `twilio.verify.cancel`
- Strict validation:
  - code length/format
  - channel allowlist

## Test strategy (MUST)
- Mock-only tests for:
  - send/check flows
  - redaction (no codes/numbers in logs)
  - error mapping (invalid code, expired, rate limited)

## Acceptance criteria
- Verify operations are mechanically authorized, safe, and do not leak secrets.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: SunnyMoose: Implemented Twilio Verify 2FA — 3 operations (send_verification, check_verification, cancel_verification). verify.twilio.com/v2 base URL, dedicated rate limit pool, golden vectors updated, 29 total ops. Commit e0eaeb53.

title: fcp.sentry: Issue assignment and status management
description:
# fcp.sentry: Issue assignment and status management (FCP2)

## Goal
Allow safe, auditable manipulation of Sentry issue workflow state:
- assign/unassign
- resolve/unresolve
- ignore/unignore
- set priority (if supported)

These are write operations that can affect on-call workflows.

## Scope
### Write operations
- `sentry.issue.assign`
- `sentry.issue.resolve`
- `sentry.issue.ignore`
- `sentry.issue.update_priority`

### Read support
- fetch minimal issue metadata required for optimistic concurrency (if available).

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `sentry.issues.write`

Policy guidance:
- Some orgs may require approvals for resolving/ignoring issues.

## FCP2 requirements
- Single-zone binding.
- NetworkConstraints pinned.
- For every write:
  - emit OperationReceipt + AuditEvent
  - include issue id + action + correlation id
  - never include raw issue payloads in logs

## Deliverables
- Operation schemas:
  - `sentry.issue.assign`
  - `sentry.issue.set_status` (resolve/ignore/unresolve)
  - `sentry.issue.set_priority`
- Denial reason codes for policy engine.

## Test strategy (MUST)
- Mock-only tests for:
  - capability gating
  - approval gating (when policy requires)
  - error mapping (permission denied, conflict)
  - audit/receipt emission

## Acceptance criteria
- Issue workflow actions are safe, explainable, and auditable.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: SunnyMoose: Implemented 3 ergonomic issue workflow operations — issue.assign (user/team), issue.set_status (resolve/ignore/unresolve + substatus), issue.set_priority (critical/high/medium/low). All reuse existing update_issue client method. 169 lib + 50 integration tests pass, clippy clean. Total 21 Sentry ops. Commit b7457553.

title: [FCP3/P4] Converge host and SDK on one execution model
description:
Background: once kernel, policy, evidence, and durable semantics exist as real owners, fcp-host and fcp-sdk must converge on one execution model. The host should orchestrate and supervise; the SDK should express the same lifecycle and semantics for connector authors; neither should redefine the platform.

Scope: refactor host into a consumer of those lower layers, publish a neutral SDK app contract, and adapt at least one connector family end to end. The phase must cover lifecycle, checkpoint, drain, health, resume, and error semantics with crate local unit tests, cross crate integration coverage, connector author ergonomics checks, and scripted end to end transcripts that include detailed structured diagnostics for both operator and connector author workflows. This phase is complete when host and SDK describe the same runtime, checkpoint, drain, health, and error semantics rather than parallel interpretations.

Acceptance: connector authors and host operators can rely on one execution vocabulary, one set of diagnostics, and reproducible test and transcript artifacts that prove the shared model in practice rather than only in architecture prose.

comments.author: CobaltHarbor
comments.text: Host convergence is the point where the platform stops being conceptually centered on fcp-host. The host remains important, but as a node local root app over shared semantics rather than the place where platform truth is invented.

title: [FCP3/P6.3] Align doctor, preflight, show, health, and explain with durable evidence bundles
description:
Background: commands like doctor, preflight, show, health, and explain should ultimately be grounded in durable evidence bundles and canonical control plane semantics, not in scattered host local heuristics.

Scope: align these operator flows with the new evidence and durable plane model so they can explain not just current availability, but why the system believes a claim, what evidence backs it, which bundle or correlation handle to inspect next, and whether the claim is offline, host local, mesh backed, degraded, or fallback derived. Require operator friendly remediation hints, concise summary paths, deep drill down paths, and detailed structured diagnostic logs so failures can be investigated without code archaeology.

Acceptance: operator diagnostics and explanations use a durable and evidence backed model rather than ad hoc host local state scraping, and they materially improve a user's ability to understand and act on system state.

title: [FCP3/P6.3] Define the shared evidence-lookup model for operator commands
description:
Background: commands like doctor, preflight, show, health, and explain cannot be evidence-backed until they share one durable lookup model for bundles, traces, and correlation handles. Right now that relationship is still too implicit.

Scope: define the evidence-bundle lookup contract for the major operator commands. Cover how commands discover bundle IDs, correlation handles, trace references, and next-step drill-down links, and keep the model consistent enough that docs and support flows can teach it once.

Acceptance: operator commands use a common evidence lookup model, and later remediation and transcript beads can rely on that model instead of inventing command-specific bundle semantics.

title: [review-pass] Fix telemetry header dedupe and SDK retry counter saturation
description:
# Why
Peer-review follow-on fixes for two concrete correctness bugs introduced or left incomplete in recent review patches.

## Findings
- `crates/fcp-telemetry/src/tracing_layer.rs`: case-insensitive header cleanup removes only one stale case-variant entry, so duplicate `traceparent`/`tracestate` variants can survive injection and later win extraction nondeterministically.
- `crates/fcp-sdk/src/retry.rs` + `crates/fcp-sdk/src/migration.rs`: unlimited retry config (`max_retries = u32::MAX`) maps to `max_attempts = None`, but the retry loop still uses a saturating `u32` attempt counter, which can repeat `operation(u32::MAX)` forever after counter saturation.

## Plan
- remove all stale case-variant tracing headers before injecting fresh context and add focused regressions
- prevent retry scheduling once the attempt counter reaches the representable limit and add focused regressions
- verify with focused `rch` runs only
close_reason: Completed: fixed telemetry context drop leak, removed all stale case-variant trace headers before injection, and stopped SDK unlimited retries at the u32 attempt ceiling

title: fcp.gmail: Google Gmail API Connector
description:
# fcp.gmail - Gmail API Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Provide an FCP2-compliant Gmail connector for email automation with strict zone isolation, sandboxing, and mechanical authorization.

## Manifest archetypes (closed set)
- `operational`
- `streaming` (optional: watch/push or polling-driven event stream)

## Zone model

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The *"zones"* described in this section are a **recommended deployment pattern** (run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies) and/or conceptual risk tiers.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

- Single-zone bound: one connector instance ↔ one `ZoneId`.
- Recommended: `z:private:gmail:<account>` (policy-owned naming).

## External surface
### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only the Gmail/Google API endpoints required by:
- Gmail API
- OAuth token refresh (if used by the OAuth library)

### Credential injection
- OAuth2 refresh/access tokens via `CredentialId`.
- Never persist tokens to disk.

## Capability model (illustrative)
- `gmail.messages.read`
- `gmail.messages.send`
- `gmail.messages.modify` (labels/trash)
- `gmail.threads.read` / `gmail.threads.modify`
- `gmail.labels.manage`
- `gmail.settings.manage` (Dangerous)

## Operations (representative)
- messages: get/list/send/reply/forward/modify/trash/delete
- threads: get/list/modify/trash
- labels: list/create/update/delete
- drafts: create/get/list/update/send/delete

## Eventing (optional)
If we support push/watch:
- connector must not expose inbound ports directly
- integrate through `fcp-host` controlled ingress (or deterministic polling)

## State model
- Stateless for simple reads.
- For incremental sync (historyId), persist cursor in connector state and advance under a singleton-writer lease.

## Tests
- Mock-only unit/integration tests with wiremock.
- Deterministic historyId/poll simulation.
- E2E compliance run validates default deny + NetworkConstraints + state/cursor behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner.
- Deterministic tests; no live Gmail calls in unit tests.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EPIC: Placeholder Implementations

Five connectors contain code that appears functional (compiles, passes tests, returns structured responses) but actually does not perform the real operation. These are dangerous because they pass CI, appear in fwc list/ops output, and would silently fail or return garbage against real provider APIs.

The core issue: a connector that declares operations, handles invoke, and returns structured JSON — but doesn't actually call the provider — looks indistinguishable from a working connector to any automated system. Only a human reading the source code would notice the 'placeholder' or 'would' comments.

Findings:
1. AWS + S3: No SigV4 request signing. Sends placeholder X-Aws-* headers. Default AWS endpoints reject all traffic.
2. GCP: Service account JWT signing returns private_key as placeholder instead of signing a JWT.
3. DocuSign: stream_events operation returns empty array with comment saying 'real implementation would poll Connect logs'.
4. LLM-Router: route_request returns routing decision metadata but never calls the actual LLM provider API.
5. S3: presigned URL generation returns a placeholder URL, not a real SigV4-signed URL.

Resolution options for each:
A) Implement the real functionality
B) Remove the operation from the connector's manifest (honest about what works)
C) Gate the operation behind a 'stub' flag that doctor/self_check reports clearly
D) Return FcpError with a clear error code instead of fake success data

The AWS SigV4 issue is the highest impact since it affects two connectors (aws, s3) and blocks all AWS operations.

title: fcp-mesh/node: zone-authorization gate silently bypassed for unknown peers and peers without populated zone state
description:
**File**: crates/fcp-mesh/src/node.rs:1339-1347 (verify_summary_signature) and 1383-1391 (verify_revocation_push_signature)

**Code**:
```rust
// Enforce zone authorization (C2)
if let Some(state) = self.peers.get(&peer) {
    if !state.zones.is_empty() && !state.zones.contains(&summary.zone_id) {
        return Err(MeshNodeError::UnauthorizedZone { ... });
    }
}
```

**Lens**: cross-agent coordination + adversarial inputs.

**Root cause**: The zone-authorization gate has TWO bypass conditions, both silent:
1. `self.peers.get(&peer)` returns `None` (peer is not yet in our peer map)
2. `state.zones.is_empty()` (peer is known but their zone set hasn't been populated)

In both cases, the function falls through to `Ok(peer)`, accepting the summary/push for any zone the message claims.

**Why this is reachable in production**:

1. *Unknown-peer bootstrap*: First contact with a peer goes through this path. The signature is verified (good — proves they hold the signing key) but ANY zone claim is accepted. So a peer who is authorized only for `z:public` can ship their first message claiming `z:private`, and the message is processed.

2. *Empty-zone state*: Bead **flywheel_connectors-fqzmp** documents that `PeerState.zones` is never populated in production (the wiring is missing — `local_zones` field doesn't exist on MeshNode, peer zones aren't derived from MeshIdentity tags). So even for peers in `self.peers`, `state.zones.is_empty()` is `true`, bypassing the gate. **Until fqzmp is fixed, the zone gate is universally bypassed for every peer in every direction.**

3. *Self-perpetuating bypass*: A peer's zone set in our map gets populated by... gossip messages that we received from them. But those messages get processed (and their zone claims trusted) BEFORE the zone state gets populated. There is no out-of-band zone-membership channel. So the bootstrap is TOFU (trust on first use) — but TOFU on a per-message basis: each new `zone_id` claimed by a peer is implicitly trusted on first sight.

**Concrete adversarial scenario**:

Setup:
- Peer P holds a valid signing key (let's say it was attested by the owner for tag:fcp-public, mapping to z:public)
- Honest node N's peer map contains P with zones = {z:public}
- Bug fqzmp gets fixed first; assume P.zones is correctly populated

Attack:
1. P sends a GossipSummary claiming `zone_id = z:private`, signed correctly with P's key
2. N's verify_summary_signature: signature.node_id matches summary.from ✓, signature verifies ✓
3. N looks up P in self.peers → state.zones = {z:public}, not empty
4. `state.zones.contains(&z:private)` → false → `Err(UnauthorizedZone)` ✓

Now bug variant:
1. Same setup but P is a NEW peer not yet in self.peers (e.g., we just restarted, or P just joined)
2. P sends a GossipSummary claiming `zone_id = z:private`
3. N's verify_summary_signature: signature checks pass
4. `self.peers.get(&peer)` returns None
5. The whole zone-check block is skipped — Ok(peer)
6. N processes the summary as if P is authorized for z:private

**Spec violation**: The comment "// Enforce zone authorization (C2)" claims a hard zone gate. The implementation silently bypasses for the common case of unknown peers. The C2 requirement (per the recent C2.x epic) should be "a peer cannot transmit messages tagged for a zone they're not attested into." The current implementation is "a peer cannot transmit messages tagged for a zone we already know they're not attested into" — much weaker.

**Fix plan**:

1. **Reject unknown peers entirely** — change `if let Some(state) = ...` to `let state = self.peers.get(&peer).ok_or(MeshNodeError::UnknownPeer { ... })?;`. Bootstrap MUST happen out-of-band (handshake / attestation flow) before any gossip is accepted.

2. **Reject empty zone sets** as malformed peer state — change `if !state.zones.is_empty() && ...` to `if !state.zones.contains(&summary.zone_id) { Err(...) }` (no empty-zone fallthrough). An authenticated peer with no known zones is not allowed to claim ANY zone.

3. **Apply the same two fixes to verify_revocation_push_signature** (node.rs:1383-1391).

4. **Regression tests**:
   - new peer + signed summary for any zone → MUST be rejected with UnknownPeer
   - known peer + empty zone state + signed summary → MUST be rejected with UnauthorizedZone
   - known peer + populated zones + summary for unauthorized zone → already covered by tests but verify

5. **Document the bootstrap order**: "PeerState (with zones) MUST be populated via the attested handshake flow BEFORE any gossip from that peer is accepted." Block on fqzmp landing first; without that, even fix (2) would reject every peer (because their state.zones is always empty).

**Severity**: MEDIUM-HIGH. Requires a peer with a valid signing key to exploit (so not internet-wide), but the FCP3 trust model is multi-tenant within a mesh — peers authorized for low-sensitivity zones SHOULD NOT be able to read/write high-sensitivity zones via gossip. This bypass defeats that boundary.

title: fcp.homeassistant
description:
# fcp.homeassistant - Home Automation Platform Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Deliver the FCP2 Home Assistant connector epic plan for safe smart-home automation with strict zone-based safety gating and auditable actuation.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 74/100** — Specialized Tier 3 connector (IoT/Home Automation family).

**Why Critical**: Home Assistant is the **leading open-source home automation platform**, with 500K+ active installations. Enables agents to control smart home devices, automate routines, and integrate physical world with digital workflows. Unique capability for personal productivity agents.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Specialized Investment (IoT + Personal Automation)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 4 Advanced (weeks 13+)

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Device Control
- Turn devices on/off
- Adjust settings (brightness, temperature)
- Trigger scenes
- Lock/unlock doors

### State Monitoring
- Read sensor values
- Track device states
- Monitor energy usage
- Get climate data

### Automation Management
- Trigger automations
- Enable/disable automations
- Read automation history
- Manage schedules

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Turn off all lights in the house"
"What's the temperature in the living room?"
"Set the thermostat to 72°F"
"Lock the front door"
"Start the 'Movie Time' scene"
"Is the garage door closed?"
"Turn on office lights at 9am"
"Alert me if motion detected while away"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Calendar Integration
**Time-aware automation:**
- Calendar events → home state changes
- "Meeting mode" activations
- Presence-based scheduling

### Agent Mail Integration
- Home alerts → agent notifications
- Coordinate with family members
- Security event escalation

### Twilio Integration
- SMS alerts for security events
- Voice notifications
- Emergency contact automation

### Weather API Integration
- Weather-based automations
- Climate control optimization
- Energy efficiency

### Spotify Integration
- Music as part of scenes
- Voice-controlled playback
- Mood-based automation

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **REST API** — Full device control
- **WebSocket API** — Real-time state updates
- **Long-lived Access Tokens** — Authentication

### Recommended Crates
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `tokio-tungstenite` — WebSocket client
- `serde_json` — JSON handling

### Entity Model
```
Domain.entity_id = service target
Examples:
  light.living_room
  switch.coffee_maker
  climate.thermostat
  lock.front_door
  sensor.temperature
  binary_sensor.motion
```

### Service Calls
```json
POST /api/services/{domain}/{service}
{
  "entity_id": "light.living_room",
  "brightness": 255,
  "color_temp": 400
}
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:home:ha:full` | Full access | All devices and services |
| `z:home:ha:readonly` | Read-only | State monitoring only |
| `z:home:ha:lights` | Lights only | Light control |
| `z:home:ha:climate` | Climate only | Thermostat control |
| `z:home:ha:security` | Security | Locks, alarms, cameras |

### Safety Tiers
- **Lights/Media**: Low risk — comfort only
- **Climate**: Medium risk — affects comfort/cost
- **Locks/Security**: High risk — physical safety
- **Garage/Entry**: Very high risk — security critical

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — REST API operations
- `streaming` — WebSocket state subscriptions

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Self-hosted platform:
- Local: `homeassistant.local:8123` or IP
- Remote: Nabu Casa (*.ui.nabu.casa:443)

### Credential Injection
- Long-lived access token via `CredentialId`
- Never write credentials to disk

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `ha.states.read` — Get entity states
- `ha.history.read` — Historical data
- `ha.config.read` — Configuration info
- `ha.automations.read` — Automation list

### Write Operations
- `ha.services.call` — Call any service
- `ha.lights.control` — Light operations
- `ha.climate.control` — Thermostat control
- `ha.switches.control` — Switch operations
- `ha.scenes.activate` — Trigger scenes

### Security Operations (Dangerous)
- `ha.locks.control` — Lock/unlock
- `ha.covers.control` — Garage doors, blinds
- `ha.alarms.control` — Arm/disarm

### Administrative (Dangerous)
- `ha.automations.manage` — Enable/disable automations
- `ha.scripts.execute` — Run scripts

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Get All States
```json
GET /api/states
```

Response:
```json
[{
  "entity_id": "light.living_room",
  "state": "on",
  "attributes": {
    "brightness": 200,
    "color_temp": 400,
    "friendly_name": "Living Room Light"
  },
  "last_changed": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}]
```

### Get Single Entity State
```json
GET /api/states/{entity_id}
```

### Call Service
```json
POST /api/services/light/turn_on
{
  "entity_id": "light.living_room",
  "brightness_pct": 75,
  "transition": 2
}
```

### Common Services
| Domain | Service | Effect |
|--------|---------|--------|
| light | turn_on/turn_off | Light control |
| switch | turn_on/turn_off | Switch control |
| climate | set_temperature | Thermostat |
| lock | lock/unlock | Door locks |
| scene | turn_on | Activate scene |
| automation | trigger | Run automation |

### WebSocket Subscription
```json
{"type": "subscribe_events", "event_type": "state_changed"}
```

---

## Safety Considerations

### Physical Safety
- Lock/security operations require confirmation
- Emergency contacts for critical alerts
- Fail-safe defaults for security devices

### Privacy
- Camera feeds are highly sensitive
- Motion data reveals presence patterns
- Energy data reveals behavior

### Rate Limiting
- Local API generally unlimited
- Don't spam device commands
- Respect device response times

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- Service call construction
- State parsing
- Entity ID validation
- WebSocket message handling

### Integration Tests
- Mock Home Assistant server
- State change scenarios
- Service call verification

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Security operation logging
- Audit trail for all commands

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real HA calls in unit tests
- State reading works
- Service calls functional
- WebSocket subscription works
- Security operations require confirmation
- Proper entity ID validation

## Success Criteria
- Connector epic is fully decomposed into implementable beads (manifest/cap map, provisioning, operations, tests, E2E compliance).
- All child beads are implemented and closed, and the connector passes the mechanical compliance runner + its E2E scenarios with structured JSON logs.
- Mechanical guarantees hold: single-zone binding, default-deny capabilities, and NetworkConstraints enforcement; no secret/PII leakage in logs.

title: fcp.twilio: Communication Infrastructure Connector (SMS, Voice, WhatsApp)
description:
# fcp.twilio - Communication Infrastructure Connector (FCP2)

## Success Criteria
- `flywheel_connectors-otqy.1` (Manifest + Capability Map) is complete and passes static validation (IDs, schemas, NetworkConstraints, safety tiers).
- `flywheel_connectors-otqy.2` (Provisioning Automation) is complete, minimizes human prompts, and is fully mockable for tests.
- `flywheel_connectors-otqy.3` (Unit/Integration Tests) are mock-only, include success + denial paths, and assert log redaction (no secrets/PII).
- `flywheel_connectors-otqy.4` (E2E Compliance Run) passes the shared compliance runner and emits an evidence bundle (logs + receipts + audit checks).
- Connector is V2-only: single-zone binding, default deny, constrained egress, audited risky/dangerous ops.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 88/100** — High priority Tier 2 connector.

**Why Critical**: Twilio is the **dominant programmable communications platform**. Enables agents to communicate via SMS, voice calls, and WhatsApp — essential for customer-facing automation, alerting, and multi-channel engagement workflows.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Strategic Investment (High Value + Communication Infrastructure)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 2 Productivity (weeks 5-8)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Bidirectional,  // Send/receive messages
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,    // Call initiation, config
    ConnectorArchetype::Streaming,      // Webhook events
]
```
- **Bidirectional**: SMS/WhatsApp send and receive
- **Operational**: Voice calls, TwiML, phone numbers
- **Streaming**: Webhooks for delivery status, inbound messages

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Message delivery tracking, call state
- State tracked: `{ pending_messages: HashMap<MessageSid, Status>, call_state: HashMap<CallSid, CallState> }`
- Lease required for writer fencing

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI recommended**: Handles API credentials, PII (phone numbers)
- Memory isolation for credential protection
- Capability-gated hostcalls

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // Twilio API endpoints
    host_allow: vec\![
        "api.twilio.com".into(),
        "verify.twilio.com".into(),
        "lookups.twilio.com".into(),
        // Media URLs for MMS
        "api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/*/Messages/*/Media/*".into(),
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// Inbound messages are external/adversarial
inbound_message.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::PROMPT_SURFACE
    | TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// Phone numbers are PII - handle carefully
phone_number.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// Outbound content may contain user data
outbound_message.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `twilio.messages.read` | Risky | Contains PII |
| `twilio.calls.read` | Risky | Call history |
| `twilio.lookups.phone` | Risky | Phone number info |
| `twilio.messages.send` | Dangerous | External communication |
| `twilio.calls.initiate` | Dangerous | Real-world call |
| `twilio.verify.send` | Dangerous | Sends verification |
| `twilio.numbers.purchase` | Dangerous | Financial transaction |
| `twilio.numbers.release` | Dangerous | Releases resource |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### SMS Operations
- Send individual and bulk SMS messages
- Receive and process inbound SMS
- MMS with media attachments
- Short code and toll-free support

### Voice Calls
- Initiate outbound calls
- TwiML for call flow control
- Conference calling
- Call recording and transcription

### WhatsApp Business
- Send template messages
- Handle conversations
- Media messages

### Verification
- Send verification codes
- Phone number validation
- 2FA support

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Send an SMS alert to the on-call engineer"
"Notify customers about their order status"
"Initiate a call to this number"
"Verify this phone number"
"Send a WhatsApp message with the invoice"
"Check delivery status of sent messages"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Stripe Integration
**Payment notifications:**
- SMS receipts
- Payment failure alerts
- Subscription reminders

### Sentry/Datadog Integration
- Alert escalation via SMS/call
- On-call notifications
- Incident updates

### Agent Mail Integration
- SMS threads → agent mail
- Voice transcripts
- Delivery confirmations

### HubSpot Integration
- Customer communication tracking
- Contact engagement

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **REST API**: Primary interface
- **TwiML**: Voice call scripting
- **Webhooks**: Event delivery

### Recommended Crates
- `twilio-rs` — Twilio API client
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `hmac` / `sha1` — Webhook validation

### Authentication
```rust
// Basic auth with Account SID and Auth Token
Authorization: Basic {base64(account_sid:auth_token)}
```

### Rate Limits
```rust
RateLimits {
    sms_per_second: 1,      // Per phone number
    mps_rate: 400,          // High-throughput
    api_requests: 100,      // Per second
}
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:comm:twilio:full` | Full access | All operations |
| `z:comm:twilio:sms` | SMS only | Message send/receive |
| `z:comm:twilio:voice` | Voice only | Call operations |
| `z:comm:twilio:readonly` | Read-only | Status checks |

### Security Considerations
- Phone numbers are PII
- Never log full phone numbers
- Message content is sensitive
- Audit all sends

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `bidirectional` — SMS/WhatsApp send/receive
- `operational` — Voice calls, configuration
- `streaming` — Webhook events

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `api.twilio.com:443`
- `verify.twilio.com:443`
- `lookups.twilio.com:443`

### Credential Injection
- Account SID + Auth Token via egress proxy
- API keys for limited access
- Webhook validation secret

---

## Capability Model

### Messaging Operations
- `twilio.messages.send` — Send SMS/MMS (Dangerous)
- `twilio.messages.read` — Get message status (Risky)
- `twilio.whatsapp.send` — Send WhatsApp (Dangerous)

### Voice Operations
- `twilio.calls.initiate` — Start call (Dangerous)
- `twilio.calls.read` — Call status (Risky)
- `twilio.calls.update` — Modify call

### Verification Operations
- `twilio.verify.send` — Send code (Dangerous)
- `twilio.verify.check` — Verify code
- `twilio.lookups.phone` — Phone lookup (Risky)

### Admin Operations
- `twilio.numbers.purchase` — Buy number (Dangerous)
- `twilio.numbers.release` — Release number (Dangerous)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Send SMS
```json
POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages
{
  "To": "+1234567890",
  "From": "+0987654321",
  "Body": "Your order has shipped\!"
}
```

### Initiate Call
```json
POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Calls
{
  "To": "+1234567890",
  "From": "+0987654321",
  "Url": "https://example.com/twiml/welcome"
}
```

### Send Verification
```json
POST /v2/Services/{ServiceSid}/Verifications
{
  "To": "+1234567890",
  "Channel": "sms"
}
```

---

## Log Redaction (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// NEVER log full phone numbers
log_phone("+1234567890") → "+1***890"

// NEVER log message content in full
log_message("Hello world") → "Hello ***"

// NEVER log auth tokens
log_token("SK123...") → "SK***"
```

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- Request construction
- Response parsing
- Webhook signature validation
- Phone number formatting

### Integration Tests
- Mock Twilio API responses
- Multi-channel workflows
- Error handling

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Dangerous operation approval flow
- Log redaction verification
- Audit logging

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real Twilio API calls in unit tests
- SMS send/receive works
- Voice call initiation works
- Webhook handling functional
- Phone number redaction in logs
- All V2 NORMATIVE requirements satisfied

title: [MOR/C3.5] Change default simulate() to deny; fix default-deny violation

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: WHAT: Change the default implementation of simulate() in the FcpConnector trait from returning SimulateResponse::allowed(req.id) to returning SimulateResponse::denied(req.id, reason: operation_not_simulated). WHY: J1 Deontic found this is a DIRECT VIOLATION of the default-deny principle. A connector that does not override simulate() currently implicitly claims ALL operations are allowed. This means a new connector scaffold that ships without implementing simulate() silently tells the system it can handle anything. The correct default is: deny everything the connector has not explicitly declared it can simulate. WHERE: crates/fcp-core/src/connector.rs or crates/fcp-sdk/src/lib.rs — the default impl of simulate() in the FcpConnector trait. Also update fwc new_cmd.rs scaffold template to include a simulate() override with proper operation matching. ACCEPTANCE: (1) Default simulate() returns denied. (2) Existing connectors that rely on default must be updated (or explicitly override with allowed for their operations). (3) fwc new scaffold includes simulate() override template. (4) At least 3 tests: default returns denied, override returns allowed, denied includes reason code. ESTIMATED EFFORT: 1 day for the default change + 0.5 day per connector that needs updating. Quick audit needed: how many connectors rely on the default simulate()? DESIGN NOTE: This is a one-line change with outsized security impact. It converts simulate() from opt-out safety (dangerous default) to opt-in safety (safe default). Any connector that was relying on the old default was ALREADY WRONG — it was claiming support for operations it had not validated.

Scaffold template in new_cmd.rs:2126 has full simulate() override with operation validation, state checks, and capability verification. protocol.rs has 3+ SimulateResponse tests (allowed, denied with reason/code, with_cost). 44 connectors override simulate() explicitly; remaining ~46 correctly use default-deny. All acceptance criteria met.

description:
# FCP Anthropic Connector - Anthropic AI Provider (LEGACY / SUPERSEDED)

> NOTE (2026-01-15): This bead predates the current **FCP2 connector model** and is kept only for historical context of an earlier prototype.
> 
> The active, FCP2-compliant Anthropic plan is: `flywheel_connectors-lszk.4` (and its child beads). Use that as the source of truth.

## Overview
A comprehensive connector for Anthropic's Claude API, enabling agents to leverage Claude models for complex reasoning, tool use, vision capabilities, and batch processing with built-in usage tracking and budget enforcement.

## Priority: P1 (Critical Infrastructure)

## Core Capabilities

### 1. Messages API
- Send messages to Claude models
- Streaming responses for real-time output
- Multi-turn conversations
- System prompts
- Model selection (claude-opus-4-5-20251101, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-haiku, etc.)
- Temperature and sampling controls
- Max tokens configuration
- Stop sequences

### 2. Tool Use Support
- Define tools with JSON schema
- Handle tool_use responses
- Execute tools and return results
- Multi-tool conversations
- Parallel tool execution
- Tool choice forcing (auto, any, specific)

### 3. Vision Capabilities
- Images in prompts (base64 or URL)
- Multiple images per message
- Image analysis and description
- Document/screenshot understanding
- Chart and diagram interpretation

### 4. Prompt Caching
- Cache system prompts
- Cache large context documents
- Cache tool definitions
- Automatic cache management
- Cache hit/miss tracking
- Usage/cost savings can be computed from tracked usage deltas

### 5. Batch API
- Submit batch requests
- Track batch status
- Retrieve batch results
- Cancel batches
- Batch pricing can change; treat billing as provider- or policy-owned (do not hardcode discounts)

### 6. Usage Tracking & Budget Enforcement
- Per-request usage calculation (tokens, images, audio seconds, etc.)
- Running total tracking
- Budget limits per agent/session/day
- Alerts at thresholds
- Automatic cutoff at budget limit
- Usage attribution and reporting

## FCP Integration

### Manifest Structure
```toml
[connector]
name = "fcp.anthropic"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Anthropic Claude API integration with usage tracking"

[capabilities]
messages = { risk = "medium", description = "Send messages to Claude" }
streaming = { risk = "medium", description = "Stream responses" }
tool_use = { risk = "medium", description = "Use tools in conversations" }
vision = { risk = "medium", description = "Process images" }
batch = { risk = "low", description = "Submit batch requests" }

[trust_zones]
default = "z:ai:inference"

[resources]
rate_limit_rpm = 1000
rate_limit_tpm = 100000
default_timeout_ms = 120000

[billing]
track_costs = true
budget_enforcement = true
```

### Tool Definitions
```yaml
tools:
  - name: anthropic_message
    description: Send a message to Claude
    parameters:
      model:
        type: string
        enum: [claude-opus-4-5-20251101, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022]
        required: true
      messages:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          properties:
            role: { type: string, enum: [user, assistant] }
            content: { type: string }
        required: true
      system: { type: string }
      max_tokens: { type: integer, default: 4096 }
      temperature: { type: number, default: 1.0, min: 0, max: 1 }
      stream: { type: boolean, default: false }

  - name: anthropic_message_with_tools
    description: Send a message with tool definitions
    parameters:
      model: { type: string, required: true }
      messages: { type: array, required: true }
      tools:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          properties:
            name: { type: string }
            description: { type: string }
            input_schema: { type: object }
      tool_choice:
        type: object
        properties:
          type: { type: string, enum: [auto, any, tool] }
          name: { type: string }

  - name: anthropic_message_with_vision
    description: Send a message with images
    parameters:
      model: { type: string, required: true }
      messages:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          properties:
            role: { type: string }
            content:
              type: array
              items:
                oneOf:
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      type: { const: text }
                      text: { type: string }
                  - type: object
                    properties:
                      type: { const: image }
                      source:
                        type: object
                        properties:
                          type: { enum: [base64, url] }
                          media_type: { type: string }
                          data: { type: string }

  - name: anthropic_batch_create
    description: Create a batch request
    parameters:
      requests:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          properties:
            custom_id: { type: string }
            params: { type: object }
        required: true

  - name: anthropic_batch_status
    description: Get batch status
    parameters:
      batch_id: { type: string, required: true }

  - name: anthropic_batch_results
    description: Get batch results
    parameters:
      batch_id: { type: string, required: true }

  - name: anthropic_get_usage
    description: Get current usage metrics (currency cost is policy/ops-owned)
    parameters:
      period: { type: string, enum: [session, day, month] }
```

## Usage / Cost Tracking (NO hard-coded pricing)

### Why we do NOT embed pricing tables
Provider pricing changes frequently. Hard-coding a “pricing model” table in a connector/spec becomes incorrect quickly.

### What we track instead (stable)
- provider-reported usage fields (when present)
- token counts (input/output/cache)
- image counts/size classes
- audio seconds

### Budget enforcement
Budgets can be enforced in two stable ways:
1. **Usage budgets** (preferred): token/image/second limits per request/session/day.
2. **Currency budgets** (optional): computed by an external, versioned “pricing catalog” object owned by policy/ops (not embedded in the connector).

### Attribution
- Track usage per agent
- Track usage per task/session
- Track usage per operation/tool
- Generate reports

## Prompt Caching Strategy
- System prompts > 1024 tokens: Always cache
- Tool definitions: Cache when > 5 tools
- Large documents: Cache with TTL
- Cache warming on connector init

## Error Handling
- Rate limit (429): Exponential backoff
- Overloaded (529): Queue and retry
- Invalid request (400): Parse and report
- Auth failure (401): Refresh credentials
- Context length exceeded: Truncation strategy

## Dependencies
- anthropic-rs or custom HTTP client
- reqwest (HTTP)
- tokio (async)
- serde (serialization)
- async-stream (streaming)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Send basic message and receive response
- [ ] Stream response tokens in real-time
- [ ] Use tools in conversation
- [ ] Process images in prompts
- [ ] Submit and retrieve batch jobs
- [ ] Track usage accurately per request
- [ ] Enforce budget limits
- [ ] Handle rate limits gracefully
- [ ] Utilize prompt caching

title: fcp.zendesk - Zendesk Support Connector
description:
# fcp.zendesk - Zendesk Support Platform Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Deliver the FCP2 Zendesk connector epic plan for tickets/comments/KB workflows with careful PII handling and audit for writes.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 77/100** — Specialized Tier 3 connector (Support/CRM family).

**Why Critical**: Zendesk is a **leading customer support platform**, used by 100K+ companies. Enables agents to manage support tickets, automate responses, analyze customer issues, and improve support efficiency. Essential for customer success automation.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Specialized Investment (Support + Customer Success)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 3 Enterprise (weeks 9-12)

### Intercom Comparison
- **Zendesk**: Traditional ticketing, enterprise support
- **Intercom**: Modern messaging, product-led
- Different market segments — both valuable

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Ticket Management
- Create and update tickets
- Assign and prioritize
- Add internal notes
- Merge duplicate tickets

### Customer Interaction
- Send replies
- Read ticket history
- Access user information
- Track satisfaction

### Support Operations
- Categorize and tag
- Apply macros
- Set SLA status
- Route to teams

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"What are the open P1 tickets?"
"Reply to this support request"
"Assign this ticket to the billing team"
"Find similar tickets to this issue"
"What's our average response time today?"
"Escalate this to engineering"
"Generate weekly support report"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Sentry Integration
**Bug-to-ticket correlation:**
- Sentry error → Zendesk ticket
- Link customer reports to errors
- Track fix status bidirectionally

### HubSpot/Salesforce Integration
- Support context for sales
- Customer health scores
- Upsell opportunity identification

### Linear/Jira Integration
- Feature requests → backlog items
- Bug reports → engineering issues
- Status sync between systems

### Agent Mail Integration
- Support threads → agent coordination
- Internal escalation workflows
- Cross-team collaboration

### Slack/Teams Integration
- Support alerts in channels
- Quick internal discussions
- Agent assistance requests

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **Support API** — Tickets, users, organizations
- **Help Center API** — Knowledge base articles
- **Search API** — Full-text search
- **Webhooks** — Real-time ticket events

### Recommended Crates
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `serde_json` — JSON handling
- `oauth2` — OAuth handling

### Authentication
- API token (email/token pair)
- OAuth 2.0 (for apps)
- Basic auth (legacy)

### Data Model
```
Organization
└── User
    └── Ticket
        ├── Comments (public/private)
        ├── Tags
        └── Custom Fields
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:support:zendesk:full` | Full access | All operations |
| `z:support:zendesk:agent` | Agent access | Handle tickets |
| `z:support:zendesk:readonly` | Read-only | View and search |
| `z:support:zendesk:group:<id>` | Group-scoped | Single team |

### Data Sensitivity
- Tickets may contain customer PII
- Internal notes are confidential
- Customer issues reveal product problems

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — REST API operations
- `streaming` — Webhook event ingestion

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `{subdomain}.zendesk.com:443`

### Credential Injection
- API token via `CredentialId`
- OAuth tokens via `CredentialId`
- Never write credentials to disk

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `zendesk.tickets.read` — View tickets
- `zendesk.tickets.search` — Search tickets
- `zendesk.users.read` — User information
- `zendesk.organizations.read` — Organization info

### Write Operations
- `zendesk.tickets.create` — Create tickets
- `zendesk.tickets.update` — Update tickets
- `zendesk.tickets.comment` — Add comments
- `zendesk.tickets.assign` — Assign tickets

### Administrative (Dangerous)
- `zendesk.tickets.delete` — Delete tickets
- `zendesk.users.admin` — User management

---

## Operations (Representative)

### List Tickets
```json
GET /api/v2/tickets.json
Query params:
  sort_by: updated_at
  sort_order: desc
```

### Search Tickets
```json
GET /api/v2/search.json
Query params:
  query: status<solved type:ticket priority:urgent
```

### Get Ticket
```json
GET /api/v2/tickets/{id}.json
```

Response:
```json
{
  "ticket": {
    "id": 123,
    "subject": "Help with billing",
    "description": "...",
    "status": "open",
    "priority": "high",
    "requester_id": 456,
    "assignee_id": 789,
    "tags": ["billing", "subscription"]
  }
}
```

### Create Ticket
```json
POST /api/v2/tickets.json
{
  "ticket": {
    "subject": "Issue with login",
    "comment": {"body": "Customer cannot access their account..."},
    "priority": "high",
    "requester_id": 456
  }
}
```

### Update Ticket (Add Comment)
```json
PUT /api/v2/tickets/{id}.json
{
  "ticket": {
    "status": "pending",
    "comment": {
      "body": "We're investigating this issue.",
      "public": true
    }
  }
}
```

### Add Internal Note
```json
PUT /api/v2/tickets/{id}.json
{
  "ticket": {
    "comment": {
      "body": "Escalated to engineering team.",
      "public": false
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Support Automation Patterns

### Auto-Triage
1. New ticket arrives
2. Agent analyzes content
3. Assigns priority and category
4. Routes to appropriate team
5. Sends initial acknowledgment

### Knowledge Base Deflection
1. Analyze ticket content
2. Search help center articles
3. Suggest relevant articles
4. Auto-respond if high confidence
5. Escalate if no match

### SLA Monitoring
1. Track response/resolution times
2. Alert on approaching breaches
3. Escalate stale tickets
4. Generate SLA reports

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- Ticket construction
- Search query building
- Comment formatting
- Status transitions

### Integration Tests
- wiremock-based API simulation
- Multi-ticket workflows
- Webhook handling

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Permission enforcement
- Audit logging

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real Zendesk calls in unit tests
- Ticket CRUD functional
- Search works
- Comment operations work
- Webhook events processed
- Status transitions handled

## Success Criteria
- Connector epic is fully decomposed into implementable beads (manifest/cap map, provisioning, operations, tests, E2E compliance).
- All child beads are implemented and closed, and the connector passes the mechanical compliance runner + its E2E scenarios with structured JSON logs.
- Mechanical guarantees hold: single-zone binding, default-deny capabilities, and NetworkConstraints enforcement; no secret/PII leakage in logs.

title: fcp-kubernetes: const fn str matches break fcp-e2e package test builds
description:
**File**: connectors/kubernetes/src/connector.rs:1424-1465, 2964-2985

**Symptom**: The user-requested verification command `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/fcp-p3-r1 rch exec -- cargo test -p fcp-conformance -p fcp-e2e` fails before reaching the touched tests because `fcp-e2e` pulls `fcp-kubernetes` as a dev-dependency and `fcp-kubernetes` no longer compiles on the current nightly.

**Compiler errors**:
```
error[E0658]: cannot match on `str` in constant functions
  --> connectors/kubernetes/src/connector.rs:1424:9
error: `PartialEq` is not yet stable as a const trait
  --> connectors/kubernetes/src/connector.rs:1424:9
...
error: could not compile `fcp-kubernetes` (lib) due to 102 previous errors
```

**Root cause**: multiple `const fn` bodies use `matches!` over `&str` literals. On the current toolchain, `str` equality inside `const fn` still requires unstable const-trait support, so these match expressions are rejected.

**Why it matters**: unrelated `fcp-e2e` verification lanes are blocked by a connector compile failure outside their test target.

**Fix plan**: replace the `matches!`-based string switches in those `const fn` helpers with non-const helpers, or rewrite them to avoid `&str` pattern matching in `const fn` entirely. Then add a focused compile/test lane that exercises `fcp-kubernetes` from the `fcp-e2e` package boundary so this regression is caught earlier.
close_reason: 491b8ad3 regression-guard comments on is_secret_mutation/is_system_namespace/is_shell_binary/approval_for_operation. Const-fn str-match regression already fixed in f8712801; audit confirmed all four helpers non-const, fcp-kubernetes builds clean, 514/514 lib tests pass. fcp-e2e has separate unrelated breakage (CapabilityToken ref/owned mismatch).

Verified: cargo build -p fcp-kubernetes clean; cargo test -p fcp-kubernetes --lib 514/514 pass; cargo build -p fcp-e2e --tests compiles clean. Unblocks P4 + fcp-e2e verification lanes.

title: TEST: Trust/Quorum Model Unit Tests (n/f Assumptions, Threshold Rules, Degraded Mode)
description:
# TEST: Trust/Quorum Model Unit Tests


## Goal
Validate trust/quorum and degraded-mode policy rules so the mesh behaves predictably under partial failure/byzantine assumptions.

## Scope
Comprehensive tests for Byzantine fault tolerance model and quorum rules.

## Test Categories

### n/f Assumptions
- [ ] 3-node mesh tolerates 0 Byzantine faults
- [ ] 4-node mesh tolerates 1 Byzantine fault
- [ ] 7-node mesh tolerates 2 Byzantine faults
- [ ] f < n/3 invariant enforced
- [ ] Quorum size = n - f calculated correctly

### Threshold Rules
- [ ] Zone operations require 2f+1 signatures
- [ ] Checkpoint advancement requires quorum
- [ ] Key rotation requires quorum
- [ ] Revocation propagation requires quorum
- [ ] Threshold signature verification

### Degraded Mode Semantics
- [ ] Degraded mode triggers at f failures
- [ ] Operations pause when quorum lost
- [ ] Clear error codes for degraded state
- [ ] Recovery path when nodes return
- [ ] Degraded mode logged/alerted

### Safety Tier Quorums
- [ ] Safe operations: single node
- [ ] Risky operations: 2f+1 quorum
- [ ] Dangerous operations: higher quorum
- [ ] Critical operations: owner quorum

### Split-Brain Prevention
- [ ] Only one partition can make progress
- [ ] Minority partition refuses writes
- [ ] Majority partition continues
- [ ] Merge after heal

## Golden Vectors
Location: `tests/vectors/quorum/`
- `quorum_3_of_3.cbor`
- `quorum_3_of_5.cbor`
- `degraded_state.cbor`

## Logging Requirements
```json
{
  "timestamp": "RFC3339",
  "test_name": "test_quorum_threshold",
  "phase": "execute",
  "correlation_id": "uuid",
  "n": 5,
  "f": 1,
  "quorum_size": 4,
  "signatures_collected": 4,
  "result": "pass"
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quorum calculations are correct
- Degraded mode is reliable
- Split-brain is prevented

title: [FCP3/P2.2] Carve fcp-policy as the single owner of zone, capability, and provenance semantics
description:
Background: zone binding, capability checks, provenance, and admission logic are central platform semantics, but today they are still partly smeared between shared core code and host owned orchestration paths. That makes policy too easy to bypass or reinterpret.

Scope: define and extract fcp-policy as the owner of security and admission semantics: zone rules, capability scoping, provenance constraints, placement eligibility inputs, and any policy relevant decision vocabulary that should be shared across host, mesh, and CLI explanation flows. Include canonical policy decision records, denial reasons, and deterministic policy fixtures so later negative tests, placement checks, and CLI explanation flows can prove semantics mechanically instead of recreating them ad hoc.

Acceptance: policy concepts have a single owner, downstream code consumes those policy contracts rather than embedding parallel policy logic, and policy outcomes are explicit enough for negative tests and operator explanations.

title: [FCP3/P3] Realign FCPC and FCPS wire and durable truth around mesh native semantics
description:
Background: V3 distinguishes a live control and evidence plane, FCPC, from a durable object plane, FCPS. Today the implementation still leans too heavily on host local runtime state and adapter specific behavior, especially around admin and control truth and durable evidence objects.

Scope: make FCPC and FCPS canonical, define durable schemas for the facts the system must remember beyond a single host process, and align store, manifest, registry, and conformance work with that model. The phase must make wire contracts and durable object shapes replayable and inspectable through deterministic fixtures, serialization round trips, repair scenarios, cross crate integration tests, and structured diagnostic artifacts so later user facing tooling can explain what is live, what is durable, and how the two relate. This phase is successful when durable truth can be replayed, repaired, and explained without treating the host process as the sole authority.

Acceptance: FCPC and FCPS semantics are backed by stable schemas, proof fixtures, and detailed transcripts or logs that later conformance, operator, and e2e beads can reuse directly instead of reconstructing from host local behavior.

comments.author: CobaltHarbor
comments.text: HTTP admin, local process memory, and ad hoc host structs are adapters in this phase, not the semantic model. If a fact matters for readiness, failover, or audit, it should have a canonical FCPC or FCPS form rather than living only in host local code paths.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: All 5 children closed (P3.1-P3.5). FCPC/FCPS wire and durable truth fully realigned around mesh-native semantics. 921 conformance vectors, 13 FCPS durability boundary tests, comprehensive store/repair/GC coverage.

title: [FCP3/P1.2] Publish canonical owner map and forbidden overlaps
description:
Background: the V3 architecture only becomes actionable when every major semantic noun has one clear home. Without that, crate splits and protocol changes will drift or reintroduce the same ambiguity under new names.

Scope: publish the canonical owner map for execution lifecycle, zone and capability and provenance policy, evidence and receipts and checkpoints and revocation, FCPC framing, FCPS durable objects, store invariants, placement and leases, host orchestration, SDK authoring surfaces, and CLI and operator projections. Name forbidden overlaps explicitly so future work knows what not to reintroduce.

title: fcp-mesh/node: handle_symbol_request accepts caller-supplied is_authenticated, OR'd with local state — peer rate limits trivially bypassable
description:
**File**: crates/fcp-mesh/src/node.rs:1027-1036 (`handle_symbol_request`) and 1115-1122 (`validate_symbol_request`)

**Code**:
```rust
pub async fn handle_symbol_request(
    &mut self,
    request: SymbolRequest,
    peer: &NodeId,
    is_authenticated: bool,    // ← caller-supplied trust claim
    now_ms: u64,
) -> Result<SymbolResponse, SymbolRequestError> {
    let (validated, meta) = self
        .validate_symbol_request(&request, peer, is_authenticated, now_ms)
        .await?;
    ...
}

async fn validate_symbol_request(...) -> ... {
    let mut authenticated = is_authenticated || self.is_peer_authenticated(peer);
    //                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ caller's bool ORed with local truth
    ...
}
```

**Lens**: Axiom 6 ("presence-only checks are worthless") + Axiom 9 ("server-authoritative state").

**Root cause**: `MeshNode::handle_symbol_request` is the `pub` entry point for symbol-request RPCs from peers. It accepts `is_authenticated: bool` as a function argument. Inside `validate_symbol_request`, the local truth (`self.is_peer_authenticated(peer)`) is OR'd with the caller's claim:

  - caller true + local false → `authenticated = true` (bypass)
  - caller false + local true → `authenticated = true` (correct)
  - caller true + local true → `authenticated = true` (correct)
  - caller false + local false → `authenticated = false` (correct)

The OR construction means a caller that lies upward is never caught. The local truth can never override the caller.

**Why this is exploitable**:

1. `is_authenticated` is supposed to be derived from the transport layer ("did this request arrive over an authenticated session?"). But the trust boundary is in MeshNode, NOT in the transport. Any code path that constructs a `SymbolRequest` and calls `handle_symbol_request(req, peer, true, ...)` bypasses rate limiting and authentication-required gates.

2. Downstream of `validate_symbol_request`, `authenticated` is passed to `AdmissionController::check_admission` (admission.rs:960) which uses it to:
   - Skip `AuthenticationRequired` rejection (admission.rs:935-943)
   - Use the LARGER `authenticated_byte_limit` / `authenticated_symbol_limit` instead of the unauthenticated tier (admission.rs:969-970)
   - Skip the strict per-request unauthenticated cap at symbol_request.rs:287

3. `AdmissionController::set_authenticated` is called at node.rs:1172-1173 with the OR'd value, which then PERMANENTLY upgrades the peer's authentication state (lines 977-983 in admission.rs). So a single hostile call with `is_authenticated: true` not only bypasses this request, it sticks the peer at the elevated tier for all future requests until session-close — without the peer ever holding a valid session.

**Concrete attack** (assuming the FCP3 transport layer at any future change accidentally trusts a wire flag, or an embedding that wraps MeshNode passes through a request-supplied bool):

1. Attacker sends a symbol request with `is_authenticated` bit set in the wire header (or otherwise causes the embedding code to pass true).
2. `handle_symbol_request(req, peer, true, ...)` runs.
3. `validate_symbol_request` ORs to true, skips authentication-required check, uses the larger byte/symbol limits.
4. `set_authenticated(peer, true, now_ms)` records the peer as authenticated.
5. All subsequent requests from `peer` get the elevated tier even if passed `is_authenticated: false`, because `is_peer_authenticated(peer)` now returns true (admission.rs:984).

**Spec violation**: Per the FCP3 admission control NORMATIVE rules, authentication is a property of the cryptographic session. A boolean argument is not a substitute for a verified MeshSession.

**Fix plan**:

1. **Remove the `is_authenticated` parameter from `handle_symbol_request`** (and from `validate_symbol_request`). The function already has `peer: &NodeId` and access to `self.is_peer_authenticated(peer)` (which checks both `self.sessions` and `self.admission`).

2. Replace the OR with the local lookup:
   ```rust
   let authenticated = self.is_peer_authenticated(peer);
   ```

3. Audit other handlers (`handle_gossip_message`, `handle_*` family) for the same anti-pattern. The OR should never appear with caller-supplied trust claims.

4. **Update tests** to exercise the new shape: a peer must establish a session via the proper handshake to get the authenticated tier. Tests that currently pass `is_authenticated: true` directly are smelling the same bug.

5. Regression test: `handle_symbol_request` with no prior session AND no admission.set_authenticated returns the unauthenticated tier limits even when the (now-removed) wire bit is set.

**Severity**: MEDIUM. The exploit requires a caller of MeshNode that propagates a wire-supplied bool — currently no production caller does so verbatim, but the API shape invites the bug. The persistent state upgrade via `set_authenticated` is the high-impact part: a single bypass call promotes the peer permanently. Defense-in-depth at the boundary (don't accept the bool) eliminates the entire class.

title: fcp-host: /rpc/connectors/{id}/artifact GET leaks supply-chain provenance without auth
description:
## Finding

`crates/fcp-host/src/bin/fcp-host.rs:2460-2464` registers

    /rpc/connectors/{connector_id}/artifact  →  connector_artifact_metadata_handler

OUTSIDE the `protected_routes` block (which is gated by `admin_auth_middleware`, fcp-host.rs:2447-2450). The handler at `connector_artifact_metadata_handler` (fcp-host.rs:2895) returns `ConnectorArtifactMetadataResponse` — the full supply-chain surface:

  * artifact content hash (blake3-256 of the connector binary)
  * SLSA level claim
  * builder-identity attestation + builder_id
  * `SupplyChainSignature { algorithm, key_id, signature, signed_fields }`
  * provenance_hash + trust_root binding (sigstore root id)
  * source URI and size

An existing `TODO(review)` comment at fcp-host.rs:2462 already flags this:

    // TODO(review): This GET route exposes supply-chain provenance (hashes/signatures) without authentication.

## Why it matters (P2)

1. **Attack-surface enumeration.** Any caller who can reach the host's HTTP endpoint — including the TCP bind target and any reverse proxy — can enumerate every installed connector's id, version, binary hash, and the exact Ed25519 `key_id` that signed its provenance. That's a free reconnaissance channel against the zone's trust anchors.

2. **Signature-key pinning leak.** The response exposes the trust_root id (e.g. sigstore root id) and the builder allowlist. An attacker planning a supply-chain substitution learns exactly which identities they need to impersonate.

3. **Inconsistent with the rest of the RPC surface.** Every other artifact-related route — `/rpc/connectors/{id}/artifact/register`, `.../install`, `.../update`, `.../rollback` — is inside `protected_routes` and requires the admin bearer token. The GET leaks what the POSTs defend.

## Fix

Move the route inside `protected_routes` (alongside the register/install/update/rollback artifact handlers). No handler logic change needed — the middleware is applied at the router level.

If public read access is ever intentionally required (e.g. for a local diagnostics dashboard), split into:

    /rpc/admin/connectors/{id}/artifact   — authenticated, full detail
    /rpc/connectors/{id}/artifact/summary — public, strip signature + trust_root + builder identity

## Verification

After the fix:

  * `curl http://host:port/rpc/connectors/fcp.discord:.../artifact` MUST return 401/403.
  * With the admin bearer token header, MUST return 200 with the existing JSON body.
  * Add an integration test under `crates/fcp-host/tests/` that asserts both outcomes against a running `fcp-host` instance.
close_reason: 5ececde6 moves GET /rpc/connectors/{id}/artifact into protected_routes (chained on existing POST register handler); admin_auth_middleware now gates both verbs. New regression test artifact_metadata_get_requires_admin_bearer_qeapt at tests/host_connector_integration.rs pins 403 unauth + 200 admin-bearer + explicit assertions that unauth 403 body does not leak supply_chain_signature/trust_root/builder_identity/artifact_hash/slsa_level fields.

title: [CRITICAL] Fix non-production default URLs in DocuSign and Plaid connectors

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CRITICAL: Non-Production Default URLs

Two connectors ship DEFAULT_BASE_URL constants pointing at non-production environments. Any deployment using the out-of-the-box defaults will silently hit sandbox/demo infrastructure rather than the provider's production API. This is the most dangerous class of hard-coded constant because it fails silently — requests succeed but against the wrong data.

FINDINGS:

1. DocuSign (connectors/docusign/src/client.rs:38):
   DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://demo.docusign.net/restapi/v2.1/accounts"
   - This is the DocuSign DEMO environment, not production
   - Production URLs follow the pattern: https://na1.docusign.net/..., https://eu.docusign.net/..., etc.
   - The connector's doctor output (connector.rs:1050) mentions both demo and production patterns, but the *default* is demo
   - Any user who doesn't explicitly override base_url gets demo

2. Plaid (connectors/plaid/src/client.rs:21):
   DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://sandbox.plaid.com"
   - This is the Plaid SANDBOX environment, not production or development
   - Plaid has three environments: sandbox, development, production
   - All data in sandbox is fake test data
   - The connector explicitly names environments (connector.rs:18,22,65) but defaults to sandbox

FIX APPROACH:
- Remove the hard-coded default entirely from both connectors
- Make base_url a required configuration field (no default = forces explicit choice)
- Add environment enum (Production/Sandbox/Demo) to the configure() handler
- Update doctor/self_check to warn if running against non-production
- Update manifest.toml to document the required configuration
- Add tests verifying that unconfigured connectors refuse to start rather than silently hitting demo/sandbox

WHY THIS MATTERS:
FCP's security model is zone-based with capability tokens. A connector that silently routes traffic to a demo server undermines the entire trust chain — real capability tokens are sent to a test environment, potentially leaking production intent to sandbox infrastructure. This is a category of bug that the FCP security invariants should mechanically prevent.

title: [MOR/C3.7] Encode zone binding as type-level invariant via ZoneBound wrapper

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: WHAT: Create a ZoneBound<Z, T> wrapper type that binds a value T to a specific zone Z at the type level. Connector instances would be ZoneBound<Z, ConnectorInstance> — the zone is part of the type, preventing accidental cross-zone operations. WHY: A7 Type-Theoretic found zone boundary crossing is runtime-checked, not type-enforced. J1 Deontic found single-zone binding is documented only with no mechanical enforcement. A connector receiving requests from multiple zones would only be caught at runtime. IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH: ```rust pub struct ZoneBound<T> { inner: T, zone_id: ZoneId, } impl<T> ZoneBound<T> { pub fn bind(inner: T, zone: ZoneId) -> Self { Self { inner, zone_id: zone } } pub fn zone_id(&self) -> &ZoneId { &self.zone_id } // Operations can only access inner if zone matches pub fn with_zone_check<R>(&self, expected_zone: &ZoneId, f: impl FnOnce(&T) -> R) -> Result<R, ZoneViolation> { if &self.zone_id != expected_zone { return Err(ZoneViolation { ... }); } Ok(f(&self.inner)) } } ``` NOTE: Full phantom-type zone encoding (where zones are types, not values) requires const generics or associated types, which may be too complex for 150 connectors. The value-level ZoneBound wrapper with runtime check is a pragmatic middle ground that still enforces the binding at the API level. WHERE: crates/fcp-core/src/zone.rs or new module. Used in fcp-host when creating connector instances. ACCEPTANCE: (1) ZoneBound<T> type exists. (2) Connector instances wrapped in ZoneBound. (3) Operations require zone match check. (4) Cross-zone operation returns ZoneViolation error. (5) At least 4 tests: bind and access within zone, cross-zone access rejected, zone_id accessor, serialization. ESTIMATED EFFORT: 2-3 days. DEPENDS ON: C3.1 (phantom tokens) — the zone binding interacts with token zone_id validation.
