title: [CUAL-E.1] jq-style field extraction with --extract flag
description:
## Goal
Add --extract (or --jq) flag to all fwc commands that produces JSON output, enabling surgical field extraction without agents needing to parse full JSON blobs.

## Commands
- fwc invoke github list_issues --extract '.issues[0].title'
- fwc invoke github list_issues --extract '.issues | length'
- fwc invoke github list_issues --extract '.issues[].{title,number,state}'
- fwc search 'send message' --extract '.[0].operation_id'

## Implementation
Use jaq crate (Rust implementation of jq) for filter evaluation. The filter is applied to the JSON output of any command AFTER successful execution.

## Why Agents Need This
Agents pay per token. A full GitHub issue listing might be 5000 tokens. The agent only needs the issue number (3 tokens). --extract reduces output to exactly what the agent needs, saving 99%+ of token budget on data-heavy operations.

## Edge Cases
- Invalid filter expression: return error with jq syntax help
- Filter returns empty: return null with exit code 0 (not an error)
- Filter returns multiple values: return JSON array
- Non-JSON command output: error with 'command does not produce JSON output'

## Deliverables
- jaq integration as output post-processor
- --extract flag on all JSON-producing commands
- Error handling for invalid filters
- Tests: field selection, array indexing, object construction, length, empty results

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: Use the 'jaq-core' and 'jaq-std' crates (Rust jq implementation). These are already well-maintained and support the full jq filter language. The --extract flag should be a post-processing step applied after the command produces its JSON output — this means it works with ANY command that produces JSON, not just invoke. Performance consideration: for large outputs (100KB+), stream through jaq rather than loading entire JSON into memory. Edge case: if the command produces TOON output (not JSON), --extract should emit an error suggesting --json flag.

Combining --extract with --format table should error: 'Cannot use --extract with --format table. Use --extract for field selection or --format table --columns for column selection.' Combining --extract with --template should also error: pick one output transformation.

title: [CUAL-E.2] Handlebars template rendering with --template flag
description:
## Goal
Add --template flag for rendering operation results through Handlebars templates, producing human/agent-optimized text output.

- {{json .}} - pretty-print as JSON
- {{compact .}} - single-line JSON
- {{count items}} - array length
- {{truncate text 80}} - truncate string
- {{timeago timestamp}} - relative time

## Why Agents Need This
Templates let agents format output for specific downstream consumers: Slack messages, commit messages, issue descriptions, email bodies. Instead of extracting fields and string-building in the agent context (expensive), the template runs on the output directly.

title: [CUAL-E.4] Streaming NDJSON output for pipe-friendly line-delimited JSON
description:
## Goal
Add --format ndjson for newline-delimited JSON output, optimized for streaming and piping between commands.

## Behavior
- Each result item emitted as a single JSON line (no array wrapping)
- Flushed immediately (no buffering) for real-time streaming
- Compatible with jq --slurp for re-assembly
- Works with streaming/event operations (each event = one line)

## Commands
- fwc invoke github list_issues --format ndjson | jq '.title'
- fwc events tail slack --format ndjson | fwc pipe github.create_issue
- fwc batch ops.jsonl --format ndjson  # Each result on its own line

## Why Agents Need This
NDJSON is the standard format for streaming JSON between processes. It enables:
- Real-time processing of streaming events
- Piping between fwc commands
- Integration with standard Unix tools (jq, grep, wc)
- Partial result consumption (don't wait for full array)

## Deliverables
- NDJSON output formatter
- Immediate flush per line
- Integration with streaming/event commands
- Tests: list output, streaming output, pipe scenarios

title: [CUAL-F] Pipeline & Composition Engine
description: Track F: Pipeline and Composition Engine. Agents often need multi-step workflows: fetch GitHub issues, filter by label, post summary to Slack. Today this requires multiple fwc invoke calls with manual JSON plumbing between them. This track adds: two-operation pipe (A output feeds B input), named multi-step pipeline definitions in TOML, conditional branching, error handling/rollback, pipeline dry-run with cost/risk estimation, and a pre-built recipe library for common cross-connector workflows.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Pipeline execution is real, composable, and explicit about data handoff, conditional behavior, rollback or compensation limits, and cost or risk signaling.
2. Dry-run or preview surfaces never pretend that connector actions already happened, and pipeline recipes remain auditable and reproducible.
3. Unit, integration, and transcript-style E2E scenarios with detailed logging are required for happy paths, branch paths, rollback paths, and cross-connector failure handling.

title: [CUAL-F.1] Two-operation pipe: output of A feeds input of B
description:
## Goal
Add 'fwc pipe' that chains two operations: the output of operation A becomes the input of operation B, with a JSON path mapping between them.

## Commands
- fwc pipe github.list_issues slack.send_message --map 'issues[0].title -> text, "#general" -> channel'
- fwc pipe github.search_issues todoist.create_task --map 'items[0].title -> content'
- fwc pipe jira.get_issue github.create_issue --map-file jira-to-github.json
- fwc pipe A B --dry-run  # Show what would be sent to B without executing

## Map Syntax
Simple: 'source.path -> target.field'
Multiple: 'a.x -> b.x, a.y -> b.y'
Literal: '"value" -> field'
Template: '"Issue: {{a.title}}" -> body'

## How It Works
1. Execute operation A with provided input
2. Apply mapping rules to transform A's output into B's input
3. Validate B's input against B's input_schema
4. Show preview if B is risky/dangerous, require approval
5. Execute operation B
6. Return B's output (with A's output available via --include-intermediate)

## Error Handling
- If A fails: report error, don't execute B
- If mapping produces invalid input for B: report validation error with fix suggestions
- If B fails: report error with A's output still available

## Deliverables
- Pipe executor with A -> mapping -> B flow
- Map expression parser and evaluator
- Map file format (JSON)
- Dry-run mode
- Approval gating for risky B operations
- Tests: happy path, mapping errors, A failure, B failure, approval

title: [CUAL-F.2] Named multi-step pipeline definitions in TOML
description:
## Goal
Define reusable multi-step pipelines as TOML files that chain N operations with mappings, conditionals, and error handling.

## Pipeline Definition Format
[pipeline]
name = 'notify-on-new-issues'
description = 'Check for new GitHub issues and post to Slack'
version = '1.0'

[[steps]]
id = 'fetch'
operation = 'github.list_issues'
input = { owner = '{{params.owner}}', repo = '{{params.repo}}', state = 'open', since = '{{params.since}}' }

[[steps]]
id = 'notify'
operation = 'slack.send_message'
input = { channel = '{{params.channel}}', text = 'New issues: {{steps.fetch.output.issues | length}}' }
depends_on = ['fetch']
condition = '{{steps.fetch.output.issues | length}} > 0'

[params]
owner = { type = 'string', required = true }
repo = { type = 'string', required = true }
channel = { type = 'string', default = '#general' }
since = { type = 'string', default = '24h' }

## Commands
- fwc pipeline run notify-on-new-issues --param owner=octocat --param repo=hello-world
- fwc pipeline validate my-pipeline.toml
- fwc pipeline dry-run my-pipeline.toml --param ...
- fwc pipeline list                        # Show available pipelines
- fwc pipeline show my-pipeline            # Show pipeline details

## Pipeline Storage
- User pipelines: ~/.fwc/pipelines/*.toml
- Project pipelines: .fwc/pipelines/*.toml
- Built-in recipes: bundled in fwc binary

## Deliverables
- Pipeline TOML parser and validator
- Step executor with dependency resolution
- Template rendering for step inputs (Handlebars)
- Parameter binding with defaults and validation
- fwc pipeline command family
- Tests: multi-step, conditional, parameterized, validation errors

Common errors to catch early: duplicate step IDs, depends_on referencing non-existent steps, circular step dependencies, missing required step fields. Emit clear validation errors with line numbers. Also: pipelines should be publishable/shareable (see F.5 recipes), so the schema must be stable and versioned from day one.

title: [CUAL-F.3] Pipeline conditional branching and error handling
description:
## Goal
Add conditional branching (if/then/else) and error handling (on_error) to pipeline definitions.

## Conditional Steps
[[steps]]
id = 'check-labels'
operation = 'github.get_issue'
input = { owner = '{{params.owner}}', repo = '{{params.repo}}', issue_number = '{{steps.fetch.output.issues[0].number}}' }
condition = '{{steps.fetch.output.issues | length}} > 0'

[[steps]]
id = 'escalate'
operation = 'slack.send_message'
input = { channel = '#urgent', text = 'Critical issue found\!' }
condition = '{{steps.check-labels.output.issue.labels | any("priority:critical")}}' 
depends_on = ['check-labels']

## Error Handling
[[steps]]
id = 'risky-op'
operation = 'github.create_issue'
input = { ... }
on_error = 'skip'  # skip | abort | retry(3) | fallback(step_id)

[[steps]]
id = 'fallback-notify'
operation = 'slack.send_message'
input = { text = 'Failed to create issue: {{steps.risky-op.error}}' }
trigger = 'on_error(risky-op)'

## Deliverables
- Condition evaluator (simple expression language)
- Error handling modes: skip, abort, retry with count, fallback to another step
- Error-triggered steps
- Pipeline execution trace showing which steps ran, skipped, failed
- Tests: branching, error-skip, error-retry, error-fallback

title: [CUAL-F.4] Pipeline dry-run with cost and risk estimation
description:

Pipeline: notify-on-new-issues (3 steps)
Step 1: github.list_issues     [safe]  ~1 API call, reads 'github.read' capability
Step 2: github.get_issue       [safe]  ~0-N API calls (conditional), reads 'github.read'
Step 3: slack.send_message     [risky] ~0-1 API call (conditional), requires 'slack.write'

Risk Assessment: MEDIUM (step 3 writes to external service)
Rate Limit Impact: github.read: 2/5000 remaining, slack.write: 1/100 remaining
Required Capabilities: github.read, slack.write
Required Approvals: step 3 requires policy approval

title: [CUAL-F.5] Pre-built pipeline recipe library for common cross-connector workflows
description:
## Goal
Ship fwc with a library of pre-built pipeline recipes for common agent workflows that work across connector combinations.

## Recipe Categories

### Development Workflows
- issue-to-branch: GitHub/Jira issue -> create branch -> post link back
- pr-review-notify: new PR -> summarize changes -> notify Slack/Discord
- deploy-announce: release tag -> deploy status -> notify team
- bug-triage: Sentry alert -> create issue -> assign -> notify

### Communication Workflows
- cross-post: Slack message -> Discord + Telegram
- digest-email: aggregate Slack messages -> send Gmail digest
- meeting-notes: notion/logseq doc -> send to attendees

### Data Workflows
- backup-to-s3: list items from service -> export -> upload to S3
- sync-contacts: HubSpot contacts -> Google Contacts
- analytics-report: Mixpanel data -> format -> send to Slack

### Operations Workflows
- health-check-all: check all connectors -> report to Slack
- rotate-secrets: list expiring -> rotate -> update configs -> notify

## Commands
- fwc recipe list                          # Show all built-in recipes
- fwc recipe show issue-to-branch          # Show recipe details
- fwc recipe run issue-to-branch --param ...  # Run with params
- fwc recipe export issue-to-branch > my-recipe.toml  # Export for customization

## Deliverables
- 15-20 built-in recipes covering the above categories
- Recipe registry with metadata (category, required connectors, risk level)
- fwc recipe command family
- Recipe customization via export + edit + re-import
- Tests: each recipe validates and dry-runs successfully

title: [CUAL-G.1] Map-over-inputs: apply one operation to N inputs in parallel
description:
## Goal
Add 'fwc map' that applies a single operation to a list of inputs, executing in parallel with configurable concurrency.

## Commands
- fwc map github.get_issue --inputs '[{"owner":"o","repo":"r","issue_number":1},{"owner":"o","repo":"r","issue_number":2}]'
- fwc map github.get_issue --input-file issues.jsonl    # One JSON per line
- fwc map github.get_issue --input-template '{"owner":"octocat","repo":"hello-world","issue_number":{{item}}}' --items '1,2,3,4,5'
- fwc map github.get_issue ... --concurrency 5           # Max 5 parallel
- fwc map github.get_issue ... --on-error continue        # Don't abort on individual failures

## Output
NDJSON by default (one result per line, matching input order):
{"index":0,"status":"success","result":{...}}
{"index":1,"status":"error","error":{"code":"FCP_ERR_NOT_FOUND",...}}
{"index":2,"status":"success","result":{...}}

## Progress
When not piped, show progress bar: [=====>    ] 3/5 (60%) 2 ok, 1 err

## Rate Limit Awareness
- Query connector rate limit pools before starting
- Auto-throttle to stay within limits
- If rate limited mid-batch, pause and wait for quota reset

## Deliverables
- Map executor with parallel dispatch (tokio tasks)
- Input sources: inline JSON, JSONL file, template + items
- Concurrency control and rate limit integration
- Progress tracking
- Error handling modes: abort, continue, retry
- Tests: parallel execution, rate limiting, partial failures

title: [CUAL-G.2] Batch-from-file: heterogeneous JSONL operations
description:
## Goal
Add 'fwc batch' that executes a file of heterogeneous operations (different connectors, different operations) with dependency ordering and parallel execution where safe.

## Batch File Format (JSONL)
{"id":"step1","connector":"github","operation":"list_issues","input":{"owner":"o","repo":"r"}}
{"id":"step2","connector":"slack","operation":"send_message","input":{"channel":"#dev","text":"Issues fetched"},"depends_on":["step1"]}
{"id":"step3","connector":"todoist","operation":"create_task","input":{"content":"Review issues"}}

## Commands
- fwc batch ops.jsonl                      # Execute batch
- fwc batch ops.jsonl --dry-run            # Validate and show execution plan
- fwc batch ops.jsonl --concurrency 3      # Max parallel operations
- fwc batch ops.jsonl --on-error abort     # Stop on first error
- fwc batch ops.jsonl --format ndjson      # One result per line

## Execution Order
1. Parse all operations and build dependency graph
2. Validate all inputs against schemas
3. Execute in topological order (independent ops run in parallel)
4. Collect results, keyed by operation ID

## Deliverables
- Batch file parser and validator
- Dependency graph builder
- Topological parallel executor
- Result collection with per-operation status
- Tests: parallel, sequential, mixed dependencies, validation errors

title: [CUAL-H.1] Unified event stream tailing across connectors
description:
## Goal
Add 'fwc events tail' that streams events from one or more connectors in real-time, with unified output format.

## Commands
- fwc events tail slack                     # Tail Slack events
- fwc events tail slack,discord             # Tail multiple connectors
- fwc events tail --all                     # Tail all streaming connectors
- fwc events tail slack --format ndjson     # Machine-friendly output
- fwc events tail slack --since 5m         # Include events from last 5 minutes

## Output Format
Each event emitted as a structured line:
[14:32:05] slack  message.new  #general  @alice: Hey team, deploy is done
[14:32:07] discord message.new  #dev     @bob: Acknowledged

JSON mode:
{"timestamp":"...","connector":"slack","event_type":"message.new","data":{...}}

## How It Works
1. For each connector, check if it supports streaming archetype
2. Call handle_subscribe() to get event stream
3. Merge streams into unified output
4. Apply filters (Track H.2)
5. Handle backpressure: if consumer is slow, buffer N events then drop oldest

## Deliverables
- Event stream merger for multiple connectors
- Unified event output format (TOON and JSON)
- Backpressure handling
- Historical replay for connectors that support it
- Tests: single connector, multi-connector, backpressure

title: [CUAL-H.2] Event filtering by type, pattern, and field match
description:
## Goal
Add event filtering to 'fwc events tail' that lets agents subscribe to precisely the events they care about.

## Filter Syntax
- fwc events tail slack --type message.new          # By event type
- fwc events tail slack --pattern 'deploy*'         # Glob on event type
- fwc events tail slack --match 'data.channel=#general'  # Field match
- fwc events tail slack --match 'data.text~bug'     # Regex match on field
- fwc events tail slack --exclude-type reaction.*   # Exclude pattern

## Compound Filters
- fwc events tail slack --type message.new --match 'data.channel=#urgent'
- fwc events tail --all --type '*.error' --match 'data.severity=critical'

## How It Works
1. Parse filter expressions into a filter chain
2. Each event passes through all filters (AND logic)
3. Events that match all filters are emitted
4. Events that fail any filter are dropped silently

## Deliverables
- Filter expression parser
- Type filter (exact, glob, regex)
- Field match filter (equality, regex, contains)
- Exclude filter
- Filter chain with AND composition
- Tests: each filter type, compound filters, no-match scenarios

title: [CUAL-H.3] Event replay from checkpoint or sequence number
description:
## Goal
Add event replay capability: resume event consumption from a saved checkpoint or specific sequence number.

## Commands
- fwc events tail slack --checkpoint slack-cp.json   # Resume from checkpoint
- fwc events tail slack --from-seq 12345             # Resume from sequence
- fwc events replay slack --from 2026-03-09T14:00 --to 2026-03-09T15:00  # Time range

## Checkpoint Format
{"connector":"slack","last_seq":12345,"last_timestamp":"...","last_event_id":"..."}

## How It Works
1. On each event, update checkpoint file (atomic write)
2. On startup with --checkpoint, read last position and request replay from there
3. Connector subscribe() accepts optional start_from parameter
4. If connector does not support replay, emit warning and start from current

## Deliverables
- Checkpoint file writer (atomic, with temp file + rename)
- Checkpoint reader and subscribe-from-position logic
- Time-range replay for connectors that support it
- Fallback behavior for connectors without replay
- Tests: checkpoint save/load, replay, fallback

title: [CUAL-H.4] Event-triggered operation execution (reactive rules)
description:
## Goal
Add reactive rules that automatically invoke operations when matching events arrive, enabling event-driven automation.

## Rule Definition (TOML)
[[rules]]
name = 'bug-to-issue'
description = 'Create GitHub issue when Slack message mentions bug'
trigger = { connector = 'slack', type = 'message.new', match = 'data.text~bug|Bug|BUG' }
action = { connector = 'github', operation = 'create_issue', input = { owner = 'octocat', repo = 'hello-world', title = 'Bug report from Slack: {{event.data.text | truncate(80)}}', body = 'Reported by {{event.data.user}} in #{{event.data.channel}}\n\n{{event.data.text}}' } }
throttle = { max = 5, window = '1h' }  # Max 5 triggers per hour

## Commands
- fwc rules add my-rule.toml              # Register a rule
- fwc rules list                           # Show active rules
- fwc rules test my-rule.toml --event '...'  # Test with mock event
- fwc rules enable/disable rule-name       # Toggle rules
- fwc rules run                            # Start reactive event loop

## Safety
- Rules that invoke risky/dangerous operations require explicit approval at registration
- Throttle is mandatory to prevent runaway automation
- Dry-run mode: log what would happen without executing
- Circuit breaker: if rule triggers too many errors, auto-disable

## Deliverables
- Rule definition parser (TOML)
- Event matcher integrated with event filters (H.2)
- Action executor with template rendering
- Throttle enforcement
- Circuit breaker logic
- fwc rules command family
- Tests: match, throttle, dry-run, circuit breaker

title: [CUAL-I] Rate Limit Intelligence
description: Track I: Rate Limit Intelligence. FCP connectors declare RateLimitPools and operation-pool mappings in manifests. But there is no CLI surface to see current usage, forecast quota resets, or automatically throttle batch operations. This track adds: rate limit status dashboard, automatic throttling in batch/parallel ops, quota forecasting, and cross-connector budget optimization.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Rate-limit intelligence is driven by real pool usage, reset windows, and connector-specific budget rules rather than synthetic dashboards.
2. Forecasting, throttling, and budget optimization remain conservative, auditable, and interference-aware when combined with retry, batch, or pipeline controllers.
3. Unit, integration, benchmark, and transcript-style E2E verification with detailed logging are required for quota exhaustion, reset prediction, and backpressure behavior.

comments.text: [Alien-artifact-coding + graveyard uplift] Automatic throttling and quota optimization should be treated as a budgeted control system, not a bag of heuristics. The plan should require an explicit queue or rate model, Little\'s Law or utilization audits where measurable, capacity tables for normal and burst regimes, and assumption monitors that detect when the model stops fitting reality. Any adaptive throttle or budget optimizer should ship shadow-first with a deterministic conservative fallback, explicit exhaustion behavior, and interference checks against batch parallelism and retry logic before promotion.

title: [CUAL-I.1] Rate limit status dashboard across all connectors
description:
## Goal
Add 'fwc rate-limits' that shows current rate limit usage across all connectors, enabling agents to plan operations within quota.

## Commands
- fwc rate-limits                          # All connectors
- fwc rate-limits github                   # One connector
- fwc rate-limits --json                   # Machine-readable
- fwc rate-limits --warning                # Only show near-limit pools

## Output
Connector      Pool           Used/Limit  Resets In  Status
github         core.read      4500/5000   12m        WARNING (90%)
github         search         8/30        1m         OK (27%)
slack          web.write      45/100      58m        OK (45%)
twilio         sms.send       198/200     3h         CRITICAL (99%)

## How It Works
1. For each configured connector, call rate_limits() to get RateLimitDeclarations
2. Query current usage from host rate limit tracking
3. Calculate percentage, time-to-reset, and status (OK/WARNING/CRITICAL)
4. WARNING: > 80% used. CRITICAL: > 95% used.

## Why Agents Need This
Before starting a batch operation, agents need to know how much quota remains. Without this, they risk hitting rate limits mid-batch and wasting work.

## Deliverables
- Rate limit aggregator across connectors
- Status calculator with thresholds
- fwc rate-limits command
- Warning/critical highlighting
- Tests: various usage levels, multi-pool scenarios

title: [CUAL-I.2] Automatic throttling and quota-aware scheduling
description:
## Goal
Integrate rate limit awareness into all execution paths (invoke, map, batch, pipeline) so operations are automatically throttled to stay within limits.

## Behavior
- Before each operation: check remaining quota in relevant rate limit pool
- If quota sufficient: proceed immediately
- If quota low (< 10%): slow down (add delay between operations)
- If quota exhausted: wait for reset, show countdown
- If multiple pools apply: respect the most restrictive

## Integration Points
- fwc invoke: single operation, simple check
- fwc map: distribute operations across time window to stay within limits
- fwc batch: schedule operations based on combined rate limit budget
- fwc pipeline: estimate total rate limit cost before starting

## User Control
- --no-throttle: bypass auto-throttling (agent accepts rate limit errors)
- --max-wait 30s: maximum time to wait for quota reset before giving up
- --rate-limit-strategy aggressive|conservative|balanced: tuning

## Deliverables
- Throttle middleware for all execution paths
- Quota prediction and scheduling algorithm
- Wait-for-reset with countdown display
- Integration with map, batch, pipeline executors
- Tests: throttle activation, wait-for-reset, strategy modes

title: fcp.youtube - YouTube Data & Studio API Connector
description:
# fcp.youtube - YouTube Data & Studio API Connector (FCP2)

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 95/100** — Critical Tier 1 connector.

**Why Critical**: YouTube is the world's second-largest search engine and a massive knowledge repository. **Transcript access alone makes this invaluable for research agents.** Video content is one of the richest information sources available.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Quick Wins (High Value + Moderate Effort)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 1 Foundation (immediate)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Knowledge,    // Video/transcript search
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,  // Channel management
]
```
- **Knowledge**: Video discovery, transcript retrieval, search
- **Operational**: Upload, publish, comment management

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Upload state, comment sync cursors
- State tracked: `{ upload_progress: HashMap<VideoId, Progress>, sync_cursors: HashMap<ChannelId, Cursor> }`
- Lease required for upload operations

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI recommended**: Handles OAuth credentials
- Memory isolation for token protection
- Capability-gated hostcalls

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // YouTube Data API v3
    host_allow: vec\![
        "www.googleapis.com".into(),
        "youtube.googleapis.com".into(),
        "oauth2.googleapis.com".into(),
        // For video upload
        "upload.youtube.com".into(),
    ],
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// Video content is external/public
video_content.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::PUBLIC_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT;

// Transcripts may contain errors
transcript.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT;

// Comments are adversarial
comment.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT
    | TaintFlags::PROMPT_SURFACE
    | TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED;

// URLs in content are unverified
if content.contains_urls() {
    content.provenance.taint |= TaintFlags::UNVERIFIED_LINK;
}
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `youtube.videos.search` | Safe | Read-only search |
| `youtube.videos.get` | Safe | Read-only metadata |
| `youtube.captions.get` | Safe | Read-only transcripts |
| `youtube.channels.get` | Safe | Read-only |
| `youtube.comments.read` | Risky | Adversarial content |
| `youtube.videos.upload` | Dangerous | Creates public content |
| `youtube.videos.update` | Dangerous | Modifies public content |
| `youtube.videos.delete` | Dangerous | Irreversible |
| `youtube.comments.write` | Dangerous | Public interaction |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Research & Knowledge Extraction
- Video metadata extraction and search
- **Transcript retrieval** (auto-generated + manual captions)
- Video summarization via transcript
- Topic research across video content

### Channel Management
- Channel analytics and insights
- Video upload and publish automation
- Comment management and moderation
- Playlist management

### Content Discovery
- Search videos by topic, channel, or criteria
- Find relevant tutorials and explanations
- Monitor competitor channels
- Track trending content

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Summarize this YouTube video" → Fetch transcript → Process
"Find videos about {topic}" → Search + metadata extraction
"What are people saying about this video?" → Comment analysis
"Monitor competitor channels for new content"
"Schedule video posts" → Content calendar management
"Extract code examples from this tutorial video"
"What are the key points from this conference talk?"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### CASS (Context-Aware Semantic Search)
- Index video transcripts
- Semantic video search
- Knowledge graph from video content

### Google AI/Gemini Integration
- Native video understanding
- Multimodal analysis
- Long video processing

### Vector DB Integration
- Transcript embeddings
- Video similarity search
- Topic clustering

### Agent Mail Integration
- Video notifications → agent threads
- Content updates
- Research findings

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **YouTube Data API v3**: Primary interface
- **YouTube Analytics API**: Channel insights
- **YouTube Reporting API**: Bulk data

### Recommended Crates
- `google-youtube3` — YouTube API client
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `serde_json` — JSON handling
- `tokio` — Async runtime

### Quota Management
YouTube API has strict quotas:
```rust
QuotaLimits {
    daily_quota: 10000,  // Units per day
    // search.list: 100 units
    // videos.list: 1 unit
    // captions.download: 200 units
    // videos.insert: 1600 units
}
```

### Authentication
| Mode | Use Case |
|------|----------|
| API Key | Public data (search, metadata) |
| OAuth2 | Private data, uploads |
| Service Account | Server-to-server |

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:media:youtube:full` | Full access | All operations |
| `z:media:youtube:read` | Read-only | Search, metadata, transcripts |
| `z:media:youtube:manage` | Management | Upload, update, delete |

### Security Considerations
- Quota exhaustion is a concern
- Public content creation is high-risk
- Comments are adversarial

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `knowledge` — Video/transcript search
- `operational` — Channel management

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `www.googleapis.com:443`
- `youtube.googleapis.com:443`
- `upload.youtube.com:443`

### Credential Injection
- API key via egress proxy (public data)
- OAuth2 tokens via CredentialId
- Never persist credentials

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `youtube.videos.search` — Search videos
- `youtube.videos.get` — Video metadata
- `youtube.captions.get` — Transcripts
- `youtube.channels.get` — Channel info
- `youtube.playlists.get` — Playlist info

### Write Operations
- `youtube.videos.upload` — Upload video (Dangerous)
- `youtube.videos.update` — Update metadata (Dangerous)
- `youtube.playlists.write` — Manage playlists
- `youtube.comments.write` — Post comments (Dangerous)

### Admin Operations
- `youtube.videos.delete` — Delete video (Dangerous)
- `youtube.channels.update` — Channel settings (Dangerous)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Search Videos
```
GET /youtube/v3/search?part=snippet&q={query}&type=video
```

### Get Video Details
```
GET /youtube/v3/videos?part=snippet,contentDetails&id={video_id}
```

### Get Captions/Transcript
```
GET /youtube/v3/captions?part=snippet&videoId={video_id}
GET /youtube/v3/captions/{caption_id}?tfmt=srt
```

### Upload Video
```json
POST /upload/youtube/v3/videos?part=snippet,status
{
  "snippet": {
    "title": "Video Title",
    "description": "Description",
    "tags": ["tag1", "tag2"]
  },
  "status": {
    "privacyStatus": "private"
  }
}
```

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- API request construction
- Response parsing
- Quota tracking
- Transcript parsing
- Error handling

### Integration Tests
- Mock YouTube API responses
- Multi-step workflows
- Quota exhaustion scenarios

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Dangerous operation approval flow
- Quota enforcement
- Audit logging

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real YouTube API calls in unit tests
- Video search functional
- Transcript retrieval works
- Quota tracking accurate
- Upload flow works
- All V2 NORMATIVE requirements satisfied

title: [MEDIUM] SymbolAck/DecodeStatus replay: signed transcripts lack recipient binding
description:
SymbolAck::transcript_bytes (fcps.rs:748-763) and DecodeStatus::transcript_bytes (fcps.rs:606-634) both include epoch_id (cross-epoch replay protection) but neither binds the recipient NodeId or a per-request nonce.

Within a single epoch, an attacker who observes a valid signed SymbolAck from B addressed to A can replay it to a third recipient D, provided D also has a pending request for the same object_id from B in the same epoch. On D, handle_symbol_ack (node.rs:1416) calls sent_symbols.remove(&ack.object_id), prematurely cancelling D's outbound transfer. Same vector for DecodeStatus via process_decode_status.

Recommended fix: extend SymbolAck and DecodeStatus to carry a `to: NodeId` field (or a per-request nonce echoed from the original SymbolRequest) and include it in the signing transcript. Bump transcript domain separators to V2 to prevent cross-version replay.

Discovered during code review of fcp-mesh after the Apr 19 swarm closed the four-handler signature-verification gap (81f303c8). The signature-verification work itself is correct; this is a residual transcript-binding gap exposed by that hardening.

Severity: MEDIUM. Requires multi-recipient request fan-out in the same epoch to exploit, and the consequence is transfer cancellation (availability), not data exfiltration.
close_reason: Bound SymbolAck/DecodeStatus V2 transcripts to recipient node and request nonce

title: fcp-store: Repair Controller has no power-aware deferral despite README claim
description:
Reality-check finding (2026-04-21).

README line 928 claims:
  'Power-aware behavior: defers non-critical repairs on battery'

Evidence: zero grep hits for battery/power/device_profile across crates/fcp-store/. RepairController::evaluate_zone + RepairController::evaluate_zone_with_report do not accept a DeviceProfile or power-state signal. All other bullets in the same list (coverage bps, placement policies, SLO-deficit/hotness/cost prioritization, bounded repair plans) are backed by real code.

Related: battery state DOES exist in crates/fcp-mesh/src/device.rs (DeviceProfile::battery_percent, is_low_battery at :357-359), so the data is available — the wiring into the repair controller is what's missing.

Fix options:
  A) Implement: plumb DeviceProfile (or a narrower PowerState) into RepairControllerConfig; add a 'defer non-critical repairs when on battery and < threshold%' gate in evaluate_zone_with_report's priority loop; add tests with DeviceProfile fixtures in crates/fcp-store/src/repair.rs.
  B) Downgrade the README claim to PLANNED (see commit that accompanied this bead for the interim doc fix).

Preferred: (A) for the target mesh-native architecture; (B) as interim doc hygiene.

File/line anchors:
  - crates/fcp-store/src/repair.rs:52 (RepairControllerConfig)
  - crates/fcp-store/src/repair.rs:1115 (evaluate_zone)
  - crates/fcp-store/src/repair.rs:1128 (evaluate_zone_with_report)
  - crates/fcp-mesh/src/device.rs:296-359 (DeviceProfile.battery_percent / is_low_battery)
  - README.md:928 (the claim)
close_reason: 42b884ab implements PowerState enum + RepairController::set_power_state + battery_defer_threshold_percent config (default 20%, matches fcp_mesh::device::is_low_battery) + next_repair() battery gate (runs before rate-limit tokens) + power_deferred stat + tracing::info! emission of repair.deferred_power_budget reason code. 4 new unit tests pin AC-dequeue / at-threshold-accept / below-threshold-defer (with rate-limit-not-consumed + queue-not-drained + AC-transition-resumes) / PowerState::is_low_battery helper. README re-upgraded PLANNED→LIMITED in 99cbe37b with new LIMITED status marker in the legend. fcp-store suite 901/901 pass.

title: [tooling] rch artifact retrieval overflows on pathological .beads recovery path depth
description:
Remote `rch exec -- cargo ...` commands in this repo can finish the actual remote compile/test successfully but then fail during artifact retrieval with rsync buffer-overflow errors against deeply nested `.beads/recovery_*` paths.

Observed repeatedly on 2026-03-25 while verifying `flywheel_connectors-0iek1` and auditing telemetry/conformance slices. Representative failure:
- `overflow: xflags=0x207a ... lastname=.beads/recovery_20260313T010949Z_rubyglen/.../.beads`
- `[Receiver] buffer overflow: recv_file_entry (file=flist.c, line=747)`
- `rsync error: error allocating core memory buffers (code 22)`

Notes:
- `.rchignore` already excludes `.beads/`, `**/.beads/`, `.beads/recovery_*`, and related patterns, so the retrieval phase appears to ignore or bypass the same exclusions that the upload phase uses.
- This is a verification/tooling bug, not evidence that the underlying cargo command failed. Some workers still retrieve artifacts successfully, but the failure is frequent enough to undermine trust in remote validation.
- Fixes must avoid deleting files without explicit user permission. Repo-side mitigation, rch-side retrieval filtering, or safe path-depth containment are acceptable; destructive cleanup is not.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `rch exec -- cargo check -p fcp-conformance --all-targets` and comparable commands can complete in this repo without artifact-retrieval failure caused by `.beads` path depth.
2. The solution does not require manual destructive cleanup of recovery trees.
3. The verification story is documented so agents can distinguish remote-command success from post-success artifact retrieval failure when it still occurs.
notes: Repo-side documentation adjusted; remaining remediation depends on local rch upgrade or upstream/tool rollout rather than a code change inside this repo.

comments.author: VioletSummit
comments.text: Claimed and starting investigation. Current hypothesis: remote cargo succeeds but rch artifact retrieval walks pathological .beads recovery paths that should have been excluded. Investigating repo config, rch flags/help, and safe non-destructive mitigations.

comments.author: VioletSummit
comments.text: Investigation update: traced rch source locally in /Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper. Upload merges transfer.exclude_patterns + .rchignore, but artifact retrieval does not reuse the exclude set; it traverses all dirs via --include '*/' and only filters by artifact globs. Also found hook-level hardcoding of remote sync roots to /data/projects in map_sync_root_to_remote_root() and ensure_worker_projects_topology(), so project config cannot currently force a fresh remote workspace path for cargo offload. This makes the bug fundamentally upstream/tooling-side, though repo docs/config can still make the verification story explicit.

comments.author: VioletSummit
comments.text: Validation result: telemetry verification succeeded end-to-end on worker vmi1227854, including artifact retrieval. Conformance verification on worker vmi1153651 compiled successfully but then failed during artifact retrieval with the same recursive .beads recovery overflow and rsync code 22. Conclusion: the defect persists, is worker-state-specific, and this repo can only document and pin excludes explicitly; the real fix belongs upstream in rch retrieval filtering and/or worker-path handling.

comments.author: VioletSummit
comments.text: Repo-side follow-up: README now explicitly says that if rch reports remote command exit=0 and only then fails during artifact retrieval, agents should treat that as a tooling or worker-state problem rather than a Cargo failure, preserve the retrieval stderr, and retry on another worker or continue upstream investigation.

comments.author: GentleOak
comments.text:
Additional validation from GentleOak on 2026-03-25:
- Installed client is /Users/jemanuel/.local/bin/rch -> rch 1.0.16.
- Local remote_compilation_helper checkout is ahead of that install: v1.0.16-2-ga5119e2, latest commit a5119e2 ("fix(transfer): apply effective excludes to retrieval rsync before directory include"). So current upstream source already contains retrieval-side exclude reuse in rch/src/transfer.rs.
- Re-ran `rch exec -- cargo check -p fcp-conformance --all-targets` on worker vmi1227854. Sync succeeded and remote command exited 101 because the shared worktree currently fails to compile in crates/fcp-mesh/src/degraded.rs (`DegradedTransportError::Encoding` missing). This run did not reach an artifact retrieval overflow.
- Re-ran `rch exec -- cargo test -p fcp-e2e subprocess::tests::drop_reaps_long_running_process --lib -- --exact --nocapture` on worker vmi1153651. That remote command also exited 101, now due to compile errors in crates/fcp-conformance/src/vectors/fcps.rs (`encoded_frame` is a Result<Vec<u8>, FrameError>` but is still compared/len()/decoded as raw bytes). This run also failed before artifact retrieval.
Conclusion: repo-side docs/config mitigation is already landed, but acceptance criterion #1 cannot be re-evaluated on the current shared worktree until these unrelated compile errors are cleared. When the original overflow does occur after `Remote command finished: exit=0`, the remaining suspicion should be installed-client lag and/or stale worker state, not missing repo excludes.

comments.author: PeachPond
comments.text:
PeachPond update:

Reproduced the current failure again in this repo with installed `rch`: remote `cargo check -p fcp-conformance --all-targets` exited 0 on worker `vmi1153651`, then artifact retrieval overflowed in rsync while traversing `.beads/recovery_20260313T010949Z_rubyglen/.../.beads`.

Traced the tooling gap to upstream `rch` at `/Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper/rch/src/transfer.rs`: upload merges `.rchignore`, but retrieval built its own `--include "*/"` rsync filter and ignored retrieval-side excludes.

Patched upstream locally to add `get_retrieval_excludes()` and make retrieval honor only runtime scratch excludes plus project `.rchignore` entries, rather than blindly reusing the full upload exclude set (which would have wrongly hidden artifact roots like `target/` and `dist/`).

Verification completed:
- `rch exec -- cargo test -p rch build_retrieve_command_applies_rchignore_excludes_before_directory_include -- --nocapture` passed in `/Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper`.
- `cargo fmt --check` passed in `/Users/jemanuel/projects/remote_compilation_helper`.
- Direct dry-run rsync against the same failing worker/path with the patched retrieval filter shape completed cleanly with `rsync_exit=0` and no buffer overflow while enumerating 47,160 files from `/data/projects/flywheel_connectors`.

Limitation: the remotely built patched `rch` artifact is Linux, so I could not execute that binary locally on macOS to replace the currently installed `rch` in-place. This bead looks technically solved in upstream source, but the local `rch` installation still needs to be rebuilt/updated from that patched source before `flywheel_connectors` itself will observe the fix.

comments.text:
PeachPond follow-up on 2026-03-25:

Installed-client gap is now fixed locally on this machine. I built a native macOS `rch` from upstream `remote_compilation_helper` commit `03f9f08421c8dfa92b7e7a5c4f742c65daa3a6ec` (the retrieval-exclude split) using an isolated target dir: `env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch-native cargo build -p rch --release --offline --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin`.

Install details:

- A straight in-place overwrite of `~/.local/bin/rch` produced a binary that macOS killed as `SIGKILL (Code Signature Invalid)` even though `codesign --verify` said valid. The same built artifact ran fine from `/tmp` and from `~/.local/bin/rch.fresh`.
- Resolved that by renaming the broken path aside to `~/.local/bin/rch.bad.20260325T190514` and moving a fresh inode into `~/.local/bin/rch`. After that, `rch --help`, `rch status`, and `rch workers probe vmi1153651` all succeeded normally.

Verification state after the upgrade:
- Direct worker/path validation remains good: the exact failing worker/path `ubuntu@38.242.134.66:/data/projects/flywheel_connectors/` still completes a retrieval-shaped dry-run rsync cleanly with no `.beads/recovery_*` overflow.
- End-to-end `rch exec` from this repo is no longer blocked by the old installed-client version, but it still does not reach remote cargo execution reliably in the current topology.
  - Without overrides: `rch exec --json -- cargo test -p fcp-e2e subprocess::tests::drop_reaps_long_running_process --lib -- --exact --nocapture` fail-opens at dependency preflight `RCH-E327` (`Path dependency topology policy failed; move dependencies under /data/projects (or /dp) and retry.`). I aborted the forbidden local fallback immediately.

Net: the local installed `rch` client is now updated enough that the old retrieval filter bug is not the only blocker, but acceptance criterion #1 is still not satisfied end-to-end because dependency preflight is now stopping remote execution before retrieval can be exercised through normal `rch exec` in this repo. The retrieval overflow itself still appears addressed at the exact worker/path level; the remaining blocker has shifted to dependency-preflight behavior.

title: fcp.terraform — Infrastructure as Code Connector
description:
# fcp.terraform - Infrastructure as Code Connector (FCP2)

## Goal
Deliver the FCP2 Terraform connector epic plan for IaC workflows with strict sandboxing, plan/diff safety, and policy-gated apply (dangerous).

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 80/100** — Important Tier 3 connector (Infrastructure family).

**Why Critical**: Terraform is the **dominant Infrastructure-as-Code tool**, managing cloud resources across AWS, GCP, Azure, and 1000+ providers. Enables agents to provision infrastructure, review plans, and automate cloud operations. Essential for autonomous DevOps.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Specialized Investment (Infrastructure + Safety Critical)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 3 Enterprise (weeks 9-12)

### Pulumi Comparison
- **Terraform**: HCL-based, mature ecosystem, state management
- **Pulumi**: General-purpose languages, same cloud targets
- Both needed for full IaC coverage

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Plan & Apply
- Generate infrastructure plans
- Review change diffs
- Apply approved changes
- Destroy resources (controlled)

### State Management
- Read current state
- Import existing resources
- State drift detection
- Resource inventory

### Workspace Management
- List workspaces
- Switch workspaces
- Lock/unlock state

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"What will this change affect?"
"Show me the current infrastructure state"
"Apply the approved changes"
"What resources exist in production?"
"Has any infrastructure drifted?"
"Import this existing S3 bucket"
"Create a new staging workspace"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Kubernetes Connector Synergy
**Full stack automation:**
- Terraform provisions clusters
- K8s connector manages workloads
- Agent handles both layers

### GitHub Integration
**GitOps workflows:**
- PR triggers terraform plan
- Agent reviews plan safety
- Merge triggers apply

### Datadog/Grafana Integration
- Infrastructure metrics correlation
- Provisioning impacts on observability
- Cost monitoring integration

### Agent Mail Integration
- Plan review requests → agent threads
- Apply approval workflows
- Drift notifications

### Stripe Integration
- Cloud cost correlation
- Resource provisioning → billing impact
- Budget enforcement

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### Execution Modes

#### Terraform CLI Wrapper
- Execute `terraform` commands via subprocess
- Parse plan/apply output
- Handle state file operations

#### Terraform Cloud/Enterprise API
- REST API for cloud workspaces
- Remote state management
- Run management

### Recommended Crates
- `tokio::process` — Command execution
- `serde_json` — JSON output parsing
- `reqwest` — Terraform Cloud API

### Core Operations
```
init → plan → apply
         ↓
      state operations
```

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:infra:terraform:full` | Full access | All operations including apply |
| `z:infra:terraform:plan` | Plan only | Plan and state read |
| `z:infra:terraform:readonly` | Read-only | State inspection only |
| `z:infra:terraform:workspace:<name>` | Workspace-scoped | Single workspace |

### Safety Boundaries
- Apply is **safety-critical** — requires explicit approval
- Destroy is **highest risk** — double confirmation
- Plan is safe — read-only simulation

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — CLI execution / API calls

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Varies by mode:
- **CLI**: Cloud provider APIs (AWS, GCP, Azure endpoints)
- **Terraform Cloud**: `app.terraform.io:443`

### Credential Injection
- Cloud provider credentials via environment
- TFE token via `CredentialId`
- Never write credentials to disk

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `terraform.state.read` — Read current state
- `terraform.state.list` — List resources
- `terraform.workspaces.read` — List workspaces
- `terraform.plan.read` — View existing plans

### Write Operations
- `terraform.plan.create` — Run terraform plan
- `terraform.apply.execute` — Apply changes (Dangerous)
- `terraform.state.import` — Import resources

### Administrative (Dangerous)
- `terraform.destroy` — Destroy infrastructure
- `terraform.state.remove` — Remove from state
- `terraform.workspaces.delete` — Delete workspace

---

## Operations (Representative)

### Terraform Plan
```bash
terraform plan -out=tfplan -json
```

Parsed output:
```json
{
  "resource_changes": [{
    "address": "aws_instance.web",
    "change": {
      "actions": ["create"],
      "before": null,
      "after": {
        "instance_type": "t3.medium",
        "ami": "ami-12345678"
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

### Terraform Apply
```bash
terraform apply tfplan -json
```

### Read State
```bash
terraform show -json
```

### Terraform Cloud Run (API)
```json
POST /api/v2/runs
{
  "data": {
    "type": "runs",
    "attributes": {
      "message": "Deploy API changes"
    },
    "relationships": {
      "workspace": {
        "data": {"type": "workspaces", "id": "ws-123abc"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Safety Considerations

### Plan Review Protocol
1. Agent generates plan
2. Plan must show all changes
3. Human/policy approval required
4. Only then can apply proceed

### Dangerous Operations
| Operation | Risk | Mitigation |
|-----------|------|------------|
| `apply` | High | Require prior plan approval |
| `destroy` | Very High | Double confirmation, no auto-approve |
| `state rm` | High | Audit log, confirmation |
| Import | Medium | Validation of resource match |

### Drift Detection
- Periodic state refresh
- Compare plan output
- Alert on unexpected changes

---

## Terraform Cloud Integration

### Benefits
- Remote state management
- Team collaboration
- Policy enforcement (Sentinel)
- VCS integration

### API Capabilities
- Workspace management
- Run triggering and monitoring
- Variable management
- State version access

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- Plan output parsing
- State JSON handling
- Change detection logic
- Workspace management

### Integration Tests
- Local terraform with mock providers
- State file operations
- Plan/apply workflow simulation

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints
- Apply requires approval
- Audit logging complete

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real infrastructure changes in tests
- Plan generation works
- State reading functional
- Apply requires explicit approval
- Terraform Cloud API works
- Proper audit trail maintained

## Success Criteria
- Connector epic is fully decomposed into implementable beads (manifest/cap map, provisioning, operations, tests, E2E compliance).
- All child beads are implemented and closed, and the connector passes the mechanical compliance runner + its E2E scenarios with structured JSON logs.
- Mechanical guarantees hold: single-zone binding, default-deny capabilities, and NetworkConstraints enforcement; no secret/PII leakage in logs.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Terraform connector verified: 147 tests (102 unit + 45 integration), all passing, clippy clean.

description:
# fcp.terraform: Manifest + Capability Map (FCP2)

## Goal
Define the Terraform connector’s **mechanical manifest contract** under FCP2.

Terraform is safety-critical; the manifest must make dangerous operations mechanically obvious.

## Required contents
- Manifest archetypes (closed set):
  - `operational` (CLI invocation; plan/apply/state)
- Operation list + schema IDs.
- Capability families + per-operation required caps.
- NetworkConstraints:
  - default deny
  - explicitly allow only the minimal outbound hosts required for the configured backends/providers
  - optionally require “offline mode” for plan-only environments
- Sandbox profile:
  - strict filesystem allowlist
  - explicit binary allowlist (terraform + minimal helpers)
- State model declaration:
  - plan artifact references + hashes (if persisted)
  - drift checkpoints (if persisted)

## Acceptance criteria
- Another engineer can implement `--manifest` from this bead alone.
- Static compliance can reject:
  - overly-broad egress
  - unsafe filesystem profiles

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Terraform manifest complete (12 ops across 4 cap families: terraform.plan, terraform.apply, terraform.state, terraform.state_write). Safety-critical design: plan/validate/detect_drift/init/show_plan/list_modules/state_list/state_show/output = safe, apply/destroy = dangerous/interactive with plan_hash binding, import = risky/policy. Infra zone only (z:work forbidden). Strict egress (registry.terraform.io, releases.hashicorp.com, checkpoint-api.hashicorp.com). deny_exec=false for terraform binary. Good/bad test vectors created. Hash: fa960fd19fa233b84aabd9a5cad509fa8c1e5a5135336f22bc3c8b6559067527. Validation: ok.

title: [FCP3/P1] Semantic lock, ownership map, and transition guardrails
description:
Background: before any carve out or wire change, the project needs a frozen vocabulary and owner map. Today too many concepts are smeared across fcp-core, fcp-host, fwc, and adjacent crates, which makes every architectural discussion slippery and every refactor prone to accidental recentralization.

Scope: define the canonical nouns, assign each one a single owner, identify current leakage, lock anti regression guardrails, and translate the V3 intent into repo local acceptance criteria and scoreboards. This phase is complete only when later implementation beads can proceed without re reading the spec to remember what a term is supposed to mean.

Do not start carving crates or rewriting protocols before the nouns have one owner, forbidden overlaps are named, and proof artifacts are specified. title: fcp.dropbox: Dropbox file storage connector
description:
## Goal
Provide an FCP2-compliant Dropbox connector for file storage operations under strict sandboxing, NetworkConstraints, and safe sharing controls.

## Manifest archetypes (closed set)

- `storage`
- `operational`

> Interaction patterns (non-archetype): Request/Response

## Overview

Implement the Flywheel Connector Platform (FCP) connector for Dropbox, a leading file storage and collaboration platform. This connector enables file CRUD operations, folder management, sharing capabilities, search functionality, Paper document handling, and team administration through Dropbox API v2.

## Value Assessment

- **Value Score**: 70/100 (Tier 4)
- **Priority**: P3
- **Archetype**: Request-Response + Webhook

Dropbox serves as a critical file storage connector alongside fcp.s3 and fcp.onedrive, providing cloud file storage capabilities for the FCP ecosystem.

## Technical Architecture

### API Integration
- **API Version**: Dropbox API v2
- **Authentication**: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE
- **Base URL**: https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/
- **Content URL**: https://content.dropboxapi.com/2/

### Zone Architecture

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The *"zones"* described in this section are a **recommended deployment pattern** (run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies) and/or conceptual risk tiers.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

The connector operates across three distinct zones:

1. **Personal Files Zone**
   - User's personal file storage
   - Individual file/folder operations
   - Personal sharing settings

2. **Shared Files Zone**
   - Team shared folders
   - Collaborative workspaces
   - Shared links management

3. **Team Admin Zone**
   - Team member management
   - Group administration
   - Team-wide policies and settings
   - Storage quota management

### Dependencies
- `fcp-core`: Core connector traits and types
- `fcp-oauth`: OAuth 2.0 authentication flow
- `fcp-webhook`: Webhook handling for file change notifications
- `fcp-ratelimit`: Rate limiting (Dropbox uses sliding window limits)
- `fcp-telemetry`: Observability and metrics

## Operations

### File Operations
- `files.upload` - Upload files (chunked for large files)
- `files.download` - Download file content
- `files.get_metadata` - Get file/folder metadata
- `files.delete` - Delete files/folders
- `files.copy` - Copy files/folders
- `files.move` - Move/rename files/folders
- `files.search` - Search for files by name/content
- `files.list_folder` - List folder contents
- `files.get_thumbnail` - Get image thumbnails
- `files.get_preview` - Get file previews

### Folder Operations
- `folders.create` - Create new folders
- `folders.delete` - Delete folders recursively
- `folders.copy` - Copy folder structure
- `folders.move` - Move/rename folders

### Sharing Operations
- `sharing.create_shared_link` - Create shareable links
- `sharing.list_shared_links` - List existing shared links
- `sharing.revoke_shared_link` - Revoke shared links
- `sharing.add_folder_member` - Add members to shared folders
- `sharing.remove_folder_member` - Remove folder members
- `sharing.list_folder_members` - List shared folder members
- `sharing.update_folder_member` - Update member permissions

### Paper Documents
- `paper.docs.create` - Create Paper documents
- `paper.docs.update` - Update Paper content
- `paper.docs.download` - Export Paper documents
- `paper.docs.list` - List Paper documents
- `paper.docs.archive` - Archive Paper documents

### Team Administration
- `team.members.list` - List team members
- `team.members.add` - Add team members
- `team.members.remove` - Remove team members
- `team.members.suspend` - Suspend team members
- `team.groups.list` - List team groups
- `team.groups.create` - Create groups
- `team.groups.members.add` - Add members to groups
- `team.info` - Get team information
- `team.features` - Get team features/quotas

### Webhook Events
- `file.change` - File added/modified/deleted
- `folder.change` - Folder structure changes
- `sharing.change` - Sharing settings modified
- `team.member.change` - Team membership changes

## Implementation Notes

### Rate Limiting
Dropbox uses per-app and per-user rate limits:
- Standard endpoints: 1000 requests/minute
- Content endpoints: Variable based on operation
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter

### Large File Handling
- Files > 150MB require chunked upload sessions
- Session-based uploads with `upload_session/start`, `append`, `finish`
- Support for resumable uploads

### Cursor-Based Pagination
- Use cursors for `list_folder` continuation
- Implement `list_folder/continue` for large directories
- Handle cursor expiration (reset after ~4 hours)

### Namespace Handling
- Support both root namespace (team) and member namespaces
- Handle namespace routing via `Dropbox-API-Path-Root` header

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] OAuth 2.0 flow with refresh token support
- [ ] Full file CRUD operations
- [ ] Folder management with recursive operations
- [ ] Sharing link creation and management
- [ ] Team member and group administration
- [ ] Paper document support
- [ ] Search functionality across files
- [ ] Webhook integration for change notifications
- [ ] Chunked upload for large files (>150MB)
- [ ] Proper rate limit handling with backoff
- [ ] Cursor-based pagination for large result sets
- [ ] Comprehensive error handling for Dropbox error codes
- [ ] Unit and integration tests

## Similar Connectors

Reference implementations for patterns:
- `fcp.s3` - File storage operations, chunked uploads
- `fcp.onedrive` - Microsoft Graph patterns, sharing model
- `fcp.google-drive` - OAuth patterns, folder hierarchy

## Resources

- [Dropbox API v2 Documentation](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/documentation/http/documentation)
- [Dropbox OAuth Guide](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/oauth-guide)
- [Dropbox Webhooks](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/reference/webhooks)

title: [MOR/C2.3] Implement zone-wide TruthPrecedencePolicy for consistent operator answers

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: WHAT: Implement TruthPrecedencePolicy as a zone-wide configuration object that defines the ordering of truth sources. All operators (fwc, host, remote agents) MUST load and follow it. Default precedence: MeshBacked > HostBacked > NodeLocal > Offline (with zone-specific overrides). Currently, each operator chooses ResolutionStrategy independently (BestAvailable, PreferHost, OfflineOnly), which means two operators in the same zone can resolve the same query to different answers. WHY: F7 Systems found Truth Multiplicity Creates Consistency Debt — three parallel truth sources without ordering causes split-brain operator scenarios. An operator on node A reads mesh-backed revocation, operator on node B reads host cache — revocation enforcement is inconsistent. The fix is simple: define ONE zone-wide precedence that all operators follow. WHERE: crates/fwc/src/truth.rs — add TruthPrecedencePolicy struct loaded from zone configuration. Modify LiveTruthResolver to accept and enforce the policy. Add with_precedence_policy() constructor. ACCEPTANCE: (1) TruthPrecedencePolicy type exists with zone-wide ordering. (2) LiveTruthResolver enforces policy (not per-operator choice). (3) Two operators in same zone always resolve to same answer for same query. (4) At least 4 tests: same-zone consistency, policy override for specific zone, fallback when higher-precedence source unavailable, serialization round-trip. ESTIMATED EFFORT: 2-3 days. DEPENDS ON: C2.2 (versioned operational model) — the policy is part of V1 operational model.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CROSS-EPIC DEP: Depends on C3.1 (phantom tokens) because the truth precedence policy should distinguish between answers backed by Verified tokens (high confidence) vs answers from unverified/cached sources (lower confidence). The phantom type system provides the compile-time distinction that the truth resolver can use to set confidence levels.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: C2.3 complete. TruthPrecedencePolicy with zone-wide ordering, OperationalModelVersion, v1_default/v2_default, for_zone overrides, resolve_with_policy on LiveTruthResolver. 8 acceptance tests all pass. Also fixed pre-existing .raw→.raw(), impl_fcp_sealed\! in new_cmd, and double #[must_use] in registry. Commit 344d8b74.

title: TEST: Telegram Connector Integration Tests
description:
# TEST: Telegram Connector Integration Tests (Deterministic)


## Goal
Validate Telegram connector integration flows (updates, sends, webhook/polling harness) with deterministic tests and mocks.

## External surface (NetworkConstraints)
Default deny.
- Network egress MUST be restricted per-operation via manifest `NetworkConstraints`.
- Allow only the configured service host(s); HTTPS-only where applicable; deny redirects by default.
- Bound timeouts + response sizes; treat all remote responses as untrusted input; never leak secrets/PII in logs or errors.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Purpose
Integration tests for `fcp.telegram` that validate **real connector behavior** against a **deterministic fake Telegram Bot API** (wiremock or a purpose-built in-process server).

These tests are NOT allowed to call the real Telegram API.

## What this test suite must prove
### 1) Bot API correctness (request/response)
- getUpdates long-poll semantics (timeout handling is bounded)
- update offset advancement and persistence
- sendMessage / sendMedia request formation
- file download URL handling (if supported)

### 2) Cursor + singleton-writer correctness
- only the lease-holder advances the update cursor
- restart behavior: resume from persisted cursor
- duplicate update defense (idempotent event emission)

### 3) FCP2 connector contract (integration-level)
- standard method surface works end-to-end (handshake/describe/introspect/capabilities/configure/invoke/health/shutdown)
- capability gating is mechanical:
  - no token → deny + DecisionReceipt
  - valid token → allow
- streaming/event emission:
  - events emitted as EventEnvelopes with correct topic
  - inbound data is tainted as external input

### 4) Error and adversity handling
- rate limits (429) and Retry-After
- invalid token (401) fail-closed
- network timeouts and bounded retries
- malformed update payloads (reject + audit, never panic)

## Required scenarios (minimum)
- scripted update stream: new message → edit → member join → member leave
- concurrent start attempt:
  - second instance denied/fenced by lease
- send operation with simulated timeout-after-send:
  - verify fail-closed behavior to avoid duplicate messages

## Logging requirements
- Structured JSON logs with: `test_name`, `phase`, `correlation_id`, `duration_ms`.
- For denials: `decision=deny`, `reason_code`, `evidence` (object IDs).
- Never log bot tokens or raw message bodies by default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Runs deterministically in CI.
- Produces a clear, searchable log trail on failure.
- Integrates cleanly with the shared E2E/compliance framework (no bespoke harness logic that can’t be reused).

title: fcp.github: GitHub API Connector
description:
# fcp.github - GitHub API Connector (FCP2)

## Strategic Context

### Value Assessment
**Strategic Value Score: 95/100** — Critical Tier 1 connector (Development family).

**Why Critical**: GitHub is **the dominant code hosting platform**. Enables agents to manage repositories, issues, PRs, CI/CD workflows, and code search. Essential for any software development automation.

### Priority Matrix Position
- **Category**: Critical Infrastructure (Development + Automation)
- **Build Phase**: Phase 1 Foundation (immediate)

---

## V2 Specification Compliance (NORMATIVE)

### ConnectorArchetype
```rust
archetypes: vec\![
    ConnectorArchetype::Operational,  // REST/GraphQL actions
    ConnectorArchetype::Streaming,    // Webhook event ingestion
]
```
- **Operational**: CRUD on repos, issues, PRs, workflows
- **Streaming**: Webhook events (push, PR, issue updates)

### ConnectorStateModel
```rust
state_model: ConnectorStateModel::SingletonWriter
```
- **SingletonWriter**: Cursor/sync state for webhook event processing
- State tracked: `{ last_event_ids: HashMap<RepoId, Vec<EventId>> }`
- Lease required for writer fencing

### ConnectorFormat
```rust
format: ConnectorFormat::Wasi
```
- **WASI**: Contains Dangerous operations (repo delete, workflow dispatch)
- Memory isolation for credential handling
- Capability-gated hostcalls

### NetworkConstraints (NORMATIVE)
```rust
NetworkConstraints {
    // GitHub.com API
    host_allow: vec\!["api.github.com".into()],
    // GitHub Enterprise: configured hostname added dynamically
    port_allow: vec\![443],
    deny_localhost: true,
    deny_private_ranges: true,
    deny_tailnet_ranges: true,
    deny_ip_literals: true,
    require_sni: true,
    require_host_canonicalization: true,
}
```

### TaintFlags (NORMATIVE)
```rust
// User inputs (issue bodies, PR descriptions) are tainted
user_content.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::USER_SUPPLIED
    | TaintFlags::PROMPT_SURFACE;

// Webhook payloads are external
webhook_event.provenance.taint = TaintFlags::EXTERNAL_INPUT;

// URLs in content are unverified
if content.contains_urls() {
    content.provenance.taint |= TaintFlags::UNVERIFIED_LINK;
}
```

### SafetyTier per Operation
| Operation | SafetyTier | Rationale |
|-----------|------------|-----------|
| `github.repos.read` | Safe | Read-only listing |
| `github.issues.read` | Safe | Read-only |
| `github.pulls.read` | Safe | Read-only |
| `github.search.read` | Safe | Code/issue search |
| `github.issues.write` | Risky | Creates/modifies issues |
| `github.pulls.write` | Risky | Creates/modifies PRs |
| `github.repos.write` | Risky | Modifies repo settings |
| `github.actions.dispatch` | Dangerous | Triggers CI/CD workflows |
| `github.webhooks.manage` | Dangerous | Modifies event routing |
| `github.repos.delete` | Dangerous | Irreversible deletion |

---

## Agent Capabilities (Concrete Use Cases)

### Repository Operations
- List/create/update repositories
- Manage branches and tags
- Access file contents
- Configure settings

### Issue Management
- Create and update issues
- Add comments and labels
- Assign users
- Link to PRs

### Pull Request Workflows
- Create and review PRs
- Request/submit reviews
- Merge strategies
- Check status

### CI/CD Integration
- List workflow runs
- Dispatch workflows
- Cancel/rerun jobs
- Access logs

### Code Search
- Search code across repos
- Search issues and PRs
- Advanced query syntax

### Examples of Agent Workflows
```
"Create an issue for this bug"
"Open a PR with these changes"
"Merge the PR after checks pass"
"Search for usages of this function"
"Trigger the deployment workflow"
"List all open PRs for review"
"Add labels to issues matching criteria"
```

---

## Flywheel Ecosystem Synergies

### Linear Integration
**Issue bidirectional sync:**
- GitHub issues ↔ Linear issues
- PR references in Linear
- Coordinated status updates

### Agent Mail Integration
- PR review requests → agent threads
- Issue assignments trigger workflows
- CI/CD notifications routed

### Sentry Integration
- Error events create GitHub issues
- Stack traces linked to code
- Release tracking

### Datadog/Grafana Integration
- Deployment events correlated
- Performance metrics linked to commits
- Incident → PR correlation

---

## Technical Implementation Notes

### API Surface
- **REST API v3**: Primary CRUD operations
- **GraphQL API v4**: Efficient queries, mutations
- **Webhooks**: Event delivery

### Recommended Crates
- `octocrab` — GitHub API client
- `reqwest` — HTTP client
- `graphql_client` — GraphQL queries
- `hmac` / `sha2` — Webhook signature validation

### Authentication Modes
| Mode | Use Case | Recommendation |
|------|----------|----------------|
| GitHub App | Organization automation | **Preferred** |
| OAuth App | User-delegated access | Good |
| PAT | Personal use | Discouraged |

---

## Zone Architecture

### Recommended Zones
| Zone | Description | Capabilities |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `z:work:github:<org>` | Organization-scoped | Full org access |
| `z:project:<name>:github` | Repo-scoped | Single repo |
| `z:work:github:readonly` | Read-only | Safe operations only |

### Security Considerations
- Org-level access is high trust
- Repo-scoped tokens preferred
- Webhook secrets per installation

---

## Manifest Archetypes (Closed Set)
- `operational` — REST/GraphQL actions
- `streaming` — Webhook event ingestion

---

## External Surface

### NetworkConstraints
Default-deny; allow only:
- `api.github.com:443` (GitHub.com)
- Enterprise: configured hostname

### Credential Injection
- GitHub App private key + installation token
- OAuth tokens via egress proxy
- Webhook secrets for signature validation

---

## Capability Model

### Read Operations
- `github.repos.read` — List/get repositories
- `github.issues.read` — List/get issues
- `github.pulls.read` — List/get PRs
- `github.actions.read` — Workflow/run status
- `github.search.read` — Code/issue search

### Write Operations
- `github.repos.write` — Update repo settings
- `github.issues.write` — Create/update issues
- `github.pulls.write` — Create/update PRs
- `github.actions.write` — Cancel/rerun jobs

### Admin Operations
- `github.repos.delete` — Delete repository (Dangerous)
- `github.actions.dispatch` — Trigger workflows (Dangerous)
- `github.webhooks.manage` — Configure webhooks (Dangerous)

---

## Operations (Representative)

### List Repositories
```
GET /orgs/{org}/repos
GET /user/repos
```

### Create Issue
```json
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues
{
  "title": "Bug: login fails",
  "body": "Steps to reproduce...",
  "labels": ["bug", "priority:high"]
}
```

### Create Pull Request
```json
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls
{
  "title": "Fix login bug",
  "head": "fix-login",
  "base": "main",
  "body": "Fixes #123"
}
```

### Dispatch Workflow
```json
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches
{
  "ref": "main",
  "inputs": {"environment": "staging"}
}
```

### Search Code
```
GET /search/code?q=function+repo:owner/repo
```

---

## Tests

### Unit Tests (Mock-Only)
- API request construction
- Response parsing
- Webhook signature validation
- Rate limit handling
- Error responses

### Integration Tests
- Mock GitHub API responses
- Multi-step workflows (create PR → review → merge)
- Webhook event processing

### E2E Compliance
- Validates NetworkConstraints (api.github.com only)
- Dangerous operation approval flow
- Audit logging for writes

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- Passes connector compliance runner (static + dynamic)
- No real GitHub API calls in unit tests
- All CRUD operations functional
- Webhook signature validation works
- Rate limiting respected
- GraphQL queries supported
- All V2 NORMATIVE requirements satisfied

title: TEST: Anthropic Connector Integration Tests
description:
# TEST: Anthropic Connector Integration Tests (Deterministic)


## Goal
Validate Anthropic connector integration flows under deterministic mocks (streaming, tool use) and compliance checks.

## External surface (NetworkConstraints)
Default deny.
- Network egress MUST be restricted per-operation via manifest `NetworkConstraints`.
- Allow only the configured service host(s); HTTPS-only where applicable; deny redirects by default.
- Bound timeouts + response sizes; treat all remote responses as untrusted input; never leak secrets/PII in logs or errors.

## Zone model (mechanical)

<!-- fcp2-single-zone-note -->
**FCP2 single-zone binding note:** A connector instance binds to exactly one `ZoneId` for its entire lifetime.
The connector MUST NOT multiplex multiple zones internally.

Recommended deployment pattern: run separate connector instances in separate zones with different capability grants/policies.

## Purpose
Integration tests for `fcp.anthropic` using a deterministic mock Anthropic API (wiremock + SSE simulation).

No real Anthropic calls are allowed.

## Must cover
- Non-streaming generation.
- Streaming SSE generation:
  - chunk parsing
  - cancellation
  - error mid-stream
- Tool/function calling request/response shapes.
- Error taxonomy mapping (401/429/5xx).
- Usage metrics extraction (tokens, latencies) — **not hard-coded currency pricing**.
- FCP2 contract: default deny / allow + DecisionReceipt reason codes.

## Logging
- Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs.
- No API key leakage; no raw prompts/responses by default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deterministic in CI.
- Failures are actionable and include reason_code + evidence.
